title: Little Computer People
build: single-file crack by Mr Z (crack screen "CRACKED BY MR Z..."): disk name LCP, one crunched 192-block program COMPUTER PEOPLE; no error bytes

records.c: 6510 data direction register: the cold start writes $2F (bits 0-3 and 5 outputs). The JSR $0000 at $B3B9 is not a call to here: its operand is rewritten before use.

6510 port: memory configuration. The game keeps the low bits at 5 (I/O in, BASIC and KERNAL out) and drops them to 4 around uses of the RAM under $D000 ($B26F, $B5C3, $B62E, $B639). The IRQ handler keeps the low three bits in $092D, forces 5 and restores them on exit.

$02-$0F: no traced instruction of the game uses these bytes (the cross-references once listed for $03, $05, $0A and $0D came from switch tables decoded as code, or from zero page itself being decoded as code). They keep what the loader left there.
No genuine use found: the only reference is at $E3E0, a byte of the switch table after JSR $3F11 at $E3CA that the disassembler decodes as code. 0 in every snapshot.

Parser pointer, low byte (high byte $11): walks a word list in s_C187 (five concept bytes, the word, $00; $FF ends the list) comparing records with the current word at $C020, and walks the 16-byte rule records from $C96A in s_C1C5.
High byte of the parser pointer $10: $C2 or $C5 for the word lists at $C234 and $C5E0, $C9 for the rules at $C96A, advanced as the records are stepped over.

Parser rule matcher s_C1C5: OR over the ten bit bytes of (rule bits AND NOT sentence bits $C016-$C01F). Zero means every concept the rule needs is in the sentence, and the rule's action codes are taken.
Parser rule matcher s_C1C5: the current sentence bit byte ($C016,y) inverted, ANDed with the rule byte.
$14-$17: no traced instruction uses these bytes ($15 and $17 were listed only from switch tables decoded as code); they hold $12 $08 $19 $16 from the loader in every snapshot.

Scratch pointer, low byte (high $19), shared by many routines: unpack_figure_sprite's packed-data pointer and s_12B7's source image; update_figure_sprites' pointer to the frame Y offsets; the body image builder at $1585-$160B; script_next's activity script pointer ($8F14); draw_object's frame list ($9708) and, through copy_frame_record ($99D5), the colour-RAM source the blitter $3E79 reads; the product of the multiply at $3E5A. draw_clock_hand keeps its direction flips in $18.
High byte of the scratch pointer $18; draw_clock_hand uses it alone as its count of steps left.

Scratch pointer, low byte (high $1B): the sprite block being written by unpack_figure_sprite, s_12B7 and s_13AC ($4000 + 64 x block, from s_1396); the blitter's colour-matrix source ($3E88); the part builder's pointer at $1592-$1606; the multiplicand at $3E5A. draw_clock_hand keeps its step index in $1A.
High byte of the scratch pointer $1A; draw_clock_hand's 2-bit pixel mask.

Scratch: the blitter's bitmap source pointer (low byte, high $1D; $3E7D, from copy_frame_record); the first byte of unpack_figure_sprite's repeated row; a part pointer at $15FE; draw_clock_hand's byte offset in the clock area.
High byte of the blitter's bitmap source pointer $1C; the second byte of unpack_figure_sprite's repeated row; draw_clock_hand's step temp.

Scratch: the blitter's bitmap destination pointer (low byte, high $1F; set by draw_object at $9727, stored through at $3E7F, moved on 320 bytes a row at $3ED5); the third byte of unpack_figure_sprite's repeated row; a part pointer at $15CF.
High byte of the blitter's bitmap destination pointer $1E ($972C, $3EDE).
$20-$27: no traced instruction of the game uses these bytes (the references once listed for $21-$27 were bytes of switch tables decoded as code); they hold the same loader values in every snapshot.
No genuine use found: the only reference is at $E3D4, inside the switch table after JSR $3F11 at $E3CA, decoded as code. 0 in every snapshot.

Pointer for the switch at $3F13: it pops the caller's return address (the last byte of the JSR) into $28/$29 and adds 2 x index + 1, then reads the handler address minus one from the inline table at ($28),1 and ($28),2 and pushes it.
High byte of the switch routine's table pointer $28.
Cleared by the cold start (it is in cold_clear_zp) and used by no other traced instruction.

Frame counter, low byte: the raster IRQ increments it every frame and carries into $2C and $2D. Also read alone: print_queued counts the text band down when it is 0 (every 256 frames), and $2E73 counts its timer when the low two bits are 0.
Middle byte of the frame counter ($2B, $2C, $2D), counting 256-frame units. The keyboard scan clears it and $2D whenever any key is down, so $2C/$2D measure the time since the last key press.

High byte of the frame counter, one step per 65536 frames (about 22 minutes at 50 Hz); cleared by any key. From 10 up (about 3.6 hours without a key) the screen is blanked (set_screen_on), start_illness does nothing and the code at $30E3 changes activity $2B into activity $27 (as it also does when $30B4 is 0).
Control port 1 bits 0-4 from $DC01 (up, down, left, right, fire; 0 = pressed), stored by read_joysticks every main loop pass. No traced instruction reads it.
Control port 2 bits 0-4 from $DC00 (0 = pressed), stored by read_joysticks. No traced instruction reads it.

The new key for the game (ASCII, or a control code for CTRL with a letter), set by the keyboard scan; the code that takes it sets it back to 0 (the line editor at $3763, the CTRL-key handler $2B54); $37B9 reads it, and $BAD4 and the time prompt ($04FD) clear it.
Copy of the last new key, stored with $30 by the keyboard scan and cleared at cold start. No traced instruction reads it.
Keyboard scan: index (0-63) of the lowest-numbered key found down that is not SHIFT, CTRL or ignored; $FF when none.

Keyboard scan: the key last taken, still held. The same key is ignored until a scan finds no key (or code $5C) and clears this, so holding a key does not repeat. Also read at $3378 inside a switch table, which is not a real use.

Scratch byte: key index in the keyboard scan (63 down to 0), BCD accumulator in parse_bcd, prompt text index and $4800 fill pointer (low) in the cold start, item index when the main loop copies the parser result, and a counter in $5756.
Scratch byte: high byte of the cold start's fill pointer ($34/$35, $48-$4F), and a mask in $5756.
Cold start: counts the five calls of update_figure_sprites (4 down to -1).
$37-$3B: no traced instruction uses these bytes ($37 and $38 were listed only from switch tables or data decoded as code); constant $00 $A0 $B1 $57 $C9 in every snapshot.

IRQ scratch: the largest sprite Y found so far (starts at 14); then the band bottom minus 21 for count_sprites_near_band; then the band_split_delays entry, whose bits 6 and 7 BIT tests for the extra cycles.
IRQ: the band's bottom raster line ($0711, or $49), upper limit for count_sprites_near_band.
IRQ: the number of sprites near the band bottom returned by count_sprites_near_band, stored and reloaded as the index into band_split_delays.
IRQ: the raster line the handler waits for before restoring $D016 and the cursor sprite (the band's bottom, $49 when $0711 is 0).
Set to 1 by every raster interrupt ($080B). No traced instruction reads it.
IRQ: $D016 as it was when the interrupt came (multicolour on), written back at the band's bottom line.
cursor_sprite_save: $D015 (sprite enable).
cursor_sprite_save: X position of the borrowed sprite.
cursor_sprite_save: Y position of the borrowed sprite.
cursor_sprite_save: $D010 (sprite X high bits).
cursor_sprite_save: $D01C (sprite multicolour).
cursor_sprite_save: the borrowed sprite's colour register ($D027+n).
cursor_sprite_save: the borrowed sprite's pointer ($5FF8+n).
cursor_sprite_save: $D01B (sprite priority).
No traced instruction uses $4A; it holds $D0 in every snapshot.

Scratch byte: in update_figure_sprites' depth sort ($103D-$1090) the index of the smallest key, a swap temporary, then the next free hardware sprite number; the water tank drawing loop $2D0D counts the tank level ($2B51) down in it; type_digit ($37D4) keeps a digit in it.

Activity phase: the index for the switches reached by JSR $3F11 inside each activity (84 sites), so it picks the handler for this pass. j_8F0B adds 1 (next phase); many handlers store a phase; cleared at cold start. The activity number itself is $8D9B.

Jump vector of sound_dispatch ($396E): for each bit set in $478D it copies that job's address from sound_jobs here ($3987, high byte $398C) and jumps through JMP ($004D) at $3999. The routines that would set $478D ($39C1, $39F4, $39FA, $456F) have no traced callers, so it keeps the $57 the loader left in every snapshot.
High byte of sound_dispatch's job vector $4D, from sound_jobs' high half ($398C).

Scratch word of the timer tune player (with $50): the jump vector for a tune command, JMP ($004F) at $4059 (set at $4045 from the command table $4072); also a branch target, the note byte in s_4243, the frequency step of vibrato and pitch slides ($4334, $4386, $43AD-$43EB) and the pointer to a tune's (register, value) list ($440F). $4F-$65 are cleared together by s_44E8.
High byte of the tune player's scratch word $4F; in s_4243 the note byte's length nibble, 0 meaning the note does not wait ($425A, $426E).

Added to each register number when a tune writes (register, value) pairs to the SID and its shadow at $7FCD ($4415): 0 from the entry at $43F8, the voice's SID offset $7FE8 from the entry at $43FE. $52 after it has no reference (only the $4F-$65 clear).

$53-$5F: the current tune voice's 13-byte record, copied in from ($62) before the interpreter s_4022 runs and copied back after ($3F96-$3FAB); s_44A9 sets it up from the tune table $3A03. $53/$54 = where the voice's next tune bytes are: s_422C reads ($53),Y with Y from $7F40, and s_405C adds $7F40 to it after each event.
Voice record byte 1: high byte of the tune position $53.

Voice record byte 2: the current note as a semitone number (0-95, an index into the frequency table at $46C9); each note byte adds a signed interval to it ($42D0), negated while flag bit 5 of $5F is set. Also reached as $55,x by the tune commands that set, push and pop registers ($415F-$417C).
Voice record byte 3: the note length in units of 8 timer-A ticks, set by a note byte with a length nibble ($426A) and reused by nibble 6.
Voice record byte 4: articulation. The gate goes off when the countdown reaches $56 x $57 ($4275-$4284); 0 = no early release. Set to 2 by s_44A9.
Voice record byte 5: the CIA1 timer A high byte (a tick is $58 x 256 cycles), $3B from s_44A9 ($447A); the tempo command also copies it into the three voice records and $DC05.
Voice record byte 6, tune register 4: only reachable through the indexed register commands ($55,x); no tune uses it.
Voice record byte 7, tune register 5: like $59, unused by the tunes.
Voice record byte 8, tune register 6: only the tune byte $E3 at $3CAD pops a finished loop count into it. (The STX $5B at $5B38 is switch-table data.)
Voice record byte 9: timer-A ticks until the voice's next event: length x 8 from a note ($4273), 1 from s_44A9. Timer A counts the record's copy down ($3F59) and runs the interpreter at 0.
Voice record byte 10: the countdown value at which the gate is released, $56 x $57 ($4284); compared at $3F62-$3F68 while flag bit 6 is set.
Voice record byte 11: index into the voice's 32-byte stack at ($60) of return addresses and loop counts (push $4235, pop $423C, loop count $420E, $40D1).

Voice record byte 12, flags: bit 7 voice active (tested at $3F4E, cleared by the end command $40F6), bit 6 early release (set by each note $424E, cleared for a tied note), bit 5 invert intervals, bit 3 call the vector at $7FF4 (always $44A8, an RTS), bit 2 slide up, bit 1 pitch slide ($431D), bit 0 vibrato ($4357). $C0 from s_44A9.
Pointer to the current voice's stack, its record + 13 ($3F89-$3F94), used by the push, pop and loop commands.
High byte of the voice stack pointer $60.
Pointer to the current voice's 45-byte record in RAM: $7F46, $7F73 or $7FA0 ($3F7B, $44C9), from which $53-$5F are copied.
High byte of the voice record pointer $62 ($7F).
Pointer to the vibrato shape table, $4353 (set at $443D; $00 $01 $03 $01), read at $436D with the counter AND 3.
High byte of the vibrato table pointer $64 ($43).
Pointer to the next character of the letter being typed: set to $7F40 at $55A9, where the code at $55C4 assembles the letter from the pieces at $5600; read and advanced by s_5599.
High byte of the letter pointer $66 ($7F while a letter is typed; $02 in the snapshots, where no letter has been written).
Second switch index: JSR $3F0C switches on it (16 sites, for example $21B5, $229D-$23AD, $3375, $94CF). Set, cleared and incremented by the activity handlers; cleared at cold start.
Head turning ($ACF3): scratch for the step between the head's current direction ($038F) and its target ($03F4); later the chosen new direction.
Head turning ($ACF3): scratch: the current direction (low three bits of $038F); later the chosen row, 0-2, for the new target.

Music player ($B000) scratch: when a song starts, song x 2 and then the offset song x 6 + 2 x voice into the song table $D764 ($B27A-$B289); when the voices are output, the count of the 7 SID registers ($B4C4, $B4CE); in the note code the frequency low byte from $B641/$B661 shifted for the octave ($D04C-$D085).

Music player: channel x 2 (0-10: channels 0-2 are the first set, 3-5 the second), the X/Y of every stream command ($B287, $B56C, $B5B7); during output, SID voice x 2, counting 4, 2, 0 down to $FE ($B35C, $B4E8).
Music player scratch: count of the 5-byte instrument copy ($B320, $B32A); during output the chosen channel x 2 ($B360, $B42F, $B452); in the note code the frequency high byte ($D051-$D08A).

Music player scratch: the voice counter 2 to 0 when a song starts ($B285, $B2DE); the end offset of the chosen voice record during output ($B45A, $B4C0); the note byte in the note code ($D046, $D071); the low byte of a slide step in $D1CB.
Music player frame loop: 0 while the first-set channel of voice $B018 is handled, 1 for its second-set channel ($B550, $B55B, $B563).
Music player: offset (0, 7 ... 35) of the current channel's 7-byte SID record in the table at $B031 ($B5B5, $D091, $B4D7), the X of most stream commands.
Music player scratch: during output the first-set record offset while the second set is checked ($B440, $B454); in a pitch slide the step's high byte ($D1EC-$D250).
Music player: cleared at $B358 and set to $FF once a set's filter and volume record ($B05B or $B062, to $D415-$D418) has been written this frame ($B490), so the other voices skip it ($B45C).

Music player: a pattern address fetched from ($83) at $D570; the stream commands $04, $0A, $20 and $24 save a return address and load it into the channel's stream pointer ($D12A, $D4A6, $D3BA, $D50D). (The ADC $73,X at $AA72 is script data.)
High byte of the pattern address $73 ($D575).

$75-$80: the six channels' 16-bit stream read pointers, indexed by channel x 2: set from the song table $D764 when a song starts ($B299, $B2A1), advanced per byte ($B314, $D000, $D09F), replaced by the jump, loop, call and return commands, and copied to $81/$82 for reading ($B5BB). Channels 3-5 ($7B-$80) play the piano pieces.
High byte of channel 0's stream pointer; the other high bytes follow at $78, $7A, $7C, $7E and $80 (reached only by index).
Music player: working copy of the current channel's stream pointer, read through ($81),Y ($B5BD, $B5C9, $D09D). The player's init also uses it to clear $B012-$B173 ($B1E6-$B204).
High byte of the music player's read pointer $81.

Music player: pointer to the pattern table used by $D527 ($D564): from $D831 for the first set (per channel, or shared when the operand's bit 7 is set), the piano piece's base + 6 for the second set (self-modified at $D53E-$D559); read at $D56E and $D573.
High byte of the pattern table pointer $83 ($D56A).
Music player pitch slide direction: 0 = step subtracted (down, $D1CB), 1 = added (up, $D1CF); read at $D221. $86 and $87 after it have no reference ($30 and $38 in every snapshot).
Text: X of the start of a line (the left margin), low byte, from $BDC4 (3); the cursor goes back here on RETURN and cannot be moved left of it.
Text: X of the left margin, high byte.
Text: right limit ($BDC6 - 6 = $0139), low byte, written by s_BD7E. No traced instruction reads it or $8B.
Text: right limit, high byte. Written by s_BD7E only.

Text cursor X in pixels across the band, low byte (high byte $8D): advanced by each glyph's width, moved back on backspace and RETURN. The IRQ places the cursor sprite at this X + 13; $5756 reads it too.

Text cursor X, high byte. While it is 1 (X of 256 or more) the line editor accepts only RETURN and DEL ($374B), and print_queued, while $54DF is set, turns a space (or a hyphen) into RETURN to break the line ($BA8C).
Text: pixel row of the top of the text line in the band, set to $0E by s_BD7E; added to each glyph's vertical offset.
No genuine use found: the references at $582A and $E3D1 are bytes of the switch tables after JSR $3F11 at $5825 and $E3CA, decoded as code. Holds $58 in every snapshot.
Text: the width in pixels of the glyph being printed (low nibble of its first byte; measured from the pixels for the second font), added to the cursor X.
Text: the pixel row where the glyph starts: $8E plus the high nibble of the glyph's first byte (just $8E for the second font).

Text: the eight bytes of the glyph being printed, $92-$99 (for the first font byte 0 holds the width and offset, rows 1-7 the pixels), shifted right by the cursor's X AND 7; the bits shifted out go to $A2-$A9. Drawn with EOR, so printing the same glyph again erases it.
Text: glyph row 1 ($92 + 1), the first pixel row of a first-font glyph.
Text: glyph row 2 ($92 + 2).
Text: glyph row 3 ($92 + 3).
Text: glyph row 4 ($92 + 4).
Text: glyph row 5 ($92 + 5).
Text: glyph row 6 ($92 + 6).
Text: glyph row 7, the last ($92 + 7); also the start value when the second font's width is measured ($BB8A).

$9A-$A1: no traced instruction uses these bytes, which lie between the glyph rows ($92-$99) and the spill bytes ($A2-$A9). $A1 changed only before the game started (the KERNAL's jiffy clock, $A0-$A2, ran during the crack screen).
Text: the right-hand parts of the glyph rows, $A2-$A9, shifted out of $92-$99 when the cursor is not on a cell boundary; drawn into the next cell.
Text: glyph spill row 6 ($A2 + 6).
Text: glyph spill row 7 ($A2 + 7).
$AA-$B1: no traced instruction uses these bytes ($AA, $AE and $AF were listed only from switch tables decoded as code); constant in every snapshot.
Text: bitmap address of the glyph's first row in its left cell (low byte; high $B3), from the cursor X and the glyph row; moved to the next cell row when the glyph crosses one.
Text: high byte of the left cell pointer $B2.
Text: bitmap address of the same row in the cell to the right ($B2 + 8), low byte; the spill bytes $A2-$A9 go here.
Text: high byte of the right cell pointer $B4.
Text: font of the glyph being printed, bit 7 of the character: 0 = the font at $5000, 1 = the one at $5800 (glyph number EOR $20, all eight rows are pixels).
No traced instruction uses $B7 (it was listed only from a switch table decoded as code); it holds $01.
Text: the character being printed (print_char stores it; bit 7 is cleared before drawing). Codes below $20 are not drawn.
Text scroll: destination pointer (low; high $BA) into the band's bitmap ($6000, $6140, $6280 for the three cell rows): each pass moves every row of each cell up one pixel.
Text scroll: high byte of the destination pointer $B9.
No traced instruction uses $BB (listed only from a switch table decoded as code); it holds $FF.
Text: pointer, low byte (high $BD): first the glyph in the font, then the bitmap address of the cell, then during a scroll the cell row below, whose top pixel row is pulled up.
Text: high byte of the pointer $BC.
Text scratch: rows left in the current cell while drawing, the OR of the glyph rows when measuring the second font, and the cell row (0-2) during a scroll.
Text scroll: how many bytes of each cell are moved up (8, 8, then 7 for the last cell row, from $BD7B).
Added, with carry set, to the scroll pointer $B9/$BA by the routine at $BB18, which no instruction or address pair in the image calls or points to. 0 in every snapshot.
Text window number, an index into the margin table $BDC4: set to 0 by $BA3A and only read by s_BD7E, so the band's single window (X 3 to $13F) is the only one used.

$C2-$FF: no traced instruction of the game uses these bytes (the references listed for $CB-$FF come from switch tables decoded as code). They hold what the KERNAL and the crack left: the screen line table pattern $84-$87 at $D9-$F2, and values at $CC-$D6 and $F3-$FD that last changed while the crack handed over.

No genuine use found: the only reference is at $E00A, inside the switch table after JSR $3F11 at $E003, decoded as code. Holds $85: $D9-$F2 still hold the KERNAL's screen line table pattern ($84-$87) from before the game started.
No genuine use found: the references at $E3CF and $E3DD are inside the switch table after JSR $3F11 at $E3CA, decoded as code. Holds $85, part of the KERNAL screen line table pattern left in $D9-$F2.
No genuine use found: the only reference, $E3D6, is inside the switch table after JSR $3F11 at $E3CA, decoded as code. Holds $87, part of the KERNAL screen line table pattern left in $D9-$F2.
No genuine use found: the only reference, $E3DA, is inside the switch table after JSR $3F11 at $E3CA, decoded as code. Holds $A2 in every snapshot.
Text output queue, write index (0-31): queue_char ($BA50) stores a character at $0202 + index and advances it.
Text output queue, read index (0-31): print_queued ($BA5E) takes one character per main loop pass while it differs from $0200.
Text output queue, 32 bytes $0202-$0221: characters waiting to be printed in the text band, one per main loop pass (the typed echo and the letters).

Write index into the typed-line ring $0224 (0-127): the line editor $3731 stores each accepted key there and advances it, DEL steps back ($379F). The parser compares its own read index $C000 with it. The time prompt resets it to 0.

The typed-line ring minus one: the parser reads $0223,X with X = $0222 ($C048) to get the last character typed. When the index has just wrapped to 0 this reads $0223 itself (always 0) instead of $02A3.

The typed line: a 128-byte ring, $0224-$02A3, of every key the line editor accepts (RETURN included), written at $0224 + $0222. The parser reads the words from it with its own index $C000; the time prompt parses the time from the start (parse_bcd). In the play snapshots $0277-$027E hold '10:00 AM', put into the KERNAL keyboard buffer by the emulator's typing, not by the game.
$02A4-$02D3: 48 bytes after the typed-line ring that no traced instruction uses; zero in every snapshot (the cold start clears all of page 2).
Floor of the figure being moved, from its floor line $03AF,x by floor_of_y at $16DB: 0 top ($65), 1 middle ($A5), 2 ground ($E5), $80 between floors (on the stairs). Read at $1897, $18B4 and $19C0.

Per walking figure ($02D5 person, $02D6 dog): twice the floor the figure is climbing from, stored on each stair step while it is still on a floor line ($18BA); used as an index for the landing depth ($1BCB).
The figure move_figure is working on (0 person, 1 dog), stored at $16C4 and reloaded into X throughout the movement code.
Movement scratch: the stair direction $00/$80 handed to set_stair_state ($1865-$187E); the X nudge at a landing ($1C00-$1C18); the stair table index and signed X step ($1C38-$1C79).
walk_step: toggled $00/$FF each step while the figure is 15 or more half-pixels from its target and not at depth 5, so X steps alternate with steps toward the walking lane at depth 5 ($1AD2, $1AD7).

Per walking figure ($02DD person, $02DE dog): pass counter, +1 each move_figure pass ($16D2). ANDed with the speed mask it decides which passes move ($18AE, $18E5, $18FC, $19AB); shifted, it gives the walking frame ($1DE6). Reset to the inverted mask by mstate_reset_timer ($171D, $1738).

Per walking figure ($02DF person, $02E0 dog): steps taken in the current part of a flight of stairs; zeroed at $18A3 and $1B55, counted at $1B32; a part ends after 28, 27, 26 or 25 steps (stair_part_steps). The low three bits index the stair animation tables ($1C3B).

Per walking figure ($02E1 person, $02E2 dog), set by set_stair_state: bit 7 = going down, bit 6 = second part of the flight (after the landing, $1C28); the low bits count every fourth step ($1B3C), which nothing reads. Bits 7-6 pick the part's length and animation tables.
walk_anim ($1DDD) scratch: walk_frame_mask,x (7 person, 3 dog) shifted left with speed + 1 one-bits ($1DE3, $1DEB); only tested at $1DFD, in a tail that changes nothing.

walk_anim scratch: the pass counter shifted right by speed + 1 ($1DF1); AND walk_frame_mask,x it is the walking frame (0-7 person, 0-3 dog) given to figure_set_pose. The later read at $1E05 has no effect.
walk_step: distance in half-pixels between the figure's reference X and its target's ($19F9-$1A0C); 0 = no X move, 15 or more = far mode; compared with $02E6 ($1A7A).
walk_step: distance in depth to the target ($19EF), or to depth 5 in far mode ($1ACF).
walk_step: $FF when the target is to the right (move right), 0 when to the left ($19FC-$1A00); flipped at $1A45 after a turn; read at $1A11 (facing check) and $1AB3 (walk_right or walk_left).
walk_step: signed depth minus target depth ($19E6), or depth minus 5 ($1AC6); negative means step deeper (+1), otherwise nearer (-1) ($1A8B).
location_x_of ($1E2E) keeps Y here and puts it back on return ($1E49).
Counter in the activity handlers at $21D3-$21FB: cleared at $21E7, incremented each pass at $21EE; every eighth pass counts $21ED down.
Activity at $2F18: steps to wait before the next phase (1, 4, or a random 64-127 at $2FAE); counted down every fourth pass by $2FB5, and the phase advances when it is 0.
Activity at $2F18: pass counter, incremented at $2FB5; $02EB is counted when its low two bits are 0.
Cleared with $478D by $3953 (j_394E, reached through $800F) and by the cold start's page 2 clear; nothing reads it.
sound_dispatch's job index: $FF at $3970, incremented for each bit at $3979, used as X at $3981.
sound_dispatch's copy of the job bits $478D ($3976), shifted right per job ($397C); the loop ends when it is 0 ($3991).
Seed of a shift and exclusive-or random routine at $3E44-$3E59 (with $02F1). Nothing calls that routine; 0 in every snapshot.
Second byte of the $3E44 routine's seed ($3E4C, $3E53); that routine has no caller.
Incremented and written to the SID filter ($D416) and its shadow $7FE3 by $3A99-$3AA5, which nothing calls.
Multiplier of a shift-and-add loop at $3E5A-$3E78 ($18/$19 plus $1A/$1B times it), which nothing calls. $02F4-$02FB after it are not referenced anywhere (only the cold start's page 2 clear).
Bitmap block copier $3EA6/$3E79: bitmap bytes per row, the width in cells x 8 ($3EB3).
Bitmap block copier: the caller's A, kept at $3EA6 and handed back in A on return ($3E9C, $3F08).
Bitmap block copier: the width in cells (the caller's Y): colour bytes per row, and the step for the colour sources; returned in Y.
Bitmap block copier: the caller's X (draw_rows' row count), kept at $3EA9 and returned in X.

KERNAL-style IRQ vector: $0713 (irq_handler), set by the cold start from $0927; irq_shim jumps through it. The music player's init reads it at $B206. The next word, $0316, the KERNAL's BRK vector, still holds $FE66: the cold start skips it and the game's IRQ entry never reads it.
High byte of the IRQ vector $0314 ($07).
KERNAL-style NMI vector: $082A (nmi_rti), set by the cold start; nmi_shim jumps through it.

Jump table, the first bytes of the block the crack copies here from $4B40 before jumping to $0340; the RESET vector $FFFC (set by the cold start from $46BD) also points here. $0340 JMP cold_start, $0343 JMP $195E (the random number generator), $0346 LDA $035F / RTS (the mood). The parser code at $C040-$C233 calls the main program only through the last two ($C064, $C074); otherwise it only reads the typed line ($0222-$02A3).
Jump table entry 2: JMP $195E, the random number generator (new value in A, state in $0414-$0417). The parser module at $C000 calls it here ($C074) rather than directly.

Jump table entry 3: returns the mood $035F in A (0, 1 or 2). Called by the parser at $C064, which adds 3, 1 or 0 for moods 0, 1, 2 (table $C0AE) to the score that decides whether a request is carried out.

Bit 7 becomes the person's facing flag $039A in the handler at $5484 (a phase of the activity switched at $52DB). $FF in the image. First of the constants in this page that no code changes ($034A-$035A, $0369, $036C, $036D, $036F, $0372, $0375); the crack brought $0340-$03FF over from $4B40, so they are this copy's settings.

Colour pair used by $B9BE for the person when the random number (AND $1F) is 16 or more; below 16 the random number itself is used. Indexes the pairs at $BA0E (body colour $1393, sprite multicolour 0 $D025). 3 in the image.
Colour index used by the handler at $B9F5 (switch at $AC5C) when its random number (AND $0F) is 8 or more: picks $D025 and $1393 from the table at $BA2E. 3 in the image.
House hour (0-23) at which daily_schedule reaches its last step and asks for the evening list ($035C = $41): 23 in the image.
House hour at which daily_schedule rings the alarm clock (step 0, tick 0) and at which step 3 returns to step 1: 3 in the image.
Tick of the alarm hour (0-11, five house minutes each) at which the ringing alarm starts the morning list ($035C = $81): 2 in the image.

Index 0-7 into three eight-entry tables at $E2FF, $E307 and $E30F, one per schedule step, that tell the activity chooser where to pick the next activity: 0 = by weekday (day 5 from the list at $E399, day 6 from $E367, other days from $E345), bit 7 set = from $E399, other values = from $E367. 4 in the image; nothing writes it.
Number of entries in morning_list ($0352): 3.
Activity numbers the chooser runs in turn after the alarm ($035C = $81): $6C, $4B, $0B (two spare bytes follow). The index is $035B.
Number of entries in evening_list ($0358): 1.
Activity numbers the chooser runs in turn at the late hour ($035C = $41): $6E (two spare bytes follow). When they are done the chooser sets schedule step 0 and clears the alarm flag $2B50.
Activity chooser: index into morning_list or evening_list; set to $FF when bit 0 of $035C asks for a restart, advanced before each entry.

Request from daily_schedule to the activity chooser ($E293): $81 = run morning_list from the start, $41 = run evening_list from the start (bit 0 = restart the index), 0 = none. Cleared by the chooser when a list is done and by daily_schedule at the alarm hour.

daily_schedule step, 0-3: 0 until the alarm (the chooser sets 0 after evening_list), then 1, 2 and 3 at six-hour steps. The activity chooser dispatches on it at $E2E3 and also tests it with the illness level at $E235.
House hour (0-23) at which daily_schedule takes its next step: six hours on (schedule_in_6_hours) or $034D (schedule_at_late_hour).

The mood, 0-2, drawn on his face: head frames below $18 get +0, +$0F or +$1E (head_mood_offsets). house_clock moves it along 1, 0, 1, 2 every two days; while the illness level $0365 is 2 or more it is held at 2; CTRL P (petting) sets 0 at $2C39 when the person is not moving ($03BC) and the check s_2DE4 with X = $2B passes. The parser adds 3, 1 or 0 for moods 0, 1, 2 to a request's score ($C064 through jt_get_mood), so mood 0 is the happiest.
Days each mood lasts before house_clock moves it on, indexed by the mood: 2, 2, 2.
Days left before the mood $035F changes (reloaded from mood_days).
Direction of the mood cycle: bit 7 clear = going down (towards 0), set = going up; flipped at the ends of 0-2, where the mood jumps back to 1.

Illness level 0-4 (0 = well). start_illness sets 1 (and sprite multicolour 1, $D026, to green 5); while $0367 is set it rises one level every 12 ticks, otherwise it falls one level per tick, and at 0 $D026 goes back to $0A. Level 2 or more holds the mood at 2. Read by the movement code at $170E and by the activity chooser at $E232.
Ticks until the illness level changes: 12 while getting worse, 1 while recovering.
1 while the illness gets worse (set by start_illness); cleared by $392F once both the food and water levels ($0371, $036E) are below 3, after which the illness recovers.

Flag used by the activity code: set to 0 at $33CF or $FF at $33DF (handlers of the switch at $338C) and read as an index at $3404-$3444. While non-zero the activity chooser picks activity $1F ($E22D, $E250) and turns requests other than $2E into $1F, keeping the request in $E127 ($E389).

Constant $2D from the image, a personality byte. Bits 0-2 pick an AND mask (tables at $20DC and $96C5) for random draws, and bit 7 decides whether a draw passes on a non-zero or a zero result: the in-bed states ($206E-$20CF), the choices at $9491-$94BA, the value stored to $47AB at $930D-$9324 (table $932F). At $E1AA bit 7 also stops the chooser from queueing activity $79. The next two bytes ($22, $02) are not read by any traced instruction.
House hour (12) at which the activity chooser runs activity $4C once a day ($E25C, flag $E26F).
House hour (17) at which the activity chooser runs activity $01 once a day ($E276, flag $E28A).

Water need level 0-3: house_clock raises it each time water_timer ($0370) runs out, and a rise from 2 or more holds it at 3 and calls start_illness. The activity chooser picks activity $1D (29, a drink of water, $37EA) at level 1 now and then (random), at 2 or more when the tank $2B51 has water or once when water_timer is 2; $33A6 does the same. Reset to 0 at $38C5, where the timer is also reloaded.
Ticks per water need level: 15 (reloads $0370).
Ticks until the water need level $036E rises; counted down every tick, and by the chooser at $E1DB when it is 2 and the tank is empty.

Food need level 0-3: house_clock raises it each time food_timer ($0373) runs out, and a rise from 2 or more holds it at 3 and calls start_illness. At 2 or more the handler at $308C can start activity $20 (32, whose handlers at $52D8 on reset this level at $5447); the activity chooser picks activity $4A at level 1 now and then, at 2 or more when $30B4 is non-zero or once when food_timer is 2. Reset to 0 at $5447, where the timer is reloaded.
Ticks per food need level: 20 (reloads $0373).
Ticks until the food need level $0371 rises; counted down every tick, and by the chooser at $E207 when it is 2 and $30B4 is 0.

Set to 1 by house_clock when the countdown $0376 runs out, 7 ticks after a food or water need reset ($392F). While it is set the activity chooser ($E21F) and $33AF start activity 4, whose script ($9076) runs activity 114 ($8ED2): that copies it into sound request 19 ($3573) and clears it.
Ticks loaded into $0376 by $392F, which the code resetting the food need ($5450) and the water need ($38CE) calls: 7.
Ticks until $0374 is set: loaded from $0375 by $392F when it is 0, counted down by house_clock.
Day counter: low three bits 0-6 are the day of the week (the chooser treats 5 and 6 specially at $E328); bit 3 alternates each week (values 0-6, then 8-14). 6 at the start.
Days passed since the start, counted by house_clock and held at 255.

Hour of the house day, 0-23, advanced every 12 ticks (about nine minutes at 50 Hz). 15 at the start. Drives daily_schedule and the chooser's timed activities. Not tied to the wall clock the player set.
Tick within the house hour, 0-11 (one tick = 2304 frames, 46 s at 50 Hz).

An activity request that also locks the keyboard (scan_keyboard does nothing while it is non-zero): activity 0, the chooser, takes it as the next activity ($E145) and clears it ($E14C). $7A in the image, so the first activity after the time prompt is $7A; while it is set the dog heads for the front door (location $2E) and gets no long waits ($17BB-$17E0), and $931D picks 2. The movement code also tests for $7B and $7C ($170A, $178F, $1793), but nothing stores those values.

Countdown of the head turning at $ACF3: when it runs out the head's frame $038F steps one notch toward its target $03F4, and it is reloaded with 5-8 ($AD19), or 7-$FF once the target is reached ($ADBF); at 0 a new target near the body's direction is chosen and it is set to 1 ($AE5E). Also set to 1 at $1B26, $24B7, $2575 and $E107 and cleared at $24AB, $549E, $E094 and $E0E2.

Column clip per figure ($0381 body ... $0385 head), applied when the image is rebuilt (s_13AC from $0F94): bits 0-6 = how many 2-bit pixel columns (1-12) are blanked, bit 7 set = from the left, clear = from the right. The doorway code sets $81/$01/$00 ($3229, $32E4, $32EF) and moves it one column per half-pixel step ($32FC-$3354); saved and cleared at $1F2A-$1F4A. $0C (the whole body blanked) in the image.
Column clip of figure 2 (element 2 of fig_clip): only ever cleared ($1F4D).
Column clip of the head (element 4 of fig_clip): always written together with the body's $0381 ($1F50, $322E, $32E9, $32F4, $330A, $3321).

Colour of each figure's multicolour sprite ($0386 body ... $038A head): stored at each rebuild ($0FAB) from the address patched into the LDA at $0FA8 ($1393, $042D, $1394, $1395, $042E) and copied to the colour shadow at $1177. The cold start first copies the dog's colour into it ($04D4), which the first rebuild replaces.
The head's colour (element 4 of fig_colour), used as the colour of the person's second sprite ($1193).

Frame number of each figure ($038B body, $038C dog, $038D and $038E props, $038F head): the graphic is figure_frames[frame + figure_frame_base,x] ($0E41). Usually set through figure_set_pose ($1ADF), which asks for a rebuild. Body frames: 0-7 walking, 8 standing, $09-$17 stairs, $11 turning, higher values other poses.

Frame of figure 2, the object sprite, from the shared object frames: set by the activities, for example the carried item ($28F6), water spray $0B ($1F6C), a pen $0E-$10 ($5BC6), food $13/$14 ($5340, $54B4).
Frame of figure 3: only ever set to $15, at $53AA (activity 32).

Frame of the head (figure 4): bits 0-2 the direction it looks (0 at the viewer, 2 left, 4 away, 6 right; 1-3 drawn mirrored), bits 3-4 the tilt row ($00, $08, $10); frames $18-$1E are special faces. Stepped toward $03F4 by the head turning ($AD96); also set at $243B (nod and shake), $541B and $E0D5.

The person's facing, 0-7, taken by figure_set_pose from the table $AE8D for his frame ((8 - d) AND 7 when not mirrored, $1AEC-$1B0C); when it changes, the direction bits of the head's target $03F4 are replaced and $037C is set to 1. Used by the head turning at $AE10 (table $AE65).

$FF while the person carries something: unpack_figure_sprite then draws body frames 0-$18 from the arms-forward set (+$5D, and $21 as $6A). Set at $2915, $30C7, $3880, $390A and $AF2E; cleared at $1E9E, $1ED3, $2A06, $2F0C, $3183, $3823, $38AA, $5357 and $AA43; read at $95ED.
Written ($FF) once at $2677, while figure 2 is set up, and never read; $0394 may have been meant there (see $0396).
Non-zero = the object sprite is multicolour ($0394 figure 2, $0395 figure 3; read at $1248). Only ever stored as $FF or $83 ($1F5B, $2910, $2F5A, $387D, $54A2 and others).
Figure 3's multicolour flag: $FF, stored at $539B only.

Non-zero = the figure's sprites go behind the background picture ($D01B): $0396 all four of the person's ($11E3), $0397 the dog, $0398/$0399 figures 2 and 3. The person's is set to 9 at $5556 and cleared at $553B and $267C (the clear at $267C, next to the write of $0392, may have been meant for $0398).
The dog's behind-the-background flag: read at $1210, never written, so always 0.
Figure 2's behind-the-background flag ($0399 is figure 3's, never written): set non-zero at $5580, 0 at $2906, $384A, $549B, $5590 and $AFE3; read through $1264.

Facing of each figure ($039A body ... $039E head): 0 = the image as stored (facing right), non-zero = mirrored (facing left). unpack_figure_sprite mirrors the rows ($0F22 on). Walking sets 0 ($1907) or figure_face_left,x (8 person, 4 dog; $1937) through set_facing, which asks for a rebuild.
Figure 2's facing: copied from the person's ($2655, $294D, $3859, $5BF4) or set to 0 ($1F53, $2FD6, $556B, $AFE6, $BFD8).
Figure 3's facing: set to 0 at $5397 only.
The head's facing: 8 when its direction is 1-3, else 0 (head turning, $AD99-$ADAB), or from the table at $2460 ($243E).

Speed index of each walking figure ($039F person, $03A0 dog), set in movement state 0 ($1715): 1 normally, 2 for the person while ill ($0365) or when $037B is $7B. speed_mask turns it into the mask $1956[n] (1 or 3: a step every second or fourth pass, half that on the stairs); walk_anim uses it too.

X / 2 of each figure ($03A3-$03A6), the unit of the location tables: recomputed by calc_half_x ($1E56) and at $5BE2. Read by location_x_of ($1E31, $1E46), $2DEF, the doorway code ($32A0-$333D) and the footsteps ($3519, $3531).
Figure 2's X / 2: written at $2A0C and $5BE2, never read.

X position of each figure, low byte ($03A7 body, $03A8 dog, $03A9 and $03AA props), in sprite units: walking moves it by 1 ($190F, $1940), the stairs and doorway code too; copied to the sprite shadow at $112A. The head has no entry: it is placed from the body.
Figure 2's X, set by the activities near the person ($1F38, $265B, $29D1, $2F46, $2F7F, $386C, $54D4 and others).
Figure 3's X: $80, stored at $538F only.

X bit 8 of each figure ($03AB-$03AE), non-zero for X of 256 or more. For the person and the dog the value is the bit of the figure's first hardware sprite ($03E3), flipped at $1914 and re-masked when the sprite changes ($10AB-$10B3); read for $D010 ($11EE, $121E, $1256) and by calc_half_x.
The dog's X bit 8, read at $121E for $D010.
Figure 2's X bit 8: copied from the person's ($1F33, $266D, $2F85, $3872, $BFE7), computed as $80/0 ($29D5-$29E6) or cleared ($5498, $556E, $AFD6).
Figure 3's X bit 8: cleared at $5394 only.

Floor line of each figure ($03AF-$03B2): $65, $A5 or $E5 on the three floors, values in between on the stairs. The sprite's Y is this minus the depth $03B3 minus the frame offset $03B7 ($10FF-$110A). Locations take it from location_y ($1D36).
Figure 2's floor line, set relative to the person's by the activities (for example $29B4).
Figure 3's floor line: $E5 (ground floor), stored at $53A0 only.

Depth into the room of each figure ($03B3-$03B6), about 2-15: a larger depth is further back, drawn higher on the screen and sorted behind (key depth x 8 + tie-break, $1021). Walking moves it by 1 ($1A93); locations take it from location_depth ($1DA4).
Figure 2's depth, usually the person's minus 1 to 5 so the object is drawn in front of him ($267F, $2F97, $54CE, $5B55).
Figure 3's depth: 9, stored at $53A5 only.

Signed Y adjustment of each figure's current frame ($03B7-$03BB), read at each rebuild from the figure's table (pointers $12AD/$12B2: $14F1 body, $154E dog, $156C props, $156A head) by frame ($0FF7-$1009); a change sets bit 0 of the flags. Subtracted at $1107 for figures 0-3 only, so the head's value ($03BB) is never used.

Movement state of the person ($03BC) and the dog ($03BD), the index of move_figure's switch: 0 idle, 1 the dog between walks, 2 and 5 choose the route, 3 walk to the stairs, 4 on the stairs, 6 walk to the target. The activities set the person's to 2 to send him walking ($AB6F, $2FF9, $3923 and others) and wait for 0 ($535E, $554C, $8FA7, $9174, $95F2).

Target location of the person ($03C0) and the dog ($03C1), 0-$36, an index into location_y/location_x/location_depth: $00-$2F sixteen per floor, $30-$35 the stair ends, $36 a scratch location (set_custom_location). The dog's is drawn from dog_destinations ($17C5-$17E2); the person's is set by $AB63 and the activities, and saved and restored around a request ($8FEE, $8F61).

Update flags of each figure ($03C4 body, $03C5 dog, $03C6 and $03C7 props, $03C8 head): bit 7 visible (sprite enable), bit 1 rebuild the image (update_figure_sprites does one figure per pass, highest number first), bit 2 image just rebuilt, bit 0 position, colour or pointer changed; bits 0 and 2 are cleared when the shadows are written ($10F5). move_figure waits while bits 0-1 are set ($16C7) and the activity dispatcher while any of bits 0-2 are ($8DBC).
The dog's flags (element 1 of fig_flags): bit 7 shows its two sprites ($11FF).
Figure 2's flags: the activities show ($83, $82, $81) and hide ($00, $02) the object sprite here.
Figure 3's flags: $83 at $53AF (shown), $00 at $5382 (hidden).

The head's flags: bit 7 enables the person's second and fourth sprites ($11CA); when bit 2 is set (head rebuilt) the head's bits are cleared and the body's bit 0 set ($10BB-$10CF). The head turning ($ACF3) and $240F wait on bits 1-2.

Depth sort workspace for figures 0-3 ($03C9-$03CC): depth x 8 + tie-break ($1021), sorted in place ($103B-$1073), then overwritten with each figure's new first hardware sprite ($1080) and compared with $03CD ($1097).

First hardware sprite of each figure ($03CD body, $03CE dog, $03CF and $03D0 props): the person uses n to n+3 (body colour, head colour, then the two black outlines), the dog n and n+1, each object one. Updated at $109F (which asks for a refresh); indexes the shadow registers ($10FA, $114D) and the bit masks ($11C7, $1917).
The dog's first hardware sprite (element 1 of fig_hw_sprite), read at $1204.
First hardware sprite of figure 2 ($03CF) and figure 3 ($03D0), read at $123C.
Tie-break added to the depth sort key, 1, 2, 3, 4 for figures 0-3 ($1027), so at equal depth the lower figure number comes out in front.

Figure numbers in depth order after the sort ($03D6-$03D9): position 3 the nearest ... 0 the furthest ($1030-$1073); hardware sprites are dealt from 0 starting with the nearest ($107B). $03DA after it, and the masks $FE, $FD ... $7F at $03DB-$03E2, are not read by any instruction.

One bit per hardware sprite, $01, $02 ... $80 ($03E3-$03EA), used for $D010, $D015, $D01B and $D01C bits ($10B0, $122C, $1242-$126C, $191A). The four bytes after it, $00 $42 $2C $16, are not referenced.
s_12B7's current image row widened by one pixel to each side ($03EF-$03F1, $12E1-$1317), ORed with the rows above and below to make the outline sprite ($131F-$1328).
Byte 1 of s_12B7's widened row ($12F2, $130A, $130D).
Byte 2 of s_12B7's widened row ($12FC-$1303). $03F2-$03F3 after it are not referenced.

The frame the head turns toward (same form as $038F): chosen at random around the body's direction by the head turning ($ADD5-$AE59); its direction bits are replaced when the body turns ($1B19-$1B21); 8 = look at the viewer ($23F4, $24BF, $E0DD, $E102); $0F at $5B6A. $03F5-$03F7 after it are not referenced.
Four bytes $01, $08, $31, $85 (they read as BCD) from the image, before the name at $03FC. No instruction, and no address pair anywhere in the image, refers to $03F5-$03FB.

ASCII 'Bill', the start of the name 'Billy Bob Binkle' that runs on to $040B, followed by zeros to $0413. Part of the $0340-$03FF block the crack copies from $4B40 (the rest comes back from $4C00 with $0400-$07FF). No instruction operand and no address pair in the image points into $03FC-$0413, so nothing traced reads or prints it; the letters are signed 'Your Friend'.
ASCII 'y Bob Binkle', the rest of the name begun at $03FC, then eight zero bytes ($040C-$0413). Not referenced by any instruction or address pair in the image.

Random number generator state (j_195E, jt_random): the last value returned in A. Many routines read it directly as a random byte (for example $17B0, $AD11, $BF66). In the image as loaded, $0414-$0417 hold the ASCII letters 'Zeke' (the crack's copy at $4C14), so those four letters are the generator's starting state; the first call (clock_start, from the cold start) overwrites them, and nothing reads them as text.
Random number generator: second state byte, also read directly by the activity chooser as a second random value ($E1E7, $E213).
Random number generator: temporary copy of $0415.
Random number generator: incremented on every call; while bit 7 is set the caller's A and carry are added into $0415.

Pointer to the next entry of the current activity script, a zero-terminated list of activity numbers (for example $AA56, $8D99): $8F0E reads the next number into $8D9B and advances the pointer. Set at $3104, $33C1, $8FCF, $9193 and $AA4D.
High byte of the activity script pointer $0423.
Non-zero (3 in the image): $B9BE leaves the head colour $042E as it is. At 0 it would pick a random one ($0B or $09, or $D025).
Real-time clock seconds, BCD 0-59, advanced once a second (every 50 frames) by $2E94 from the raster IRQ; each wrap flags a new minute in $09E9.
Real-time clock minutes, BCD 0-59: set by the time prompt, advanced by $2E94. The wall clock's minute hand.
Real-time clock hours, BCD 1-12 (0 is accepted at the prompt): set by the time prompt, advanced by $2E94. The wall clock's hour hand.
0 for am, 1 for pm as typed at the prompt; $2E94 increments it at every 12 o'clock rather than toggling it. No traced instruction reads it.
Counted up (held at 255) by the handler at $2EE1 (a phase of the activity switched at $2797). Nothing else reads it.
Eight flags filled one random bit at a time by the handler at $2EE1 until all are set ($FF). Nothing else reads it.
The dog's colour (9, brown): loaded for figure 1 through the self-modified LDA at $0FA8; the cold start also copies it to $0386.

Colour of the person's head sprite (figure 4, the upper sprite, whose lower rows hold the head), loaded through the self-modified LDA at $0FA8; $B9BE would randomise it if $0425 were 0. 9 in the image.
Second frame counter, incremented by the raster IRQ; house_clock watches its bit 7 go back to 0, once every 256 frames.
1 while the activity timer runs: set with $0433 = 104 by $2E87 (called at $2753) and cleared by $2E73 when $0433 runs out. Read by the activity code at $2469, $2768, $276E, $33D2.
Activity timer count: counted down by $2E73 (main loop stage 7) on passes when the frame counter's low two bits are 0, so it lasts about 104 x 4 frames when the loop is quick.

Cold start, reached from reset_jumps at $0340 (the crack jumps there; $FFFC also points there). Stack to $FF; copies the six hardware vectors $FFFA-$FFFF from $46BD and the IRQ and NMI vectors $0314/$0318 from $0927; stops the CIA timers and masks all CIA interrupts; VIC bank 1 ($DD00); $01 = x5 (I/O in, ROMs out) and $00 = $2F; VIC registers $D000-$D02E from vic_init_values ($06E1); enables the raster interrupt at line $28. Also sets $DD03 = 0 and the SID volume to 0. Clears $4800-$4FFF (where the crack screen was; the figures' sprite images are unpacked there, blocks $20-$3F), the nine zero-page bytes listed at $08D3 and page 2 ($0200-$02FF). Then $3713 (clears the sound state and the SID voices, then the music player init $B000), clock_start, $B9BE (random colours for the person; its exit through $8F0B leaves the activity phase $4C at 1), copies $042D to $0386, builds the figures five times (update_figure_sprites), sets bitmap mode ($D011=$3B, $D018=$78, $D016=$D8, $D026=$0A) and falls into the time-of-day prompt at $04F8.

The time-of-day prompt: opens the text band ($BA3A), prints txt_time_prompt, then loops reading the joysticks, the keyboard (scan_keyboard_now, which ignores the $037B lock) and echoing keys through the line editor $3731 into the typed line $0224, keeping $0710 at 2 so the band stays open. More than 15 characters restarts the prompt. On RETURN the line must be digits, ':', digits, optional spaces, then A or P and M in either case: hours (kept as the last two digits, BCD) must be below $13 and minutes below $60, else the prompt starts again. Stores hours in $0428, minutes in $0427, $0429 = 0 for am and 1 for pm, closes the band ($BAD4), calls clock_start and enters the main loop through set_screen_on ($0589). Hour 0 is accepted.

End of every main loop pass (and entry from the time prompt): sets the display-enable bit of $D011, but clears it again, blanking the screen, while the idle counter $2D is 10 or more (about 10 x 65536 frames, three and a half hours at 50 Hz, without a key), then jumps to main_loop.

Reads both joystick ports with the keyboard matrix idle: $DC00 bits 0-4 (control port 2) into $2F, then $DC01 bits 0-4 (control port 1) into $2E; active low. Leaves port A as output with $FF and port B as input, as the keyboard scan expects. Called from the main loop (stage 2) and from the time prompt.
Keyboard scan: number of SHIFT keys found down this scan (key code $23).
Keyboard scan: number of CTRL keys found down this scan (key code $24).
The RTS shared by scan_keyboard and scan_keyboard_now for their early exits.
Main-loop keyboard scan (stage 2). Does nothing while $037B, a pending activity request, is non-zero; otherwise falls into scan_keyboard_now.

Keyboard scan without the $037B lock (the time prompt calls it directly). Returns at once unless $DC01 reads $FF with all rows released and $DC00 reads back $FF (no joystick line held). Any key down clears the idle counters $2C/$2D. Walks the 64 keys from index 63 down (index in $34, row = index AND 7 selected by key_row_select, column = index / 8 tested with key_col_bits), counting SHIFT ($23) in $05C4 and CTRL ($24) in $05C5, skipping $21 keys; the lowest-numbered other key held is kept in $32. Letters: SHIFT subtracts $20 (upper case), CTRL leaves the control code (AND $1F); SHIFT also clears bit 4 of digits and turns / : ; into ? [ ]. A key equal to $33 (the key already taken and still held) is ignored; code $5C or no key clears $33. A new key is stored in $30, $31 and $33.

The keyboard, as scan_keyboard reads it: 64 ASCII codes indexed by row + 8 * column of the key matrix (row selected through $DC00, column read from $DC01). Special codes: $23 SHIFT, $24 CTRL, $21 a key ignored, $5C no character.
One bit per keyboard column, tested against what $DC01 reads back.
The byte written to $DC00 to select each keyboard row: one bit low.

47 values copied by the cold start to the VIC registers $D000-$D02E: sprite X/Y pairs ($20,$80 $38,$80 ... $C8,$80), $D010=$00, $D011=$0B (screen off), $D016=$08, $D018=$78, then zeros (sprites off, no interrupts) through $D02E.

Text band open counter: set to 3 when something is printed ($BA3A, print_queued), counted down every 256 frames while the output queue is empty; at 0 the band is cleared ($BAD4). The time prompt keeps it at 2. The IRQ handles the band (hires split, cursor sprite) while this or $0711 is non-zero.

Bottom raster line of a taller text band: the IRQ waits for it instead of $49 and hides the cursor while it is non-zero, and the line editor ($3731), CTRL R ($2BA6) and the movement code at $17C8 test it. No store to it was found anywhere in the image and it is 0 in every snapshot, so the band always ends at line $49.
Hides the cursor sprite while non-zero (read at $07A8). No store to it was found anywhere in the image; 0 in every snapshot.

The game's IRQ handler, reached through $0314 from irq_shim; about three interrupts a frame, one of them the raster interrupt at line $28. Keeps the low bits of $01 in $092D and forces I/O in. Any source but the raster (the CIA1 timers of the timer-driven tune player) goes to timer_irq through $8018. Raster: saves $D016 in $41, finds the sprite lowest on the screen ($092E) and runs the real-time clock ($2E94). While the text band is open ($0710 or $0711 non-zero) it switches the band to hires ($D016 AND $EF), borrows that sprite as the text cursor (pointer $1F, so $47C0; dark grey; Y $35; X = the text cursor $8C/$8D + 13; shown only while $0711 and $0712 are zero), waits for the band's bottom line ($0711, or $49 when it is 0), delays by band_split_delays, restores $D016 and puts the sprite back. Then acknowledges, clears the raster high bit, counts the frame in $2B/$2C/$2D and $0430, sets $40, and calls sound_dispatch ($800C) while $801E is set (a timer-player tune is playing) or else the $B000 music player's frame routine ($B003). Restores $01 and the registers.

IRQ handler continued (raster path): carries the frame count from $2B into $2C and $2D, counts $0430, sets $40 = 1, then calls sound_dispatch through $800C while $801E is set (a tune of the timer-driven player is playing), else the $B000 music player's frame routine through $B003; finally puts back the $01 bits kept in $092D, pulls Y, X and A and returns (RTI).
The NMI handler: a lone RTI. $0318/$0319 point here (set from $092B by the cold start) and nmi_shim jumps through them, so RESTORE does nothing.
Hardware IRQ entry ($FFFE in RAM; the KERNAL is banked out, $01=$35). Pushes A, X and Y as the KERNAL would and jumps through $0314, so the game keeps a KERNAL-style vector.
Hardware NMI entry ($FFFA in RAM): jumps through $0318, which points at an RTI ($082A), so RESTORE does nothing. Counted zero hits in play.

IRQ helper: saves the registers of the hardware sprite chosen for the text cursor (register offset in $092E, the sprite with the largest Y this frame): $D015 to $42, its X and Y to $43/$44, $D010 to $45, $D01C to $46, its colour to $47, its pointer ($5FF8+n) to $48 and $D01B to $49. Returns with X = sprite number and Y = register offset.

IRQ helper: puts back everything cursor_sprite_save kept in $42-$49 (pointer, colour, $D01B, $D01C, $D010, Y, X and $D015) once the raster has passed the text band, so the borrowed sprite shows at its own place further down the screen.

IRQ helper: counts the hardware sprites whose Y lies from $3C (band bottom minus 21) up to, but not including, $3D (the band's bottom line). The count, 0-8, picks the delay in band_split_delays ($08FC) so the $D016 write lands at the same place on the line whatever sprite DMA steals.
Converts a lower-case ASCII letter in A to upper case (subtracts $20 from anything $60 or above). Used by the time prompt on the am/pm letters.

Reads decimal digits from the typed line $0224 starting at index X into $34 as BCD (each digit shifted in from the right, so only the last two count). Returns with the first non-digit in A and X just past it. Used by the time prompt for hours and minutes.
Nine zero-page addresses the cold start clears ($04B7): $2A, $2C, $2D (idle counter), $4C (activity phase), $68 (sub-phase), $30, $33, $31 (keys) and $32.
One bit per sprite, 1 << n for n = 0-7: ORed into $D010 and $D015 by the IRQ handler for the cursor sprite, and used by $2EED to pick a free bit.
The complements of bit_masks ($FE, $FD ... $7F): the IRQ handler ANDs $D010, $D01C, $D01B and $D015 with them to take the cursor sprite out of multicolour, priority and enable.
Sixteen bytes, each bit mask twice ($01,$01,$02,$02 ... $80,$80). No traced instruction reads them; bit_masks_inverted is only ever indexed 0-7.

Nine timing values for the text band split, indexed by the number of sprites near the band's bottom (count_sprites_near_band): the low nibble is the DEY delay count; bits 6 and 7 add a cycle each through BIT $3C / BVS / BMI before $D016 is written at $07E9.
ASCII, printed a character at a time through print_char until a byte with bit 7 set ($FF here): "Enter time of day (HH:MM am/pm)> "
Initial KERNAL-style vectors copied by the cold start to $0314-$0319 (a zero byte is skipped, so the BRK vector is left alone): IRQ $0713 (irq_handler), BRK $0000 (skipped), NMI $082A (nmi_rti).
IRQ handler: the low three bits of $01 as the interrupted code had them, put back on exit.
IRQ handler: register offset (2 x sprite number) of the sprite lowest on the screen, borrowed for the text cursor.

Score of the last parsed request ($C014, kept by the main loop at $098B). The activity chooser ($E16E) carries out the queued request from the ring at $E12A while it is 8 or more, sets it to 0 when the ring is empty, and adds 1 on each visit while it is 4-7, so a request scoring 4-7 is carried out a few visits later and one below 4 is not taken from the ring.
Main loop stage number, 1-12, written before each stage. No traced instruction reads it.

The main loop. At most one pass per frame, since stage 1 waits for raster line $FA before it writes the sprite registers (46 passes in about a second were counted live). Counts passes in $09DB and writes the stage number 1-12 to $0930 before each stage (nothing reads it). 1 update_figure_sprites; 2 read_joysticks, scan_keyboard, print_queued; 3 $E3BF (an RTS); 4 house_clock; 5 $2E6F (CLC, RTS); 6 nothing; 7 $2E73 (the $0432/$0433 timer); 8 $3476; 9 the line editor $3731 and the parser $C040, then, when the parser has a result ($C002 non-zero), keeps its score ($C014) in $092F, copies the result bytes into the 16-entry ring at $E12A (write index $E128; a score of 8 or more first sets the read index $E129 to it and $BEFC to 1) and clears $C002 ($C141); 10 $16C4 for the person (X=0), then for the dog (X=1); 11 $ACF3 (turns the head, figure 4); 12 $8DAB, the activity dispatcher. Ends through set_screen_on.

Main loop pass counter (incremented at the top of every pass); other code tests its low bits to act only every fourth or eighth pass ($2D59, $9739, and also $2CAA, $2CEB, $2DBB, $58EA, $59B6, $59C5, $5BA6).

Called by the cold start and when the time has been entered: sets the phone countdown $09EA to a random 32-63 house-clock ticks and runs house_clock from $0AA4: draws the wall clock (while $09E9 is non-zero, as it is at start) and runs the food, water, illness and schedule checks that follow it.
Wall clock redraw flag: $2E94 sets it to $FF when a minute passes; house_clock redraws the clock when bit 7 is set, and on every tick while it is non-zero; draw_wall_clock sets it to 1.
Ticks until the phone rings by itself: clock_start and each ring set it to a random 32-63; at 0 house_clock sets $BEF5 and $2B4C to that new value, as CTRL C sets them to $FF.

Main-loop stage 4. Clears the tick flag $0BB0; every 256 frames (bit 7 of the frame counter $0430 going back to 0) counts $0A11 down, and every 9th time (2304 frames, 46 s at 50 Hz) makes a tick: 12 ticks ($037A) make an hour ($0379, 0-23); a new day advances the weekday counter $0377 and the saturating day count $0378, and every $0363 days (two) moves the mood $035F one step along the cycle 1, 0, 1, 2. Each tick counts down the food and water timers $0373/$0370: when one runs out it is reloaded ($0372, $036F) and its need level ($0371 food, $036E water) goes up; if the level was already 2 or more it is set to 3 and start_illness is called. Each tick also counts down $0376 (sets $0374 at zero) and the phone countdown $09EA (at zero the phone rings as with CTRL C), runs the illness course ($0365-$0367; sprite multicolour 1, $D026, green 5 while ill, back to $0A when well) and daily_schedule. The wall clock is redrawn from the real time $0428/$0427 on every tick and whenever the interrupt clock flags a new minute ($09E9 bit 7).
house_clock: counts the 256-frame periods down; at 0 a tick happens and it is reloaded with 9.
house_clock: non-zero once bit 7 of the frame counter $0430 has been seen set, so the return to 0 is counted once.

house_clock continued: $0A13 jumps to the redraw when a new minute is flagged; $0A16 is the tick: reloads the divider, advances the tick and, when due, the hour, weekday and day count, sets $0BB0, counts down the food, water and $0376 timers, and every $0363 days moves the mood; then the redraw check at $0AA4.

Redraws the little analogue clock on the house wall: copies the clock face (clock_face_top/bottom) into the bitmap at $6D90 and $6ED0, then draws the hour hand (3 steps; the hour $0428 in BCD, plus one from minute 35 on) and the minute hand (5 steps; minutes $0427 divided by five in decimal mode) with draw_clock_hand.

Called when the food or water need level rises while already 2 or more. Does nothing while the player has been idle for $2D >= 10 (the screen is blanked). Otherwise, if not yet ill ($0365 = 0), makes him ill: level 1, $0366 = 12 ticks, sprite multicolour 1 ($D026) = 5, green; always sets $0367 so the illness gets worse.
Set to 1 by house_clock on a tick and cleared at the start of the next pass; the phone countdown, the illness course and daily_schedule run only when it is set.
Set to $FF by CTRL A ($2BDE); in schedule step 0 the next tick starts the morning list at once, then it is cleared.

Part of house_clock, run once per tick: the daily schedule around the alarm clock. $035D is the step, $035E the house hour of the next step, $035C the request flags read by the activity chooser at $E293. Step 0: at hour $034E, tick 0, rings the alarm clock ($2B50/$2B4E/$3574); at tick $034F of the ringing hour, or at once after CTRL A ($0BB1), sets $035C = $81 (run the list at $0352) and goes to step 1 with the next step six hours on. Steps 1 and 2 move on every six hours (the second to hour $034D); step 3 sets $035C = $41 (run the list at $0358) at hour $034D and at hour $034E goes back to step 1. The activity chooser returns it to step 0 ($E2DA) once the $0358 list has run.
Sets the schedule's next hour $035E to the house hour $0379 plus 6, wrapped to 0-23.
Sets the schedule's next hour $035E to $034D (23 in this image), wrapped to 0-23.

Draws one hand of the wall clock by clearing 2-bit pixels in the 8 x 16 clock area at $6D90/$6ED0. A = length in steps (3 hour hand, 5 minute hand), X = position (0-11 for minutes; BCD 1-$13 for hours) looked up in clock_hand_dirs: its low nibble is the start in clock_hand_steps and its high nibble flips the steps' directions. Works in $18 (flips), $19 (steps left), $1A (step index), $1B (pixel mask), $1C (byte offset: bits 0-2 row, bit 3 right cell, bit 7 lower cell row), $1D (temp). Calls $5B2A before and $5B29 after each bitmap write (both are RTS here).

Steps for draw_clock_hand, 20 bytes, one per pixel of a hand: bits 5 and 7 of the high nibble move one row (bit 7 up, else down) and bits 4 and 6 (after the shift at $0C9B) move one 2-bit pixel (left or right); a step whose moves cancel after the direction flip draws nothing.

Hand positions for draw_clock_hand, indexed 0-19 (minutes / 5, or the hour in BCD so $10-$13 are hours 10-13): low nibble = first entry in clock_hand_steps, high nibble = direction flips. Indexes 12-15 are not valid BCD hours.
The wall clock's face, top half: 16 bytes of multicolour bitmap (two cells side by side) copied to $6D90 by draw_wall_clock before the hands are drawn.
The wall clock's face, bottom half: 16 bytes copied to $6ED0 (the cells below $6D90).
Shadow of $D015 (sprite enable), rebuilt by update_figure_sprites ($11B6 on) from the figures' visible flags (bit 7 of $03C4-$03C8) and the slots they hold, then written to the VIC at $1299.
Shadow of $D01C (sprite multicolour): the person's two colour sprites (body and head) and the dog's colour sprite, and figures 2 and 3 when their $0394/$0395 flag is set; written at $129F.

Shadow of the sprite positions, $0D3C-$0D4B = $D000-$D00F, copied with $0D4C to the VIC at $127F. Indexed by 2 x the figure's first hardware sprite: $0D3C,y = X of its first sprite (the figure's X $03A7).
Sprite position shadow, $0D3D,y: Y of a figure's first sprite: its Y $03AF minus $03B3 minus the frame's Y offset $03B7.
Sprite position shadow, $0D3E,y: X of a figure's second sprite: the same X for the dog's outline; for the person, his X plus the head offset $135E (the head's colour sprite).

Sprite position shadow, $0D3F,y: Y of a figure's second sprite: the dog's Y again; for the person, his Y minus $135D (21 lines, one sprite height, for most poses), so the head sprite sits on top of the body sprite.
Sprite position shadow, $0D40,y: X of the person's third sprite (the body outline, same X as the body).
Sprite position shadow, $0D41,y: Y of the person's third sprite (the body outline).
Sprite position shadow, $0D42,y: X of the person's fourth sprite (the head outline, at the head's X).
Sprite position shadow, $0D43,y: Y of the person's fourth sprite (the head outline). The shadow ends at $0D4B.
Shadow of $D010 (sprite X bit 8): bits for the sprites of each figure whose X high flag ($03AB-$03AE) is set; written with the positions at $127F.
Shadow of the sprite colours $D027-$D02E ($0D4D-$0D54), copied at $1290. $0D4D,y (y = first sprite) = the figure's colour $0386,x.
Sprite colour shadow, $0D4E,y: 0 (black) for the dog's outline; for the person, the head colour $038A.
Sprite colour shadow, $0D4F,y: 0 (black), the person's body outline.
Sprite colour shadow, $0D50,y: 0 (black), the person's head outline. The colour shadow ends at $0D54.
Shadow of the sprite pointers $5FF8-$5FFF ($0D55-$0D5C), copied at $128D. $0D55,y = the figure's sprite block $0D68,x (its fill image).
Sprite pointer shadow, $0D56,y: the block after the fill (the outline) for the dog; for the person, the head's block $0D6C.
Sprite pointer shadow, $0D57,y: the person's body outline (his block + 1).
Sprite pointer shadow, $0D58,y: the head outline ($0D6C + 1). The pointer shadow ends at $0D5C.
Shadow of $D01B (sprites behind the background): the person's and the dog's sprites when $0396/$0397 are set, figures 2 and 3 when $0398/$0399 are set; written at $12A5.
unpack_figure_sprite: the figure number being rebuilt (X is used for other things meanwhile).
Where each figure's frames start in figure_frames, by figure: body 0, dog $76, figure 2 $B1, figure 3 $B1 (the same set), head $92.
Added to the head's graphic number for the mood $035F (its frames below $18): 0, $0F, $1E. The three faces are three runs of graphics, $8A-$98, $99-$A7 and $A8-$B6.

Each figure's current sprite block (VIC bank 1, address $4000 + 64 x block): body $24, dog $2A, figure 2 $21, figure 3 $20, head $26 in the image; unpack_figure_sprite flips it by EOR 8 before each rebuild (double buffering, so $24 alternates with $2C). The outline built for figures 0, 1 and 4 goes in the next block.
The head's (figure 4's) entry of figure_sprite_block: read at $116B to make the person's second and fourth sprites (the head's colour sprite, and its outline at +1).
Low bytes of the address each figure's colour is loaded from (self-modified LDA at $0FA8): $1393 body, $042D dog, $1394 figure 2, $1395 figure 3, $042E head.
High bytes of the figure colour addresses, paired with figure_colour_src_lo: $13, $04, $13, $13, $04.

Frame table: the graphic number for each figure frame, indexed by frame + figure_frame_base. Graphic n's packed image is found through the word at $E453 + 2n. $0D77-$0DEC: the person's body, 118 entries (graphics 0-$61); entries $5D-$75 are the frames 0-$18 used instead while $0391 is set.
Frame table, the dog's part: frames 0-$1B. Frames 0-3 and 5-$18 repeat graphics $62-$65 in turn, frame 4 is $66 and frames $19-$1B are $67-$69.

Frame table, the head's part (figure 4; decoded, frame 0 is a face and frame 4 the back of the hair): frames 0-$17 are three rows of eight directions (graphics $8A-$98; directions 1-3 use the graphics of 7-5, drawn mirrored because $ACF3 sets the head's facing flag $039E for them) and get the mood offset; frames $18-$1E are graphics $83-$89 without it.
Frame table, the part shared by figures 2 and 3: frames 0-$18, graphics $6A-$82, one each.

Builds the sprite image of figure X (0 the person's body, 1 the dog, 2 and 3 objects, 4 the person's head) for its frame $038B,x. The frame table index is the frame plus figure_frame_base,x; for the body, frames below $19 get +$5D (and $21 becomes $0D) while $0391 is set; for the head, frames below $18 (table index below $AA) have head_mood_offsets[$035F] (0, $0F or $1E) added to the graphic number. The frame table gives a graphic number; the graphic's packed data is found through the offset table at $E453 (stored offset - $5000 + $E453). The figure's sprite block ($0D68,x) is flipped between two buffers (EOR 8) and the data unpacked into $4000 + 64 * block: a count byte with bit 7 set copies (n AND $7F) * 3 literal bytes, otherwise the next three bytes are repeated n times, until 61 bytes are written. If the facing flag $039A,x is set each row is mirrored (s_135F, left and right bytes swapped) and, for the body and the head, moved one multicolour pixel. Then columns are clipped off by s_13AC when $0381,x is set, the figure's colour is stored in $0386,x through the self-modified LDA at $0FA8, and for figures 0, 1 and 4 the hires outline sprite is built in the next block by s_12B7.
unpack_figure_sprite: index into the packed graphic data at ($18). Two data bytes inside the code (the BEQ at $0EE8 always skips them).
unpack_figure_sprite: number of sprite bytes written so far at ($1A); unpacking stops at 61 ($3D).

unpack_figure_sprite continued: a count byte below $80 repeats the next three bytes ($1C, $1D, $1E) as that many sprite rows. From $0F1F the finished image is mirrored when the figure's facing flag $039A,x is set: each 3-byte row has its bytes swapped end for end and each byte's 2-bit pixels reversed (s_135F); for the body and the head (figures 0 and 4) the mirrored row is also shifted left one multicolour pixel.
Byte counter for s_13AC, the column clip at $13AC: counts down the three bytes of each sprite row while it ANDs them with the clip masks from $13EF.

unpack_figure_sprite, last part: clips columns off the image with s_13AC when $0381,x is non-zero, loads the figure's colour through the self-modified LDA at $0FA8 into $0386,x, and for figures 0, 1 and 4 points $18/$19 at the new image and $1A/$1B 64 bytes on and calls s_12B7 to build the hires outline sprite (X kept in $1390).

records.s: Self-modified: the operand of this LDA is set by the two stores above from figure_colour_src_lo/hi ($0D6D/$0D72), so it loads the colour of figure X: $1393 body, $042D dog, $1394 and $1395 figures 2 and 3, $042E head. The result goes to $0386,x.

records.c: Operand low byte of the LDA at $0FA8, rewritten per figure from $0D6D,x.
Operand high byte of the LDA at $0FA8, rewritten per figure from $0D72,x.

Main-loop stage 1 (and five times at cold start). Looks from figure 4 down to 0 for one whose flags $03C4,x have bit 1 (new frame) set and rebuilds only that one: for the body (X=0) first takes the head's offsets $135D/$135E from the tables $1437/$1494 by frame; clears bit 1 and sets bit 2; reads the frame's Y offset from the figure's table (pointer from $12AD/$12B2) into $03B7,x, setting bit 0 when it changed; then unpack_figure_sprite. It continues past $1000: sorts figures 0-3 on $03B3 to share out the eight hardware sprites (four for the person, two for the dog, one each for figures 2 and 3, the front one getting the lowest numbers), refreshes the shadow registers $0D3A-$0D5D for figures that changed, waits for raster line $FA and copies them to the VIC.

Not an instruction: the operand byte of the STA $19 at $0FFF. The sprite frame routine at $0FD2 (main loop stage 1, $0939; also called by the cold start at $04DB) crosses into this range here, and this label only marks the boundary. The code resumes at sprite_pose_offset ($1001).

Continuation of the sprite frame routine ($0FD2), inside its loop over figures 4 down to 0, for the first one whose pose or facing changed (bit 1 of $03C4,x; $0FED has already swapped it for bit 2). Reads the figure's per-pose Y offset from its table (pose_yoff_lo/pose_yoff_hi, index = pose $038B,x) into $03B7,x, setting bit 0 of $03C4,x when it changed; then rebuilds the figure's sprite image ($0E41) and goes to sprite_depth_sort, so only one image is rebuilt per pass. When no figure needs one, the loop ($101C) runs out into the sort. Figures: 0 = the person's lower body, 1 = the dog, 2 and 3 = one-sprite objects, 4 = the person's upper body.

Gives figures 0-3 their hardware sprites by depth. Key = depth $03B3,x times 8 plus a fixed tie-break $03D2,x (1-4); a selection sort puts the order in $03D6. Sprite numbers are then dealt from 0 upward, nearest figure (smallest key) first, so nearer figures get lower-numbered sprites, which the VIC draws in front: the person takes four (lower body, upper body and their two outlines), the dog two, figures 2 and 3 one each, eight in all. A figure whose number changed gets it in $03CD,x, bit 0 of $03C4,x set, and its X high bit, kept as that sprite's bit in $03AB,x, moved to the new bit ($03E3,y).

Once figure 4's new image is built (bit 2 of $03C8) keeps only its bit 7 and sets bit 0 of $03C4, so the person is repositioned. Then for figures 3 down to 0 with bit 0 or bit 2 of $03C4,x set (both cleared) writes the shadow registers at the figure's sprite number n = $03CD,x: Y = floor line $03AF,x - depth $03B3,x - pose offset $03B7,x, X = $03A7,x, pointer $0D68,x, colour $0386,x. Figures 0 and 1 also get sprite n+1 at the same place showing the next sprite block (the outline) in colour 0, black. For the person n+1 and n+3 are the upper body (pointer $0D6C, colour $038A) and its outline, placed person_upper_dy lines higher and person_upper_dx pixels across; n+2 is the lower body's outline.
Sprite bit masks %0101 shifted left 0-5 times (6 bytes, $119F-$11A4): entry n selects sprites n and n+2, the person's lower body and its outline when his first sprite is n (read at $11DA).
mask_person_lower read one entry on: entry n = %1010 shifted left n times, sprites n+1 and n+3, the person's upper body and its outline (read at $11CF when bit 7 of $03C8 is set).
%1111 shifted left 0-4 times: all four of the person's sprites from sprite n; used for his behind-background bits ($0396, at $11E8) and his X high bits ($03AB, at $11F3).
%11 shifted left 0-4 times: the person's two colour sprites (n and n+1), the ones switched to multicolour; the outlines stay hires (read at $11F9).
%11 shifted left 0-6 times: the dog's two sprites (n and n+1), for its enable bits, its behind-background bits ($0397) and its X high bits ($03AC) (read at $1207, $1215, $1223).

End of the sprite frame: builds the enable ($0D3A), multicolour ($0D3B), X high bit ($0D4C) and behind-background ($0D5D) masks. Person: lower pair if bit 7 of $03C4, upper pair if bit 7 of $03C8, all four behind the background if $0396, X high bits from $03AB, multicolour on the two colour sprites. Dog: its pair if bit 7 of $03C5, with $0397 and $03AC, multicolour on the first. Figures 2 and 3: if bit 7 of $03C6/$03C7, multicolour if $0394/$0395, X high bit $03AD/$03AE, behind background if $0398/$0399. Then waits for raster line $FA and, with interrupts off, copies the shadows to $D000-$D010, the pointers $5FF8-$5FFF, the colours $D027-$D02E, $D015, $D01C and $D01B. The STX $1387 at entry stores $FF where nothing reads it before it is rewritten.

records.s: VIC sprite X/Y registers $D000-$D010 (I/O is in here)

records.c: Split lo/hi pointer table, one entry per figure 0-4 (lo bytes here, hi bytes at pose_yoff_hi): each figure's table of per-pose Y offsets, read at $0FF7/$0FFC. Figure 0 -> $14F1 (person), 1 -> $154E (dog), 2 and 3 -> $156C (objects), 4 -> $156A (two bytes before the objects' table; figure 4's offset is computed but its sprites are placed from the person's).
High bytes of the five pose_yoff_lo pointers ($14, $15, $15, $15, $15).

Builds the black outline sprite that sits behind a colour sprite: ($18) = the colour image just built, ($1A) = the next 64-byte block. Called for figures 0, 1 and 4 from $0FCB after a rebuild, and by compose_from_parts ($15FB). Works up the 21 rows from the bottom: each source row has every non-empty two-bit pixel turned to %11 (outline_fetch_row), the row is ORed with itself shifted one pixel left and right ($03EF-$03F1) and with the rows above and below, so the outline is the figure's silhouette grown by one hires pixel left, right, up and down.

For build_outline: fetches the next source row upward, the three bytes before index outline_src_idx in ($18) (zero once the index is below 0), with every non-empty two-bit pixel made %11, into $1387-$1389; updates outline_src_idx.
