How many lines the person's upper-body sprites sit above the lower-body ones: set per pose from person_upper_dy_by_pose at $0FE4, subtracted at $1119. $15 (21, one sprite height) for most poses.

Horizontal offset of the person's upper-body sprites from the lower-body ones, in pixels: set per pose from person_upper_dx_by_pose at $0FEA, added to the X low byte at $113C (without carrying into the X high bit). 0 for most poses.

Returns A with its four two-bit pixels in reverse order, a multicolour sprite byte mirrored (A = 0 returns at once). X is kept in mirror_save_x. The image decoder calls it at $0F31-$0F40 to mirror a figure's image when it faces left ($039A,x non-zero).
mirror_mc_byte keeps the caller's X here.
mirror_mc_byte's work copy of its input, which it rotates the pixels out of.
mirror_mc_byte assembles the mirrored byte here and returns it.

Scratch for the sprite routines: build_outline's current (upper) source row, three bytes with $1388-$1389, cleared at $12BB and filled by outline_fetch_row; clip_sprite's mask offset; the image decoder's count times three ($0ECC-$0ED1); sprite_write_vic stores X ($FF) in it.
build_outline: the row being written (three bytes, $138A-$138C), one below the current source row; its shifted copies are ORed together into $03EF-$03F1.
Second byte of outline_row_mid, read on its own at $12EB-$1306 while the row is shifted.
Third byte of outline_row_mid, read at $12F5 and $12F9.
build_outline: the row below outline_row_mid (three bytes, $138D-$138F), ORed into the output unshifted.
The image decoder keeps the figure number here across build_outline ($0FC8, $0FCE).
build_outline's source index into ($18): starts at 63 and drops three per row; below 0 the fetched row is empty.
build_outline's destination index into ($1A): starts at 62 and drops three per row; the loop ends when it goes negative.

Colour of the person's lower-body sprite. $0FA8 copies it into $0386 whenever figure 0's image is rebuilt, through the pointer $0D6D/$0D72 (the LDA there is self-modified). Chosen together with $D025 from the table at $BA0E ($B9CC) or at $BA2E ($BA02); $0D, light green, in the loaded image and the snapshots.

Colour of figure 2, the first one-sprite object (a carried item, the shower's water, an item by the front door...): copied into $0388 when its image is rebuilt. Set by the activities that show it, e.g. $1F60 (3, cyan water), $28FC (per carried object, from $2A5A), $AFBB (9).
Colour of figure 3, the second one-sprite object: copied into $0389 when its image is rebuilt. Only $538A writes it.
Sets ($1A) to the address of the 64-byte block that sprite pointer $0D68,x names: $4000 + pointer x 64 (VIC bank 1).
clip_sprite keeps the caller's X here.
clip_sprite's argument: bits 0-6 = how many two-bit pixels to hide (1-12), bit 7 set = hide them on the left instead of the right.

Hides a vertical strip at one side of a figure's image: A = the figure's clip value ($0381,x; called from $0F99 once the image is built, not at all when 0), ($1A) = the image. Every row is ANDed with the same three-byte mask from clip_masks, entry n - 1 for n = A AND $7F, from the second half when bit 7 is set: values 1-12 clear that many two-bit pixels from the right, or from the left with bit 7. Row counter in $0F93. $32E4-$3354 sets and steps the person's values ($0381 and $0385) as he moves.
clip_sprite's row masks, three bytes each: entries 0-11 (here) keep the left 11, 10 ... 0 two-bit pixels, clearing the right end; entries 12-23 at clip_masks_left keep the right end instead.
clip_masks entries 12-23 (bit 7 of the clip value): keep the right 11, 10 ... 0 two-bit pixels, clearing the left end.

One byte per pose of the person, $00-$3F here and $40-$5C at $1477 (93 poses): lines between his lower and upper sprites, copied to person_upper_dy at $0FE1. $15 for most poses; $12 for $1A-$1D, $23-$29 and $3B; $11 for $1E-$20 and $2A; $14 for $33.
person_upper_dy_by_pose for poses $40-$5C: $05 for $40-$44 (the bath poses: the upper body only five lines up), $13 for $45-$46, $14 for $4F, $52, $53, $58, $5A, otherwise $15.
One byte per pose of the person, $00-$3F here and $40-$5C at $14D4: horizontal shift of his upper body, copied to person_upper_dx at $0FE7. 0 except $06 for poses $2F and $30 and $FF (-1) for $32.
person_upper_dx_by_pose for poses $40-$5C: all 0.

Per-pose Y offset of figure 0, the person's lower body (93 bytes, poses $00-$5C, signed), subtracted from the sprite's Y: -2 draws it two lines lower. The walking poses 0-7 go -2, -3, -2, -1 twice, a bob in step; the bath poses $40-$44 are +$0B, 11 lines higher.
Per-pose Y offset of the dog (figure 1), poses $00-$1B: all 0.

Where pose_yoff_lo points for figure 4 (the person's upper body): two zero bytes, then the objects' table. The offset read through it only sets bit 0 of $03C8, which nothing tests; the upper body is placed from the person's position.
Per-pose Y offset of the one-sprite objects (figures 2 and 3), poses $00-$18, signed: $F0 for pose 0, $0A for the water drops $0B-$0D, $02 for $0E-$10, and others.

Builds the person's lower-body image from three part images instead of a stored pose: swaps his sprite buffer ($0D68 EOR 8), points the store below at the new block (self-modified operand $15D2/$15D3, from sprite_addr) and fills it: rows 0-9 take their left byte from ($18) and the other two from ($1A), rows 10-20 from ($1C) and ($1E). The four pointers are sprite_parts plus the offsets at $E41D-$E420 ($00, $40 or $80: part 0, 1 or 2), so the left and right halves of the top and of the bottom change separately. Then $03C4 = $81 (shown, repositioned) and on to build_outline. Only caller: the JMP at $E450 in activity 79 (which walks to location 6, at the piano in the picture, and silences the sound and sets $3563 at $E3F1), when $E421 is set; $3665-$36AE set the offsets from the music player's flags $B013-$B016.

The STA abs,Y of compose_from_parts's copy loop. Its operand ($15D2/$15D3) is rewritten at $1594/$1599 with the new sprite block's address, so the bytes land in the person's sprite, not here; the JMPs at $1600, $1608 and $160D return to it with the next byte.
Low byte of compose_store's operand: the target sprite block, written at $1594 from ($1A).
High byte of compose_store's operand, written at $1599 from ($1B).

Three multicolour sprite images used as parts by compose_from_parts (not addressed directly: it loads #$10/#$16): part 0 at $1610 (no hands showing), part 1 at $1650 (hands, colour %11, out at both sides; its legs a row higher), part 2 at $1690, of which only rows 0-9 (30 bytes) exist, since the next byte is code: the other hand positions. The code at $3665-$36AE only ever picks parts 0 or 1 for the bottom rows.

Copies location X's floor line, X/2 and depth (location_y, location_x, location_depth) into entry 54, the location activities adjust and walk to. Callers: $8EF9 and $A853 (which then make 54 the person's target), $2FE8, $33E7, $390D, $95BC, $A887, $AF9B, $E026.

Per figure (0 person, 1 dog, 2): the value $039A,x takes when the figure faces left (8, 4, 1); turning EORs it in. It is also the pose the person (8) and the dog (4) take when they arrive (state 6, $18D3). The third byte is never read: only figures 0 and 1 walk.

Moves figure X (0 the person, main loop $09BB; 1 the dog, $09C5) one step of its movement state machine. Waits while the figure's last change is not on screen yet (bits 0-1 of $03C4,x). Otherwise increments its pass counter $02DD,x, puts the floor of its floor line in $02D4 (floor_of_y: 0-2, $80 on the stairs), stirs the random generator, refreshes X/2 ($03A3,x) unless idle, and switches on the state $03BC,x through move_states: 0 idle, 1 the dog between walks, 2 and 5 choose the route, 3 walk to the stairs, 4 climb, 6 walk to the target location $03C0,x.

move_figure's switch table (handler address minus one), by state: 0 $1701 mstate_idle, 1 $173C mstate_dog, 2 $1844 mstate_route, 3 $185B mstate_to_stairs, 4 $18A9 mstate_stairs, 5 $1844 mstate_route again after a flight, 6 $18CB mstate_to_target.

Per figure: state 1's countdown before the dog picks its next destination, decremented every eighth pass at $1797. Only the dog's byte (dog_wander_wait, $1700) is used: $16FF, the person's, is never read because the person never enters state 1.

The dog's wait before its next walk (wander_wait + 1): set at $17C2 to 3, 7, 11 or 15 from the random byte, or $E3-$EF for destinations 0-8 when $037B is 0, to $40 when it goes to eat ($17F3), and to $FF by the phase handler at $28CD. At $10 or more the dog rests in pose $19 ($174D).

Movement state 0, idle. Sets the figure's speed $039F,x to 1 (a step every second pass), or to 2 (every fourth) for the person when $037B is $7B or $0365 is non-zero ($0365 is non-zero while he is sick: $0B4F then makes the skin colour $D026 green), and restarts the step timer. The person then stays idle until an activity sets state 2 ($AB63 and others); the dog goes straight on to state 1.
Advances figure X to its next movement state ($03BC,x + 1) and restarts its step timer (mstate_reset_timer).

Restarts figure X's step timer $02DD,x as the complement of its speed mask, so the next step is a full period away; for the dog, when the person's timer is 0, its timer is set to 2 instead. Also entered at $1733 (from $1A54).

Movement state 1, the dog between walks. On every pass while it eats (dog_eating non-zero), dog_eat_timer counts down, each underflow takes one unit of food from the bowl ($2A62) and redraws it (draw_bowl), and a pose from dog_eat_poses is shown every fourth count. On every eighth pass it counts dog_wander_wait down, except while $037B is $7B or $7C; at 0 it stops eating and picks a random entry 0-20 of dog_destinations, drawn again if it is on the top floor (below 16) while $0711 is non-zero or the activity ($8D9B) is $7E or more; with $037B non-zero it goes to 46, the front door, instead. Sets the new wait, the target $03C1 and state 2. Going to 32, its bowl, with food in it starts eating on arrival.
Non-zero while the dog eats: set at $17EE (to the bowl level $2A62) when it heads for location 32 with food in the bowl; cleared at $179C when its wait runs out.
Counts down every pass while the dog eats; on underflow one unit of food goes and it restarts at a random 0-63. When its two low bits are 0, the value / 4 picks the pose from dog_eat_poses.
Dog poses while eating, by dog_eat_timer / 4 (0-15): $1B (head down) for 0-3, then $04 (standing) and $1A alternating. The 17th byte, $180B, is never reached.

The 21 locations the dog wanders to, by a random index 0-20 (random values 21-31 are folded to 5-15): 11, 15, 16, 31, 27, 32, 42, 45, 47, 32, 20, 21, 26, 29, 46, 32, 46, 32, 1, 12, 46. 32 is its bowl, 46 inside the front door. Indexes 0-8 get the long wait ($E3-$EF) unless $037B is non-zero.

Redraws the dog's bowl for the food level $2A62 (0-6): lines 3 and 4 of the bitmap cell at row 23, column 1 ($7CCB, $7CCC) from bowl_line3/bowl_line4, and that cell's colour RAM ($DB99) set to 0, black, the colour of its %11 pixels: the fuller the bowl, the more black pixels. Called when the dog eats ($176B) and after $2A63 fills the bowl to 6.
Bitmap line 3 of the bowl cell for food levels 0-6: $AA, $AA, $AA, $BA, $BA, $BE, $BE (each %11 pair is a black pixel).
Bitmap line 4 of the bowl cell for food levels 0-6: $AA, $EA, $FA, $FA, $FE, $FE, $FF.
Movement states 2 and 5: if the target location ($03C0,x) has the figure's floor line ($03AF,x), goes to state 6 (walk to it); otherwise to state 3 (walk to the stairs).

Movement state 3: walks (walk_step) to the stair end that leads toward the target's floor. On arrival stores the direction in $02E1,x (bit 7 set = going down, set_stair_state), passes the floor being left to $E3C1 (the person only; an RTS in this build), faces the figure for the first part of the flight ($039A,x = 8, or 0 when going down from the middle floor), zeroes the step count $02DF,x and moves to state 4.

Movement state 4, on the stairs: acts at half the walking rate (mask x 2 + 1), keeps floor x 2 in $02D5,x while the figure is still on a floor line, flags a reposition and takes one step (stair_step).
Movement state 6: walks to the target location; on arrival takes the standing pose figure_face_left,x (8 the person, 4 the dog), state 0, and restarts the step timer.
Steps figure X one pixel left (move_left) if its speed mask allows it this pass, and sets bit 0 of $03C4,x.
Steps figure X one pixel right (move_right) if its speed mask allows it this pass, and sets bit 0 of $03C4,x.

Moves figure X one pixel right: faces it right (set_facing with 0), increments $03A7,x and on overflow flips its X high bit ($03AB,x, the bit of its sprite from $03E3), refreshes X/2 (calc_half_x) and returns A = 1.
Sets figure X's facing $039A,x to A (0 right, non-zero left); if it changed, sets bit 1 of $03C4,x so the image is rebuilt (mirrored when facing left).
Moves figure X one pixel left: faces it left (figure_face_left), decrements $03A7,x and on underflow flips its X high bit, refreshes X/2 and returns A = 1.
Loads X with the figure being moved ($02D7) and returns speed_masks[$039F,x]: the figure acts only on passes where its counter $02DD,x AND this mask is 0.
Step masks by speed index 0-7: 0, 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 63 (every pass, one pass in 2, in 4 ...). Walking uses index 1 or 2 (mstate_idle); the stairs use the mask doubled plus one.

The random number generator, also the second entry of the jump table ($0343). State $0414-$0417; in the crack-screen snapshot, where the crack's own screen occupies $0400, this page is parked at $4C00 with "Zeke" at $4C14 (the later snapshots have "Billy Bob Binkle" back at $03FC). Increments $0417; while that is negative, first adds the caller's A and carry into $0415; then $0414 = ((($0414 rotated left) + $C3) EOR $0414) + $0417, $0415 = old $0415 EOR ($0415 shifted left with $0414's top bit), and returns the new $0414 in A (X, Y kept). No fixed period, since the callers' A goes in. 68 JSRs plus the jump table (used by $C074) mask the result for random choices (waits, destinations, poses); move_figure calls it every pass for both figures, and many routines read $0414 directly as the last value.

Unreferenced: nothing calls, jumps or branches to $198E, and no pointer to it is stored anywhere in RAM (no $198E word; the only $198D words are inside STA $D019 instructions). Saves A in $02D8 and converts its high nibble with hex_digit, then increments X and converts the low nibble; nothing stores the first digit, which is lost.
Returns the hex digit for A (0-15): $30-$39 for 0-9 and $01-$06 for 10-15, the screen codes of A-F rather than ASCII. Only hex_digits_unused calls it.

One walking step for figure X toward its target location ($03C0,x), or toward the stair end on its floor when the target is on another floor (location 48 + 2 x floor going up, 49 + 2 x floor going down). Returns A = 0 (Z set) when there (depth and location_x_of both match), non-zero otherwise, including on the passes its speed skips. From 15 half-pixels away or more it alternates X steps with steps toward depth 5 ($02DC toggles); nearer, it steps along whichever of X and depth is further off. To reverse it first turns: pose $11 (facing out) for a step, then pose 0 facing the new way, unless turning alone would carry its reference point past the target ($1A23). Work bytes $02E5-$02E8.

Sets figure X's pose $038B,x to A; if it changed, sets bit 1 of $03C4,x so the sprite frame routine rebuilds the image. For the person (X = 0) it also takes a direction 0-7 for the pose from the table at $AE8D (as (8 - d) AND 7 when he faces right, unless d is 0 or 4) into $0390, and when that differs from the low bits of $03F4 (the pose $ACF3 turns figure 4, the upper body, towards) puts it there and sets $037C = 1.

One step on the stairs for figure X: $02DF,x counts the steps of the current part of the flight (every fourth step the low bits of $02E1,x count too, which nothing reads). Part = bits 7-6 of $02E1,x: 0 up first, 1 up second, 2 down first, 3 down second, with 28, 27, 26, 25 steps (stair_part_steps). After a first part it keeps the screen Y but takes the depth of the stair end on the arrival floor, sets the facing for the second part, nudges X and Y (stair_land_dx/dy) and sets bit 6. After a second part it puts the figure exactly on the arrival stair end (49 + 2 x floor going up, 48 + 2 x floor going down; the middle floor when the target is two floors away), passes the new floor to $E3C2 (the person only; an RTS in this build) and moves to state 5. Otherwise it animates the step (stair_anim).

Animates one stair step: index = part x 8 + (step AND 7) into four 32-entry tables: stair_poses (the pose, via figure_set_pose), stair_face (only in parts 0 and 3, the parts with no sideways movement: 1 = mirrored), stair_dx (X change, negated when facing left) and stair_dy (Y change).
Stores A in $02E1,x (the stair direction and part) and sets bit 0 of $03C4,x (reposition).
Pose for each stair step, 8 per part: up first $0D $0E $0F $0E, up second $09-$0C, down first $11-$14, down second $15 $16 $17 $16 (each pattern twice).
Facing per stair step, used in parts 0 and 3 only: 1 (face left, mirrored) on steps 5-7 of each 8, else 0; the part 1 and part 2 entries are 0 and unused.
X change per stair step, before negation for a left-facing figure: 0 in parts 0 and 3, 2 on three steps in four in parts 1 and 2 (the sideways run of the flight).
Y change per stair step, signed: part 0 -2 on half the steps, part 1 -1 or -2, part 2 +1 or +2, part 3 +2 on half the steps (8 lines per 8 steps in each part).
Steps in each part of a flight: 28, 27 (up), 26, 25 (down).
X nudge between the two parts of a flight, read at index 0 going up (0) or 2 going down (8, negated on the upper staircase); index 1 and 3 belong to stair_land_dy.
Y nudge between the two parts of a flight: +1 going up (index 0), -1 going down (index 2).
Floor number for floor line A, in Y: 0 for $65 (top floor), 1 for $A5 (middle floor), 2 for $E5 (ground floor), $80 for anything else (on the stairs).

The 55 locations figures walk to, table 1 of 3 (location_x and location_depth have the same index): the floor line, a sprite Y. $65 top floor (0-15), $A5 middle floor (16-31), $E5 ground floor (32-47). 48-53 are stair ends: 48 + 2 x floor where the stairs up start, 49 + 2 x floor where the stairs down start (48 and 53 are dummies). 54 is a scratch entry that set_custom_location and the activities fill. 32 is the dog's bowl, 46 inside the front door, 6 at the piano. Also read by index at $2DE4-$2DF4.
location_y entry 46, the spot inside the front door; $AFBE reads it directly to put figure 2 (pose 9, colour 9) there. Entries 47-53 follow.
location_y entry 54, the scratch location: written by set_custom_location, $3239, $3261, $328C and $8F77, read at $9004.
Table 2 of 3: each location's X in half pixels (sprite X / 2). walk_step and at_target compare it with the figure's $03A3,x as location_x_of adjusts it.
location_x entry 46 (inside the front door); $AFC9 reads it directly and places figure 2 13 half-pixels to its right.
location_x entry 54, the scratch location: activities copy a location in and shift it, e.g. +$14 at $E02F, +4 at $30DF, +9 at $AFA9.
Table 3 of 3: each location's depth into the room, 2-15. A figure's sprite is drawn that many lines higher, and nearer figures (lower depth) get the front sprites.
location_depth entry 54, the scratch location: written by set_custom_location, $327E, $3292, $3362 and $8F71, read at $8FFE.
Walking animation mask per figure: 7 for the person (poses 0-7), 3 for the dog (poses 0-3).

Sets figure X's walking pose from its pass counter: ($02DD,x shifted right speed + 1 times) AND walk_frame_mask,x, so the frame advances once per step. For the person the code after figure_set_pose tests $02E3/$02E4, but both of its exits return with X = 0: it has no effect.

Is figure X at its target location $03C0,x? Refreshes X/2 (calc_half_x) and returns Z set when X/2 (as location_x_of adjusts it), floor line and depth all match. The activities call it before starting a walk ($AB68, $2FF2, $391C, $E039).

Returns figure X's X/2 ($03A3,x) as compared with the X of location Y: for the person going to an ordinary location (Y below 48) minus 1 when he faces right or minus 11 when he faces left, as his reference point depends on his facing; unchanged for the dog and the stair ends. Y is kept (via $02E9).
Sets $03A3,x to figure X's X position halved: the 9-bit X ($03A7,x, with the high bit when $03AB,x is non-zero) shifted right once.
Pass counter for the phase handler wait_8_passes: counted up there, the phase ends when its low three bits come round to 0.

Activity 47 ($2F; entry 47 of the activity table at $8DC9): switches on the phase $4C through activity_47_phases. All its handlers are outside this range: $30CD (walk to location 37, just right of the refrigerator in the picture), $8FA7 (wait to arrive), $9469, $94CC, $AF58, $2136 (pose $21), $2156, then the common end $8F0E. What the player sees is not established here.
activity_47's phase table (handler address minus one): $30CD, $8FA7, $9469, $94CC, $AF58, $2136, $2156, $8F0E.

Activity 48 ($30): switches on the phase $4C through activity_48_phases. As the code reads, the person cooks: walks to location 37, just right of the refrigerator ($30CD), waits to arrive ($8FA7), picks up object 3, a small yellow pot (take_object), walks to location 34 at the stove ($A833), carries it ($293D), sets it on the stove (put_on_stove, drawn into the picture), faces the room in pose $19, waits eight passes and lights the burner (stove_on), then the common end $8F0E.
activity_48's phase table (handler address minus one): $30CD, $8FA7, take_object, $A833, $293D, put_on_stove, pose_19, wait_8_passes, stove_on, $8F0E.

Activity 49 ($31): switches on the phase $4C through activity_49_phases. The other half of cooking: walks to location 34 at the stove ($A833), waits ($8FA7), pose $19, waits eight passes, turns the burner off (stove_off), takes the pot off the stove (take_object, which also clears it from the picture), walks to location 36 at the sink ($A83D), carries it ($293D), puts it away (drop_object), then the common end $8F0E.
activity_49's phase table (handler address minus one): $A833, $8FA7, pose_19, wait_8_passes, stove_off, take_object, $A83D, $293D, drop_object, $8F0E.
Phase handler (activity 49): puts the carried object away: $0391 = 0 (the person's lower body goes back to its normal images) and figure 2 hidden ($03C6 = 0); next phase.

Phase handler (activities 48 and 49): the person takes object 3: $2783 = 3 and $28F0 give figure 2 that object's pose and colour ($2A4A/$2A5A: pose $12, yellow) and set $0391 (carrying); the DEC $4C undoes the phase step $28F0 makes. Then clears the pot from the stove in the picture (stove_patch with zeros) and moves to the next phase.

Draws or clears the pot on the stove in the house bitmap: X to $7A48, A to $7A49-$7A4C, Y to $7A51 (cell row 21, column 1, lines 0-4, and line 1 of column 2: the top of the stove at the left of the kitchen), colour $7F (yellow on light grey) to the colour-matrix cells $5F49/$5F4A; next phase.
Phase handler (activity 48): puts the carried pot down: $0391 = 0, figure 2 hidden, and the pot drawn on the stove (stove_patch with $14, $55 and $50).
Phase handler (activities 48 and 49): the person takes pose $19 (facing out of the screen, arms out); next phase.
Phase handler (activities 48 and 49): counts wait8_count and moves to the next phase once every eight passes.

Phase handler (activity 48): $357A = 1 (one of the sound flags $355C-$357B that $3713 clears; no reader of this one was found) and $2B52 = 1, the burner lit: $2CD9 then sets line 6 of the stove cell to $EA and flickers its colour RAM ($DB49) through yellow, blue, orange and white; next phase.
Phase handler (activity 49): $357B = $FF (another of the sound flags, no reader found) and $2B52 = 0, the burner off (line 6 of the stove cell back to $2A); next phase.
Pass counter of the shower (activities 84 and 102), counted every pass by shower_run: every eighth pass counts shower_time down, and its low bits time the water frames ($20ED) and the steps.

Shows the delivered food by the front door: set_carried_item ($AFB8) with frame 8 and colour 7 places figure 2, the item sprite, at location $2E ($1D64, $1D9B), makes it visible ($03C6 = $83) and advances the phase. Activity 44 phases 6 and 24.
Working copy of cupboard_food for draw_cupboard, shifted right one bit per place.
Activity 43 phase 0: from a random start (random routine $195E) tries the four places in turn for one whose cupboard_food bit is set, stores it in cupboard_slot (0 when none is) and advances.
Activity 43 phase 7: flips the bit of cupboard_slot in cupboard_food (clearing it: the place was chosen full), redraws the cupboard and advances.
Activity 44 phases 10 and 13: like act43_pick_full_place, but finds a place whose bit is clear (0 when none is), stores it in cupboard_slot and advances.
Activity 44 phase 20: clears $0391, sets the bit of cupboard_slot in cupboard_food, redraws the cupboard and advances.

Draws the food on the kitchen cupboard shelves from cupboard_food: for each place (X from 3 down, bit 0 first) writes five bitmap bytes at the address from cupboard_addr_lo/hi, which it patches into the STA at $31B8: cupboard_item_gfx when the bit is set, zeros when not. The places are char cells (6,19), (7,19), (6,20) and (7,20), the open shelves right of the fridge.
Low byte of the STA $6000,Y operand at $31B8, rewritten by draw_cupboard for each place.
High byte of that STA operand; draw_cupboard's inner and outer loop ends follow.
Bitmap address, low bytes, of the four cupboard places: $F0, $F8, $30, $38.
High bytes of those addresses: $77, $77, $79, $79 ($77F0, $77F8, $7930, $7938).
The food item's five bitmap rows, top first: $15 $00 $15 $15 $15 (multicolour pixels of colour 01, one blank row).
Bit of each cupboard place in cupboard_food: $08, $04, $02, $01.
Activity 81 phase 3: $68 = $10 (doorway_script sequence C) and next phase.
Activity 86 phase 0: $68 = $19 (doorway_script sequence D) and next phase.
Activity 7 phase 4 and activity 97 phase 0: $68 = 0 (doorway_script sequence A) and next phase.
Activity 7 phase 14 and activity 100 phase 0: $68 = 9 (doorway_script sequence B); the four set_doorway entries share this STA $68 and JMP $8F0B.

One step of a walk through a doorway, in which the person vanishes or reappears a column at a time: switch_68 through doorway_table. Sequence A ($68 = 0): a small step, then he walks 12 half-X units (24 pixels) right while his image is clipped from the right one more column per unit (fig_clip $0381 and the head's $0385, 1 to 12), and a pause of about 64 passes; B (9): he walks 12 back left while the clip shrinks to 0, then steps back. C ($10) and D ($19) do the same leftwards, clipping from the left (bit 7). The handlers step $68 themselves; the $8F0B that ends a sequence advances the calling activity's phase. Used by activities 7 (the fire, parser rules $C98A and $C99A: A, later B), 81 (C), 86 (D), 97 (A) and 100 (B).

doorway_script's 32 words (handler minus one), four sequences each ending with $8F0B. A from 0: dw_step_a, walk_sub_take_requests ($95ED), dw_clip_right, dw_walk, dw_clip_grow, dw_pause_start, dw_pause_wait, dw_nop. B from 9: dw_show, dw_walk, dw_clip_shrink, dw_clip_off, dw_step_a, $95ED. C from $10: dw_step_c, $95ED, dw_clip_left, dw_walk, dw_clip_grow, dw_pause_start, dw_pause_wait, dw_nop. D from $19: dw_show, dw_walk_right, dw_clip_shrink, dw_clip_off, dw_step_c, $95ED.
Sequence C: fig_clip $0381 and the head's $0385 = $81, one column clipped from the left; next step.

Sequences C and D: destination floor line = the person's ($03AF to $1D6C) and dw_last_x = 0; at step $10 the same X/2 with depth + 3, otherwise X/2 + 3 with depth - 3 (fig_depth $03B3); then the shared tail of dw_step_a makes it his destination.
Sequence D: dw_walk with $68 forced to 3, so the destination is X/2 + 12 rather than - 12; restores $68 and goes to the next step.

Sequences A and B: destination = the person's place ($03AF, $03A3, $03B3 into the scratch location $1D6C, $1DA3, $1DDA) with X/2 and depth + 3 at step 0 and - 3 otherwise; destination $36 through set_person_destination ($AB63) and next step. $3272 onwards is shared with dw_step_c, and $3286 (INC $68) is every handler's 'next step'.

Sequences A-D: destination at the person's floor line and depth, X/2 + 12 when $68 is 3 and - 12 otherwise; remembers the starting X/2 in dw_last_x, sets destination $36 (the scratch location) and next step.
Sequences A and C: dw_pause = 8, next step.
Pass counter of dw_pause_wait: the pause counts down once every 8 passes.
Pause left in dw_pause_wait, in units of 8 passes (8 at the start, so 64 passes).
Sequences A and C: waits dw_pause x 8 passes, or goes on at once when a request is pending (request_pending $8F86 non-zero).
Sequences A and C: a step that only moves on to the next.
Sequences B and D, first step: fig_flags of the body $83 and of the head $82 ($03C4, $03C8: visible, image to be rebuilt), next step.
Sequence A: fig_clip $0381 and $0385 = 1, one column clipped from the right; next step.
Sequences B and D: fig_clip $0381 and $0385 = 0, no clipping; next step.
The person's X/2 ($03A3) when the clip last changed; the clip changes once per unit he moves. $32FB after it is not referenced.

Sequences B and D: each pass on which the person's X/2 differs from dw_last_x, one column less is clipped (fig_clip $0381, bit 7 kept; $0385 the same) and bit 1 of fig_flags $03C4 and $03C8 asks for both images to be rebuilt; when X/2 has not changed, or the clip is already 0, and he is not moving ($03BC = 0), next step.
Sequences A and C: as dw_clip_shrink but clipping one column more per unit, stopping at 12 (the whole image); next step when X/2 no longer changes and $03BC is 0.
Activity 81 phase 0: the scratch location moved 9 right ($1DA3 + 9) with depth $0C, destination $36 (set_person_destination) and next phase.
Code that nothing reaches (no JSR, JMP, branch or table word points here; the JMP $8F0B before it ends act81_target): LDA #0, STA $68, JMP $8F0B.
Pass counter of every_8th_pass, shared by activities 30 and 31.

Activity 30, which the activity chooser starts at $E243 when $0368 is 0 and either schedule_step ($035D) is 0 (the night: from the evening until the alarm) or the illness level $0365 is 3 or more. Switches on $68, not $4C, through act30_phase_table: walk to location $12 (the bed, middle floor left), divert to a drink or to activity 4 if one is due, turn, then four timed moves with poses $2E, $31, $32, $33 (17 pixels left in all) and $0368 = $FF. While $0368 is set the chooser ($E389) runs activity 31 before any other activity except 46.

Activity 30's steps, chosen by $68 through switch_68 (10 words, handler minus one): act30_walk_to_bed, act30_check_needs, act30_turn, bed_move_0, bed_move_1, bed_move_2, bed_move_3, act30_set_state, act_bed_finish, $8F0E.

Activity 31, started by the activity chooser at $E255 (a request pending, or schedule_step non-zero, daytime, with the illness level below 3) and put first by $E391 while $0368 is set. Switches on $68 through act31_phase_table: the four moves of activity 30 in reverse (17 pixels right), a pause, $0368 = 0.
Activity 31's steps (8 words, handler minus one): bed_move_3, bed_move_2, bed_move_1, bed_move_0, act31_wait_step, act31_clear_state, act_bed_finish, $8F0E.

Activity 30 step 1: if there is water (water_level $2B51 non-zero) and water_need $036E is 2 or more, switches to activity 29 (a drink); otherwise, if act4_request $0374 is set, to activity 4 (script $9076). Either switch clears the phase counters and empties the queued list ($0423/$0424 = $8D99). With neither, carries on through walk_sub_take_requests ($95ED).
Last step of activities 30 and 31: increments $4C as well as $68.
Activity 31 step 5: $0368 = 0; when $0432 is non-zero calls $2E71, a CLC/RTS stub; next step.
Activity 30 step 7: $0368 = $FF, next step.

Activity 30 step 0: set_custom_location ($16AE) with location $12 (floor line $A5, X/2 $22: beside the bed), destination $36 through set_person_destination, next step. $33EF (INC $68) is the 'next step' of activities 30 and 31.
Activity 30 step 2: turn_to_pose ($255B) to pose 8 with facing 0, each pass; next step once turn_busy ($2540) is 0.
Activity 30 step 3 and activity 31 step 3: every eighth pass moves the person's x by 0 (or +10 while $0368 is set, getting up), pose $2E, next step. The RTS at $3416 after it is never reached.
Activity 30 step 4 and 31 step 2: every eighth pass x - 10 (getting up +8), pose $31, next step.
Activity 30 step 5 and 31 step 1: every eighth pass x - 8 (getting up - 1), pose $32, next step.
Activity 30 step 6 and 31 step 0: every eighth pass x + 1 (getting up 0), pose $33, next step.
Activity 31 step 4: waits for the next eighth pass, then next step.
Returns normally only when bed_tick, incremented here, is a multiple of 8; otherwise pulls its return address and so returns from the calling handler too, leaving the step for another pass.
Adds A to fig_x of the person ($03A7, in sprite units, twice fig_x_half) and sets bit 0 of fig_flags $03C4.

Main-loop sound scheduler, called once per pass from $0974. If $801F is set (a tune ended, tune_end, or stereo_off at $9280) it first resets all sound (sound_reset), stops the CIA music timers ($8012) and clears $801F and the music flag $801E. Then it serves the highest-numbered request slot that is non-zero (snd_req_water $3560 to snd_req_alarm_off $3575, 22 slots) by patching its handler from snd_slot_handlers into the JMP at $34A2 (X = slot) and returns from there. With no slot requested it goes on to play_oneshots and footsteps. The sounds are started through the sound driver's jump table at $B000: sound_start_a ($B009, set A) and sound_start_b ($B006, set B).
Low byte of the JMP operand at $34A2, rewritten from snd_slot_handlers for the slot being served.
High byte of that JMP operand.

Reached when no slot is requested: for each of the four one-shot triggers (snd_oneshot_0b to snd_oneshot_02) that is set, starts its sound from snd_oneshot_sound on set A (sound_start_a, $B009) and clears the trigger; then falls into footsteps.

Footstep sounds for the person (Y = 0) and the dog (Y = 1). When a figure's pose ($038B,Y) is below 5 and equals the pose expected next (step_next,Y: 0 or 4), step_next flips through step_next_table and a sound is chosen by floor and x: none at y $65 (the attic floor); at y $A5 (middle floor) only for x $54-$83, step_mid_l/step_mid_r; at any other y (the ground floor, or on the stairs between floors) only for x below $5C, step_low_l/step_low_r; the pose (0 or 4) picks the l or r sound. Those x ranges are the tiled bathroom and kitchen floors of the picture (screen x about 2 x - 24). For the person, poses 9, 13 and 17 (the first of three runs of four, step_run_start/step_run_end) also play step_stair_sound, once per visit (step_stair_count).
Pose expected next after a step on pose 0-4: $04 $04 $04 $04 $00, so the steps alternate between poses 0 and 4.
Pose that makes the next footstep sound: $354E the person, $354F the dog (0 or 4).
Middle-floor step sound on pose 0: person 4, dog 9.
Middle-floor step sound on pose 4: person 7, dog 9.
Ground-floor step sound on pose 0: person 3, dog 9.
Ground-floor step sound on pose 4: person 6, dog 9.
Sounds for the person's poses 9, 13 and 17: 5 and 8, taken alternately by bit 0 of step_stair_count.
Counter behind step_stair_sound: bit 0 picks the sound; bit 7 is set once the sound has played for the current run and cleared on its other poses. $355B after it is not referenced.

One-shot trigger for sound $0B, set by $5743; the first of the four triggers play_oneshots reads and the first of the 32 bytes sound_reset clears ($355C-$357B: triggers, 22 request slots and six spare bytes).
One-shot trigger for sound $0A: set by each key the player types (type_key at $375F) and by the typing at $572F and $58D4.
One-shot trigger for sound $01, set at $962F by the code that redraws the house's changing pictures ($96ED).
One-shot trigger for sound $02, set at $9672 by the same picture code. stop_slot_below also writes through this address (STA $355F,X) to clear the request of the slot below.

Request slot 0, the first of 22 (a slot is requested by writing any non-zero value): sound $11 played once (play_once). Set by CTRL W at $2C90 when water_level $2B51 is below 11 (the level then rises by one), and by water_drink_glass at $A924 when he drinks (the level falls by one).
Request slot 1: sound $12 played once, set at $26E7 by the pose-$59 handler of activity 39 (phase 5 of its table at $233B).
Request slot 2: sound $13 played once, set by phone_hang_up.

Request slot 3: the piano piece, sound $0C on set B (slot3_piece). Set to $FF by activity 79 (act79_start_piece, $E3F6) and by stereo_on ($925E); cleared by piece_done. $2BCB, $2BE6, $926E and $E400 read it as 'a piece is playing' (CTRL A leaves the alarm alone then). While the stereo plays, the raster interrupt runs sound_dispatch instead of sound_frame, so set B does not advance.

Request slot 4: sound $0F, started once and held until slot 8 stops it; set at $1F14, $211C and by face_away_sound ($2133, activity 29 phase 15, when he stands with his back to the viewer at the sink).
Request slot 5: sound $0E, held until slot 9; set at $5B5D.

Request slot 6: the telephone ring, sound $0D restarted every fourth pass while set (phone_ring_repeat). Set and cleared by the ringing routine ($2AF5, $2AFE) and cleared at $2C1B when the ringing is over.

Request slot 7 (stop_piece): ends the slot-3 piece if it is still requested. piece_done also stores snd_piece_ended ($B012) here, and activity 79 waits for it ($E441) as 'the piece has finished'; written by $2BCE, $9268, $9271, $E3FA and $E403, read at $220C.
Request slot 8 (stop_slot4): stops slot 4 and then everything; set at $1FA6 and $2171.
Request slot 9 (stop_slot5): stops slot 5 and then everything; set at $5B96.
Request slot 10: no code writes it and its handler (slot10_nop) is a bare RTS.

Request slot 11: sound $14 once, then 40 passes of hold-off (chime_with_holdoff). Set by the CTRL key handler for CTRL F ($2B65, only while the cupboard has room), CTRL D ($2B78), CTRL B ($2B8F) and CTRL R ($2BAD).
Request slot 12: sound $18, held until slot 13; set by activity 7 (the fire) at $AFEE.
Request slot 13 (stop_slot_below): stops slot 12 and everything; set by activity 7 at $AFF6.
Request slot 14: sound $1A played until the sound driver sets snd_piece_ended ($B012) (play_to_end); set at $A94A.
Request slot 15: stops slot 14 and everything; set at $A957.
Request slot 16: sound $19, held until slot 17; set at $5AE1.
Request slot 17: stops slot 16 and everything; set at $5899 and $5ADC.

Request slot 18: the talking sound, $15, played to its end (play_to_end). Raised at $24E8 by talk_mouth ($24C8), the mouth step of the talking sub-machine act41_talk ($237E), which talk_or_wait ($2759) also runs inside activities 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11 and the telephone call (25): when it picks the widest mouth (head pose $1C) and this slot is free. So every burst of his speech plays sound $15 once on set A. Cleared at $8EDF (activity 114).
Request slot 19: sound $16 played to its end; set by activity 114 at $8ED7 from $0374.
Request slot 20: the alarm clock, sound $17 held until slot 21; set by CTRL A ($2BEB) and at $0BD8.
Request slot 21, the last one served: stops slot 20 and everything; set at $2A74 when the alarm's count runs out.
A request byte beyond the 22 slots: set at $97D2 but never read (sound_requests starts its scan at slot 21); only sound_reset clears it.
Another request byte beyond the slots: set at $97CD, never read.
Another: set at $543F by activity 32's handler, never read.
Another: set at $53D9, never read.
Another: set at $1EF8, never read.
The last of the six: set at $1F03, never read; the last byte sound_reset clears.

Handler of each request slot, 22 addresses, copied into the JMP at $34A2 by sound_requests: slots 0-2 play_once, 3 slot3_piece, 4, 5, 12, 16 and 20 start_and_hold, 6 phone_ring_repeat, 7 stop_piece, 8 stop_slot4, 9 stop_slot5, 10 slot10_nop, 11 chime_with_holdoff, 13, 15, 17 and 21 stop_slot_below, 14, 18 and 19 play_to_end.
The same table read one byte on for the high bytes (LDA $357D,Y at $349C); it runs to $35A7.

Sound number of each request slot for the sound driver: $11 $12 $13 $0C $0F $0E $0D $10 $10 $10 $10 $14 $18 $10 $1A $10 $19 $10 $15 $16 $17 $10 (slots 0-21). $10, which the stop handlers start, is also what sound_init starts on set B ($B217).
Last entry of snd_slot_sound (slot 21, $10). stop_slot_below writes through this address (STA $35BD,X) to clear the state of the slot below.
State of each request slot, 22 bytes: 0 not started, otherwise the sound number once started (start_slot_sound) or the handler's own value.
State of slot 3: $0C while the piece is running; cleared by piece_done.
State of slot 4, cleared by stop_slot4.
State of slot 5, cleared by stop_slot5; the states of slots 6-21 follow up to $35D3.
X (the slot number) kept by slot3_follow_flags while it loops over the four flags.
Delay counters for flags 0 and 1 in slot3_follow_flags: 3 when the flag drops, counted down before $40 is stored. $35D7-$35D8 after them are not referenced.
Handler for slots 0-2: clears the request and starts snd_slot_sound,X on set A (sound_start_a, $B009).

Handler for slots 14, 18 and 19: the first pass starts the slot's sound (start_slot_sound); later passes wait for snd_piece_ended ($B012), then start sound $10 on set A and clear the slot's state and request.
Handler for slots 13, 15, 17 and 21: clears the state and request of the slot below (12, 14, 16 or 20), then stop_all.
Handler for slots 4, 5, 12, 16 and 20: starts the slot's sound on the first pass and then does nothing while the request stays set; the matching stop slot ends it.
Handler for slot 9: clears slot 5's state and request, then stop_all.
Handler for slot 8: clears slot 4's state and request, then stop_all.
Shared end of the stop handlers: clears the served slot, starts sound $10 on set A and clears all 22 requests and states.
Handler for slot 10: RTS.
Code that nothing reaches (after the RTS of slot10_nop; no address points here): STA $3560,X and JMP $348B, which would re-request the slot and carry on scanning.
Handler for slot 3: on the first pass stores state $0C and starts sound $0C, the piano piece, on set B (sound_start_b, $B006); afterwards slot3_follow_flags.
Shared tail: stores A as the slot's state (snd_slot_state,X) and starts sound A on set A (sound_start_a, $B009).

Slot 3 while the piece plays: once snd_piece_ended ($B012) is set, piece_done. Otherwise copies set B's channel 3 and 4 key-down bits ($B013, $B014) and their toggles ($B015, $B016) into piano_part_offsets ($E41D-$E420), the image offsets of the four quarters of the person at the piano: a key-down bit gives $00 while set and, once clear, $80 for three passes (slot3_flag_delay) and then $40; a toggle gives $40 while set and $00 while clear. Any change is also stored in piano_parts_changed ($E421), which activity 79 checks at $E446 before rebuilding his image (compose_from_parts, $1585).

Ends slot 3: A (snd_piece_ended, or 0 from stop_piece) goes to snd_req_piece_end; clears slot 3's state and request, the served slot's state and $B012, and starts sound $10 on set B (sound_start_b, $B006).
A lone RTS after piece_done's JMP; nothing points here.
Handler for slot 7: when slot 3 is still requested, piece_done with A = 0 (which clears slot 7 too); otherwise just returns, leaving slot 7 requested.
Handler for slot 6: on the first pass ring_tick = 0 and sound $0D starts (start_slot_sound); then every fourth pass (ring_tick) starts it again, for as long as the request is set.

Handler for slot 11: when chime_holdoff is 0, sets it to 40 and starts sound $14; on later passes counts it down and clears the request when it reaches 0, so for 40 passes the chime cannot restart and lower slots wait.
Passes left before slot 11's request is cleared (40 after each chime).
Pass counter of phone_ring_repeat: the ring restarts when its low two bits are 0.
Sounds of the four one-shot triggers: $0B, $0A, $01, $02.
End (exclusive) of each run of the person's poses that footsteps checks, searched from the last: $15, $11, $0D, $09.
First pose of each run (the same bytes one on, read as $370F,X): $11, $0D, $09, $09; the sound plays when the pose equals it, and poses 5-8 fall in no run.

Silences everything: clears the 32 bytes from snd_oneshot_0b ($355C-$357B) and the 22 slot states, zeroes SID registers $D400-$D414, and restarts the sound driver (JMP $B000, sound_init). Called at cold start ($04C8), by sound_requests when $801F is set, by stereo_off ($9286), by act79_start_piece ($E3F1) and at $1FFA.
The last key type_key took (DEL included); nothing else reads it.
Characters typed on the current line: typed_advance counts it up, typed_back down, DEL is refused at 0; RETURN sets it to $FF and the advance after it makes it 0.

Takes a key from $30 into the typed line; called from the main loop ($097C) and at start-up ($052D). Nothing happens while $0711 or $54DF is set. Takes RETURN, DEL and printable keys (codes below $20 are left for the CTRL key handler); printable keys only while $8D, the high byte of the text cursor's x ($8C/$8D, placed by the interrupt at $0769), is 0, which limits the line's length. The first key while the text band is idle ($0710 = 0) calls $BA3A (print position reset, $0710 = 3). Each key goes to type_digit, requests the key click (snd_key_click), is taken ($30 = 0), stored at $0224 + $0222 and echoed through queue_char. DEL steps back (typed_back) and echoes the removed character with $BA38 = 1; RETURN ends the line (typed_count $FF, then typed_advance).
One character back: typed_count - 1 and $0222 - 1 (kept to 0-127).
One character on: typed_count + 1 and $0222 + 1 (kept to 0-127).
Low byte (last two digits) of the four-digit BCD number type_digit collects; $00 in the snapshot, typed as 10:00.
High byte (first two digits) of that number; $10 in the snapshot.
Collects the typed digits as a four-digit BCD number in typed_bcd_hi/lo: a digit shifts it four bits left and adds itself, DEL shifts it four bits right. No reader of the number was found.

Activity 29, a drink of water: the parser rules at $CA5A (DRINK + WATER) and $CA6A (LOOK + GLASS/COOLER) choose it, act30_check_needs switches to it, and the list at $AAB2 includes it. Switches on $4C through act29_phase_table: he goes to location $25 (the kitchen cupboard), then carries an item (figure 2, frame $13) to location $29 by the water cooler, fills and drinks while the tank (water_level $2B51) has water, sometimes again, takes the item to location $24 at the sink, then face_away_sound and face_away_idle (sound $0F while he stands with his back to the viewer). Figure 3 (frame $15) is shown from phase 2 (meal_show_fig3) to phase 17 (meal_hide_fig3).

Activity 29's phase table, 19 words (handler minus one) chosen by $4C: 0 act29_start, 1 wait_or_request ($8FA7), 2 meal_show_fig3 ($5388), 3 act29_take_glass, 4 act29_check_interrupt, 5 act29_at_cooler, 6 act29_wait_step, 7 act29_fill_glass, 8 act29_wait_step, 9 act29_drink, 10 act29_wait_step, 11 act29_maybe_again, 12 act29_return_glass, 13 carry_walk ($293D), 14 act29_glass_away, 15 face_away_sound ($2131), 16 face_away_idle ($2156), 17 meal_hide_fig3 ($5380), 18 $8F0E (end).
Activity 29 phase 4: when a request is pending (request_pending $8F86 non-zero) jumps to phase 12 (take the item back); otherwise continues with carry_walk ($293D).
Pass countdown for act29_wait_step: 8 or 60 passes.
Activity 29 phase 14: clears carrying ($0391) and hides figure 2 ($03C6 = 0), gaze mode $ACF2 = 2, advances.
Activity 29 phase 0: destination location $25, in front of the kitchen cupboard (set_person_destination, $AB63), advances.

Activity 29 phase 3: shows figure 2, the item sprite, with frame $13 ($038D) and colour 3 ($1394), visible ($03C6 = $83), in front ($0398 = 0), facing as the person ($039C = $039A), on a floor line 12 above his ($03B1 = $03AF - 12), 17 units ahead of him ($03A9 = $03A7 plus or minus $11 by his facing) at his X bit 8 and depth, multicolour and carried ($0394 = $0391 = $FF), bit 1 of $03C4; then heads for location $29 beside the water cooler through the tail at $390D (set_custom_location, $03C6 = $83, destination $36, at_target).
Activity 29 phase 5: gaze mode $ACF2 = $C1, hides figure 2 ($03C6 = 0), pose $0D with an 8-pass wait.
Activity 29 phase 7: with the tank empty (water_level $2B51 = 0) sets the phase to 12 (no drink); otherwise clears carrying ($0391), gaze mode $A1, pose $1E with a 60-pass wait.

Activity 29 phase 9: gaze mode $C1; water_drink_glass ($A91F) takes one unit of water (water_level - 1, request slot 0); clears letter_done ($54E2) and water_need ($036E), restarts water_timer from water_period ($0370 = $036F), calls needs_check; pose $46 with a 60-pass wait. $38D7-$38DF, shared with phases 5 and 7, stores the wait count and sets the pose (set_pose, $9363).
Activity 29 phases 6, 8 and 10: counts act29_wait down by one per pass, advancing at 0.
Activity 29 phase 11: gaze mode 2; unless a request is pending, one time in four (random $195E: low four bits below 4) goes back to phase 7 for another drink; otherwise advances.
Activity 29 phase 12: carrying ($0391) = $FF and heads for location $24 (the sink, ground floor, X/2 $30) with figure 2 shown again, through the tail at $390D.
Code that nothing reaches (after act29_return_glass's JMP $8F0B; no address points here): LDA #0, STA $8D9B, RTS, which would set activity 0.

Called after a drink (act29_drink) and by activity 32's handler at $5450: loads act4_countdown ($0376) from act4_delay ($0375, 7) when it is 0; then, when both food_need ($0371) and water_need ($036E) are below 3, clears illness_worsening ($0367), so that the illness level falls back and the green face goes.

Starts the stereo: reached through driver_jumps $800F, whose only caller is stereo_on ($9256), the phase of activity 120 that also sets turntable_on ($2B45, the turntable picture). Clears the sound-job mask $478D and $02ED, then JMP music_start ($4424), which sets up the music driver and starts tune music_tune ($478C) with CIA1 timer A as the note clock and timer B for the effects. Activity 9 (parser rule $C9BA: HEAR, LISTEN, PUT, START or SPIN with STEREO, MUSIC, RECORD...) runs the script $AAEC: 121 (stereo off), 119 ($AB0F picks the tune at random), 118, 120 (stereo on); the DANCE rule ($CAAA) runs activity 9 and then activity 53, the dance, so he dances to these same tunes.

CIA1 interrupt, reached through driver_jumps $8018 from the IRQ handler ($072C) when the source is not the raster. Reads $DC0D (acknowledging it): timer A goes to music_timer_a, timer B to music_timer_b, each after CLI so the raster interrupt can still come in; anything else returns.

Called by the raster interrupt ($0812, through driver_jumps $800C) instead of sound_frame ($B003) while the music flag $801E is set: for each set bit of the job mask $478D (bit 0 first; $02EE the bit number, $02EF the bits left) calls the routine from sound_jobs through jmp_sound_job. music_start clears $478D and no tune sets it, so with the four tunes it calls nothing; only unused code ($39C1, $39F4, $39FA, $456F) sets bits.
JMP ($004D): calls the sound job whose address sound_dispatch put in $4D/$4E.

Split address table, low bytes first, high bytes from $39A4: the eight jobs of sound_dispatch, one per bit of $478D. 0 $4574 filter cutoff from voice 3's envelope ($D41C); 1 $4586 and 2 $4599 add $D41C to voice 2's frequency; 3 $45B2 slides the three voices down; 4 $45EF moves voice 1 by $D41B - $80; 5 $4610 slides voice 3 down; 6 $4625 and 7 $4677 per-voice sweeps from tables at $4794-$479F and $478E.
High-byte half of sound_jobs ($45 and $46), read as $39A4,X by sound_dispatch at $3989.
The RTS sound_dispatch jumps to when done ($3996).

Native routine the tunes call when voice 1's stream is over ($C1 $AD $39 near the end of each tune*_voice1): $801F = $FF, which makes sound_requests reset the sound and clear the music flag on its next pass, then falls into stop_music_timers.
Disables all CIA1 interrupts ($DC0D = $7F) and stops timers A and B ($DC0E = $DC0F = $08: stopped, one-shot). Reached through driver_jumps $8012 from sound_requests and by falling in from tune_end.
A lone RTS after stop_music_timers; nothing points here.
Music-driver helper that no tune calls (no stream holds $C1 $C1 $39 and no code points here): $478D = 1, sound job 0.

SID setting lists that nothing references, in the format of music_regs_all: register and value pairs, ended by a byte of $80 or more. $39C7: 4 $80, 5 $09, 6 $0A, 8 $F8, 9 $F6, 10 $6E. $39D4: 4 $20, 5 $09, 9 $A3. $39DB: 5 $06. $39DE: 2 $B0, 3 $10, 4 $40, 5 $0A, 6 $09. $39E9: 2 $0F, 3 $0A, 4 $40, 5 $0A, 6 $09.
Helper no tune calls: $478D = 3, sound jobs 0 and 1.
Helper no tune calls: $478D = 5, sound jobs 0 and 2.
One more setting list nothing references: register 4 = $10 (triangle), end.

The stereo's four tunes: for each, the start of the stream of SID voices 1, 2 and 3 (music_voice_init at $44A9 takes entry voice + 3 x music_tune; activity 119 picks the tune at random). Tune 0: $3A1B, $3AD5, $3AF5; 1: $3A2D, $3ADB, $3AF9; 2: $3A43, $3AE5, $3B01; 3: $3A60, $3AEF, $3B0B. The streams, read by music_run_voice ($4022): a byte below $80 is a note, high nibble its length (1-5 given, 6 the previous length, 7 length in the next byte, 0 no wait), low nibble the pitch step from the note before: 0-12 is -6 to +6 semitones (so in the text 'a'-'l' are -5 to +6 at the previous length, 'f' repeats the pitch), 13 ties ('m'), 14 is a rest ('n'), 15 takes the step from the next byte ('o', then e.g. '4' $34 = -12, '9' $39 = -7, $0C = +12: six bits signed, bit 6 set for full length). A length unit is 8 ticks of CIA timer A, whose period is the tempo x 256 cycles. A byte of $80 or more is a command, low three bits the group and bits 4-6 a parameter: $80 n push, $90/$A0/$B0 n set/AND/OR the voice flags, $C0 n and $D0 repeat, $81 end of voice, $A1 return, $C1 lo hi call 6502 code, $E1/$F1 n skip on/back; $82+p push and $83+p pull register p, $84+p n set it (p 0 pitch, 1 length, 2 articulation, 3 tempo); $86+p jumps and $C6/$D6/$E6/$F6 calls (1-byte relative, 2-byte relative or absolute), $87+p the same when the count on the stack, decremented, is not 0. Voice flags: bit 7 playing, 6 release before the end, 5 invert every step, 3 run the voice's effect routine, 1 glide (bit 2 its direction), 0 vibrato.

Tune 0, voice 1: flags OR $08 (effect routine, which is left at the do-nothing $44A8), sid_list_voice music_regs_all, tempo $36, pitch $48, calls part_a1, then tune_end and end of voice. 294 length units, about 33 seconds on a PAL machine.
Tune 1, voice 1: flags OR $08, music_regs_all, saves the tempo, vibrato on, pitch $34, calls part_b1 (tempo $5A, later $50), vibrato off, restores the tempo, tune_end, end. 134 length units.
Tune 2, voice 1: music_regs_all, flags OR $09, tempo $36, music_regs_t2, flags OR $20 (every step inverted), articulation 2, pitch $3C, calls part_a1 upside down, flag $20 off, tune_end, end.

Tune 3, voice 1: music_regs_all and then music_regs_t3, pitch $48, part_a1, tune_end, end. No tempo is set, so tune 3 is tune 0 at the starting tempo $3B (about 36 seconds) with another sound on voice 1.
Native helper no tune calls: points voice 1's effect hook (music_hook, $7FF4/$7FF5) at effect_nop. The NOP at $3A7F after it is padding.
Native helper no tune calls: filter resonance and routing $47 (sid_shadow_resonance and $D417), band-pass mode with the volume kept (sid_shadow_volume and $D418).
NOP, RTS: the effect routine unused_set_effect would install. The NOP at $3A98 pads the next helper.
Native helper no tune calls: increments $02F2 and writes it as the filter cutoff (sid_shadow_cutoff and $D416).

SID settings for tune 2's voice 1, read by sid_list_voice (register relative to the voice, value; ended by a byte of $80 or more): control $10 (triangle), attack/decay $36, sustain/release $22, register $17 = 0, end.
SID settings for tune 3's voice 1: pulse width high $01, control $10 (triangle), attack/decay $36, sustain/release $22, end.

SID settings every tune's voice 1 loads first; at voice offset 0 they reach all three voices: attack/decay $A8 x 3, sustain/release $A9, $A9, $79, pulse width low $08 (voices 1, 2) and high $08 (voice 3), control $40 (pulse) x 3, filter routing 0, mode/volume $5C, end.
Tune 0, voice 2: pitch $29, calls part_a2, end of voice.
Tune 1, voice 2: vibrato on, pitch $3C, part_b2, vibrato off, end.
Tune 2, voice 2: inverted, pitch $48, part_a1, inversion off, end.
Tune 3, voice 2: pitch $29, part_a2, end (as tune 0).
Tune 0, voice 3: calls part_a3, end of voice. Tune 3's voice 3 jumps back here.
Tune 1, voice 3: vibrato on, part_b3, vibrato off, end.
Tune 2, voice 3: inverted, pitch $30, part_a1, then clears all its flags ($A0 $00) and ends.

Tune 3, voice 3: part_a3, then jumps back ($96 $1B) to tune0_voice3 to play it again. The second pass would start as voice 1 ends, and tune_end stops the timers then, so it is not heard; the end byte at $3B10 is never reached.
Piece B (tune 1), top part: tempo $5A, the phrase at $3B1C twice (the pitch saved and restored around it), then the passage at $3B30, which changes the tempo to $50 at $3B39; return.
Piece B, middle part: the phrase at $3B70 twice, then $3B92 (with octave leaps written 'o4' and 'o' $0C), return.
Piece B, bass: pitch $21 and sixteen notes, most of them long (lengths 4, 8, 16 and 22 units), return.
Piece A (tunes 0 and 3), middle part: sections at $3C19, $3C53, $3C6C twice, $3C86, $3CA4 twice (an octave figure repeated eight times with $80 $08 ... $97 $06), $3C19 again and $3CAF; return.
Piece A, bass part: pitch $24; sections at $3D02, $3D19, $3D2D twice, $3D35, $3D4C twice, $3D02 again and $3D54; return.

Piece A, top part (voice 1 of tunes 0, 2 and 3, and voices 2 and 3 of tune 2): a rest, $3D8C (itself two calls of $3DAF and more notes), $3DBA, $3DCD twice, $3DE2, $3DF3 twice, $3D8C again and $3E10; return.
A stream subroutine nothing calls: eight notes of length 2 stepping 0, +2, +2, +1, +2, +2, +2, +1 (a major scale) and a return.

Pseudo-random routine nothing calls: shifts the 16-bit value $02F0/$02F1 left one bit, feeding in bit 2 of $02F0 XOR bit 7 of $02F1, and returns the new low byte. The game's own random routine is $195E.
Shift-and-add multiply nothing calls: adds $02F3 x ($1A/$1B) into $18/$19, using up $02F3 and doubling $1A/$1B as it goes.

Copies one character row of a stored image to the screen: $02FC bytes of bitmap from ($1C) to ($1E), and $02FE bytes each of colour-matrix values from ($1A) and colour RAM values from ($18) to the addresses in the patched STA operands (row_matrix_dest, row_colour_dest). Returns with A, Y and X from $02FD, $02FE and $02FF.
Low byte of the colour-matrix destination (operand of the STA at $3E8A, $5C00-based): set at $96F0 from $97F0,X, then 40 on per row.
High byte of that destination, set at $96F6 from $9800,X; the colour RAM loop follows.
Low byte of the colour RAM destination (operand of the STA at $3E96, $D800-based): set at $96FC from $9810,X, then 40 on per row.
High byte of that destination, set at $9702 from $9820,X; the routine's end follows.

Draws one character row of an image and moves everything on to the next row: keeps A, X, Y (width Y cells) in $02FD, $02FF, $02FE, sets $02FC = 8 x Y, calls copy_image_row, then advances the destinations (matrix and colour RAM by 40, bitmap $1E/$1F by 320) and the sources ($1C/$1D by 8 x Y, $1A/$1B and $18/$19 by Y). Called once per row by the loop at $99CB, after $96ED has chosen picture X's destination and image.
The switch on $68: LDA $68 and on to switch_a. Used with JSR, the table of handler addresses minus one following the call (16 call sites, among them act30_to_bed, act31_get_up and doorway_script).
The switch on the activity phase $4C (84 call sites): LDA $4C and falls into switch_a.

On n go to, n in A: pulls the return address (the JSR's last byte) into $28/$29, adds 2n + 1 to reach word n of the table after the JSR, pushes that word (a handler address minus one) and returns into the handler. Control never comes back to the call site, and n is not checked against the table's length. Called directly at $16EE and by the activity switch at $8DC6.
n, kept here while switch_a works.

Timer A interrupt (from timer_irq): the note clock, one tick per timer period (the tempo x 256 cycles). Stops both timers (timers_stop), then for each voice (rec_cur_voice $7FE7 = 0-2, SID offset from music_sid_offset in rec_cur_sid_ofs, record offset from music_voice_offset in $7FE9) whose flags (byte 12 of its record, $7F52) have bit 7 set: counts its length counter (byte 9, $7F4F) down; at 0 copies the 13-byte state from rec_voice1 + offset into $53-$5F (stack pointer $60/$61 = record + 13), runs music_run_voice ($4022) and copies the state back; otherwise, with flag bit 6 set and the counter at the release point (byte 10, $7F50), clears the gate bit of the voice (sid_shadow_ctrl and $D404 + offset). Restarts the timers at the end ($400F).
SID register offset of each voice: 0, 7, 14.
Offset of each voice's 45-byte record from rec_voice1 ($7F46): 0, $2D, $5A (13 bytes of state, 32 of stack); also read by music_voice_init at $44C3.

Timer B interrupt (from timer_irq; period $4295 cycles, set by music_start): stops the timers; when any voice's flags have one of bits 0-3 set, calls music_effects ($4303) for each playing voice with A = $0F: bit 0 vibrato, bit 1 glide, bit 3 the voice's effect routine through $7FF4. Restarts the timers.
Stops CIA1 timers A and B (clears bit 0 of $DC0E and $DC0F), keeping A. Used by music_timer_a, music_timer_b and music_start ($4424); the matching restart is at $400F.

Second half of the routine at $3FFC, which starts just below this range (PHA, LDA $DC0E): clears the start bit of CIA1 timer A ($DC0E) and of timer B ($DC0F), pausing both music interrupts, then restores A. The timer A handler ($3F3B) and the timer B handler ($3FBF) call $3FFC on entry and timers_start on the way out, so the timers stand still while either handler works.

Sets the start bit of CIA1 timer A ($DC0E) and timer B ($DC0F) again, resuming both music interrupts after $3FFC paused them; A is preserved. Called at the end of the timer A handler ($3FB5) and the timer B handler ($3FF8).

The music interpreter: runs one voice's byte code until something makes it wait. Called by the timer A handler ($3FA0) when the voice's tick countdown r7 runs out, with the voice's 13 bytes of state copied from its block ($7F46 + $2D * voice) to $53-$5F: $53/$54 the byte-code pointer; $55-$5C registers r0-r7 (r0 the current note number, r1 the last length, r2 the release fraction, r3 the tempo, r7 the tick countdown; r4-r6 are free for the byte code); $5D the tick at which the gate is released; $5E the stack index and $5F the flags; $60/$61 point at the voice's 32-byte stack. Bytes are read with music_fetch (offset in $7F40). A byte below $80 is a note (music_note); a byte of $80 or more is a command: its low three bits pick a handler in music_ops and its bits 4-6 go to $7F41 as n. Carry set from a handler means carry on; carry clear ends the pass, and music_commit then moves the pointer past the bytes read.

JMP ($004F): the indirect call of the music code. music_run_voice calls its command handlers through it ($404D), op_flow its native-code calls, and fx_hook the per-voice hook ($434F). Callers JSR here, so the code at ($4F) returns to them.

Adds the bytes fetched so far ($7F40) to the byte-code pointer $53/$54 and clears $7F40, so the pointer then addresses the next unread byte; A is preserved. Called before every command that reads or changes the pointer (jumps, calls, returns, loops, native calls) and at the end of each pass ($4052).

The eight command handlers of the music byte code, as exact addresses for JMP ($004F) (not minus one), picked by the low three bits of a command byte $80-$FF: 0 op_misc, 1 op_flow, 2 op_push_reg, 3 op_pop_reg, 4 op_load_reg, 5 op_nop, 6 op_jump, 7 op_djnz. n, bits 4-6 of the command, is passed in $7F41; bit 3 is ignored.

Music command op 0 ($80, $90 ... $F0): a second dispatch on n ($7F41) through op_misc_ops; for n = 0 to 4 it first fetches the operand byte into A. n = 0 push the byte, 1 set the flags $5F, 2 AND the flags, 3 OR the flags, 4 start a loop, 5 end of loop, 6 nothing, 7 drop the top of the stack. Returns carry set.
op_misc n = 0 (command $80): pushes the operand byte onto the voice's stack with music_push.

op_misc n = 1 ($90): sets the voice flags $5F to the operand. Bit 7 voice playing, bit 6 release the gate early (set by every note), bit 5 invert note steps, bit 3 run fx_hook, bit 2 slide up rather than down, bit 1 fx_slide, bit 0 fx_vibrato.
op_misc n = 2 ($A0): ANDs the operand into the voice flags $5F. The four tunes use $FE (vibrato off), $DF (inversion off) and $00.
op_misc n = 3 ($B0): ORs the operand into the voice flags $5F. The four tunes use $01 (vibrato), $08 (hook), $09 and $20 (invert the note steps: the phrase is played upside down).
op_misc n = 4 ($C0): start of a loop. Pushes the byte-code pointer (music_push_pc, the address after the operand), then the operand, the number of passes; op_next jumps back to that address.

op_misc n = 5 ($D0): end of a loop. Pops the pass count and decrements it; if passes remain it pushes the count back and sets the pointer to the address saved beneath it (the byte after op_loop's operand); when it was 1 it drops the saved address and carries on after this byte.
op_misc n = 6 ($E0): does nothing (an RTS; the caller returns carry set).
op_misc n = 7 ($F0): pops the top byte of the voice's stack and discards it.
op_misc's eight handler addresses, exact, indexed by n: op_push_imm $409E, op_flags_set $40A2, op_flags_and $40A5, op_flags_or $40AA, op_loop $40AF, op_next $40B8, op_misc_nop $40D6, op_drop $40D7.

Music command op 1 ($81 ... $F1), by n: 0, 1 and 3 end the voice: clear flag bit 7 and the gate bit of its control register (shadow $7FD1+voice and SID $D404+voice) and return carry clear. 2 returns from a byte-code call (pops the pointer, high byte first). 4 and 5 call machine code at the address in the next two bytes; 6 and 7 call machine code at the pointer (after the operand) plus or minus the next byte. The pointer is committed first, so the machine code can take further inline bytes with music_fetch (sid_list_voice does). The four tunes use n = 4 to call sid_list_voice ($43FE) and, at their end, $39AD (sets record_stop_req, turns the CIA1 interrupts off and stops both timers).
Music command op 2 ($82 ... $F2): pushes register n ($55+n) onto the voice's stack. The tunes use it to save r0, the current note, around a phrase.
Music command op 3 ($83 ... $F3): pops the top of the voice's stack into register n ($55+n); for n = 3 it also sets the tempo (music_set_tempo).

Music command op 4 ($84 ... $F4): loads register n ($55+n) with the next byte; for n = 3 it also sets the tempo (music_set_tempo). The tunes load r0 (the starting note), r2 (the release fraction) and r3 (the tempo).

When X = 3 (register r3), copies A to r3 of all three voices ($7F4B, $7F78, $7FA5) and into CIA1 timer A as its high byte ($DC05; low byte $DC04 = 0): the tick rate, which all three voices share. For any other X it does nothing.
Music command op 5 ($85 ... $F5): does nothing and carries on (carry set).

Music command op 6 ($86 ... $F6), also op_djnz's taken branch: sets the byte-code pointer by n AND 3: 0 forward by the next byte, 1 back by the next byte (both counted from the byte after the operand), 2 forward by the next two bytes, 3 to the absolute address in the next two bytes. With n bit 2 set it is a call: the address after the operand is pushed first (music_push_pc) for op_flow's return. The tunes use $C6 (call forward), $F6 (call absolute) and $96 (jump back).
Commits the pointer (music_commit) and pushes it onto the voice's stack, low byte then high byte: the return address for op_jump's calls and the loop start for op_loop.

Music command op 7 ($87 ... $F7): decrements the byte on top of the voice's stack in place (it is not popped); if the result is not zero it jumps as op_jump does, and if it is zero it skips the jump's operand (one byte, two when n bit 1 is set) and carries on.
Returns in A the next byte-code byte, ($53) indexed by $7F40, and advances $7F40.
Pushes A onto the voice's stack: stores it at ($60) indexed by $5E and increments $5E; Y is left at the slot written. Nothing checks the 32-byte size of the stack.
Pops the top byte of the voice's stack into A: decrements $5E and reads ($60) indexed by it.

A byte-code byte below $80: a note. Bits 4-6 give the length: 0 no wait (only the pitch changes), 1-5 that many units, 6 the previous length (r1), 7 the next byte; r1 keeps it and the countdown r7 gets 8 ticks a unit (more than 31 units wraps). Bits 0-3 give the pitch: 0-12 step the note number r0 by -6 to +6 semitones; 13 hold (no new pitch, no new attack); 14 rest (gate off); 15 take the step from the next byte (-32 to +31 in its low six bits; its bit 6 cancels the early release for this note). Flag bit 5 inverts the step. The pitch comes from freq_table at r0 * 2 into the SID ($D400/$D401 + voice) and the shadow ($7FCD/$7FCE + voice), and the gate bit is set. When r2 is not 0 the gate is released at countdown r1 * r2 (mul8), r2 eighths of the note before its end; $5D keeps that tick. Also sets flag bit 6 and counts the note in $7FEA+voice and note_count. Returns carry clear to wait, carry set when the length is 0.

The per-voice effects, called by the timer B handler ($3FED) with A = $0F for each playing voice whose flags have any of bits 0-3 set: ANDs A with the flags $5F, then bit 0 runs fx_vibrato, bit 1 fx_slide (bit 2 giving its direction) and bit 3 fx_hook.

Flag bit 1: a pitch slide. Adds (flag bit 2 set) or subtracts (clear) frequency * rate / 2048 to or from the shadow frequency, the rate being $7FF1+voice (7 after music_start), writes the result to the SID and keeps it in the shadow, so each call moves the pitch by the same musical interval. None of the four tunes sets bit 1.

Flag bit 3: calls the machine code whose address is in $7FF4/$7FF5 + 2 * voice. music_start points all three at $44A8, the RTS that ends music_start, so it does nothing in this build, although tunes 0, 1 and 2 set bit 3.

Four vibrato depths, 0, 1, 3, 1, reached through $64/$65, which music_start sets to $4353 ($443D-$4443, immediate operands, so nothing names this address). fx_vibrato takes one per tick, times the frequency / 256, added for four ticks and subtracted for the next four.

Flag bit 0: vibrato. Counts ticks in $7FED+voice; the count AND ($7FF0 - 1) (0-3, $7FF0 being 4) picks a depth from the table at ($64), vibrato_shape. Depth * frequency / 256 is added to the shadow frequency when the count AND $7FF0 is 0 and subtracted otherwise, and written to the SID only: the shadow keeps the true pitch. A depth of 0 writes the plain frequency.

Loads the voice's shadow frequency ($7FCD/$7FCE + $7FE8) shifted right Y times into $7F43 (high) and $7F44 (low), and clears $7F42 and the product $4F/$50: the set-up for freq_scale. fx_slide uses Y = 3, fx_vibrato Y = 0.
Multiplies the 24-bit $7F42/$7F43/$7F44 by A (kept in $7F45, shift and add) and adds the product's upper 16 bits to $50/$4F: $4F/$50 = shifted frequency * A / 256.

With Z clear, writes the shadow frequency of the voice at register offset X minus $4F/$50 to the SID ($D400/$D401,X); entered with Z set (or at $43E2), writes it plus $4F/$50. The result is also left in $4F/$50; the shadow is not changed here.

Native routine for the byte code, twin of sid_list_voice with absolute register numbers ($51 = 0): takes a pointer from the next two byte-code bytes and writes the (register, value) pairs there to the SID and the shadow, up to a register byte with bit 7 set. Nothing refers to $43F8: no instruction, no table and no byte-code call (searched for $F8 $43 in all 64 KB).

Native routine called from the byte code (bytes $C1 $FE $43, then a two-byte pointer): writes the (register, value) pairs at the pointer to the SID ($D400+) and the shadow ($7FCD+), register numbers counted from the current voice's registers ($7FE8), until a register byte with bit 7 set. The four tunes call it six times, from voice 1, to set waveforms, envelopes, pulse widths, the filter and the volume.

Starts the record player's music, tune music_tune (0-3), from scratch; reached by JMP from $3956 (rec_drv_start $800F leads to $394E, which first clears $478D and $02ED). Pauses the timers ($3FFC), disables and acknowledges the CIA1 interrupts, clears sound_job_bits, clears zero page $4F-$65, $7F40-$7FF9 and $46C9-$478B (music_clear), programs every SID register (sid_init), builds freq_table, points the vibrato at vibrato_shape with four phases ($7FF0), sets the three hook vectors to $44A8 (an RTS) and the slide rates to 7, sets up the three voices (music_voice_init), sets the tempo to $3B (timer A every $3B00 cycles, about 65 ticks a second on PAL, 68 on NTSC), starts timer A and timer B (every $4295 cycles, the effects, about 58 a second on PAL, 60 on NTSC) and enables their interrupts ($DC0D = $83).

Sets up voice X (0-2) for music_start: the byte-code pointer from the tune table at $3A03 (entry 3 * music_tune + X), flags $C0 (playing, early release), countdown r7 = 1 (so the first tick starts it), release fraction r2 = 2 (the gate goes off a quarter of each note before its end), everything else zero; then copies the 13 bytes $53-$5F into the voice's block at $7F46 + $2D * X.
Clears zero page $4F-$65 (the interpreter's work area), $7F40-$7FF9 (the three voice blocks and stacks, the SID shadow and the effect variables) and $46C9-$478B (freq_table and note_count).
Builds freq_table (96 words, notes 0-95): copies freq_top_octave into its last 12 entries, then makes each lower entry the one 12 above halved (LSR high byte, ROR low byte), down to entry 0.

SID frequency values (low, high) of notes 84-95, the top octave, C to B, copied into freq_table: $861E, $8E18, $968B ... $FD2E. $861E gives 2093 Hz, C7, on an NTSC C64 (1.0227 MHz): the music is tuned for NTSC, and a PAL machine (0.9852 MHz) plays it about 3.7% flat, two-thirds of a semitone.
Copies the 25 bytes of sid_init_values to the SID registers $D400-$D418 and to the shadow $7FCD-$7FE5.

The SID set-up of music_start (sid_init), register by register from $D400: voice 1 frequency $10C3, pulse width $0800, control $40 (pulse, gate off), attack/decay $09, sustain/release $00; voice 2 $1660, $0800, $10 (triangle), $09, $00; voice 3 $1C30, $0A00, $40 (pulse), $09, $29; filter cutoff $07/$80, resonance and routing $80, mode and volume $1D (low-pass, volume 13).

Sets sound job bit 0 ($478D = 1) and falls into job_filter_env3, so that job also runs once straight away. Nothing refers to $456F (no JSR, JMP, table entry or byte-code call; searched for $6F $45 in all 64 KB); $39C1 sets the same bit without the immediate run.
Sound job 0 (bit 0 of $478D): copies voice 3's envelope output ($D41C) to the filter cutoff, whole to $D416 and AND 7 to $D415. Both shadow stores go to $7FE2 ($D415's), so $7FE3 is never updated.

Sound job 1: adds voice 3's envelope output ($D41C) to voice 2's frequency by reading $D407/$D408 back, but those SID registers are write-only, so the value read is not the frequency. Job 2 (job_v2_env3) does the same through the shadow.
Sound job 2: adds voice 3's envelope output ($D41C) to voice 2's frequency (shadow $7FD4/$7FD5, SID $D407/$D408): a pitch that climbs with the envelope.

Sound job 3: lowers the frequencies of all three voices, by 5, 10 and 15 a call, in the shadow. Several stores look mistyped: voice 1's borrow DECs $D400 instead of $D401, voice 2's new low byte goes to $D400 instead of $D407, and voice 3's borrow DECs $7FDB and $D40E instead of $7FDC and $D40F.

Sound job 4: moves voice 1's frequency (shadow $7FCD/$7FCE, SID $D400) by voice 3's oscillator output ($D41B) minus $80, a random wobble when voice 3 plays noise. Its carries INC or DEC $D401 directly, a write-only register, so the high byte on the chip is not the shadow's.
Sound job 5: lowers voice 3's frequency by $14 a call (shadow $7FDB/$7FDC, SID $D40E); the borrow DECs $D40F directly, a write-only register.

Sound job 6: for each of three slots (X = 2 to 0) whose trill_targets entry is not zero, that entry minus one being the SID register offset of a frequency: flips bit 7 of trill_phase+X, then adds trill_up+X to the shadow frequency (bit clear) or subtracts trill_down+X (bit set), writing the low byte to the SID; the high byte changes only in the shadow.

Sound job 7: for each of three slots (X = 2 to 0) whose slide_targets entry is not zero, lowers the frequency at SID register offset entry - 1 by $B0 a call, low and high bytes, in the SID and the shadow.
A = $47A0 * $47A1, 8 bits (shift and add; both operands are used up). music_note uses it for the release tick r1 * r2.
The six bytes the cold start copies to the hardware vectors $FFFA-$FFFF (at $043A): NMI $0833 (nmi_shim), RESET $0340 (reset_jumps), IRQ $082B (irq_shim).

Six bytes $FF $00 $FF $00 $FF $00 after hw_vectors, the same in the load image; the cold start copies only the six before them. No reference found (searched all 64 KB for $C3-$C8 $46); not known to be used.

SID frequency values (low, high) for notes 0-95, C0 to B7 by semitones (NTSC tuning: see freq_top_octave), built at each music_start by freq_table_build; zero in the load image. music_note reads entry r0; entry 0 is $010C. Nothing keeps r0 below 96: notes 96-127 would read note_count and the bytes after it, and 128 or more wrap round to the low entries.
Three note counters, one per voice, incremented by music_note ($424B) at every note and cleared by music_clear. No reader found, and none for the similar counters at $7FEA-$7FEC either.

The tune music_start plays, 0-3: music_voice_init reads the three byte-code pointers of tune n at $3A03 + 6n. Written only by activity 119 ($77, entry $AB0F): a random number ($195E) AND 3, then script_next.

Sound jobs to run: sound_dispatch ($396E, called from the raster IRQ at $0812 while record_playing is set) runs job n of sound_jobs ($399C) for each bit n that is set. Cleared at $3950 and by music_start. Set only by $39C1 (1), $39F4 (3), $39FA (5) and job_filter_start (1), and no caller of any of them was found (no JSR, JMP, table entry or byte-code call); it is 0 in every snapshot, so in this build the eight jobs look unused.
job_slots_fall's three slots: the SID register offset + 1 of a frequency to lower, 0 for an empty slot. No writer found: they stay 0 after music_clear.
Scratch for job_trill and job_slots_fall: the slot's SID register offset, stored from Y so that it can be loaded into X for INC/DEC abs,X.
Scratch for job_trill and job_slots_fall: saves the slot index X while X holds the register offset. $4793 after it is unused.
job_trill's three toggles: bit 7 flips at every call; after the flip, clear means add trill_up, set means subtract trill_down.
job_trill's three slots: the SID register offset + 1 of a frequency low byte to wobble, 0 for an empty slot. No writer found.
job_trill: per slot, the amount added to the frequency on the up call.
job_trill: per slot, the amount subtracted from the frequency on the down call.
