Zeroed by snd_output every frame ($B355); nothing reads it.

Per channel: filter cutoff sweep step, low three bits (read from the stream by $D15A: music commands $11, $1C, $1D, $1F); added to the set's cutoff by $D258 (commands $12, $17, $18, $19, $1A, $1B), reversing at the ends.
Per channel: filter cutoff sweep step, high byte.
Per channel: pulse width sweep step, low byte (read by $D1A2: music commands $13, $1C, $1E, $1F); added to the pulse width by $D2B5 (commands $14, $15, $16, $17, $1A, $1B), reversing at the ends.
Per channel: pulse width sweep step, high nibble.

Sixteen bytes a channel for channels 0-5 ($B174-$B1D3), not cleared by sound_init. Filled from the stream by music command $23 (up to 16 bytes, ended by a $23) and commands $40-$4F (n+1 bytes) at $D3E2-$D3FD; commands $30-$3F play entry (command - $30) as a note ($D416). In every snapshot after start-up channel 3's list begins 'RAMS' ($B1A4) and channel 5's 'ANGMAN' ($B1C4): the bytes after 'G' and 'H' in ANAGRAMS and HANGMAN at $C90D and $C918, and 'A' ($41), 'G' ($47) and 'H' ($48) are note-list commands, so those set-B channels once ran through the parser's word list. Before sound_init sets them, their stream pointers are bytes of BASIC's CHRGET routine left in zero page by the loader: $7B/$7C = $08 $C9 (channel 3, $C908) and $7F/$80 = $0A $C9 (channel 5, $C90A), just before ANAGRAMS; two frames of stepping from there give exactly these lists. sound_init's first tune start ends with CLI ($B2F4) before the second one resets channels 3-5; how two frame updates fell in that gap is not established.
The note lists of channels 4 ($B1B4-$B1C3) and 5 ($B1C4-$B1D3), the last two of snd_note_lists. Channel 5's begins 'ANGMAN' in every snapshot after start-up.
Counter incremented every frame by sound_frame, and once more when it reaches a multiple of 4 ($B509-$B513); mixed into snd_random.
Register offset (7 x channel) of each channel, stored twice so that the index 2 x channel can be used directly: 0, 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42 for channels 0-6. Only channels 0-5 are used.

Start the sound driver: SEI, clear $B012-$B173 (all channel state, not the note lists), copy the IRQ vector into snd_saved_irq_lo/hi, start tune 0 on set A (instrument 0, filter preset 4 with volume 15, then nothing) and tune $10 on set B (an empty stream), which also re-enables interrupts.

Read two bytes from the stream of channel $6C into snd_slide_lo/hi and move the stream pointer ($75/$76 + $6C) past them; X = $70 on return. Called by music commands $1D, $1E, $1F and by command 6 ($D481).
Music command $11 (handler table at $D700): read the filter sweep step ($D15A), then read the next command (snd_next_command).
Music command $12: one filter sweep step ($D258), then the next command.
Start tune A on set A (channels 0-2, the set that wins a SID voice): keep Y in snd_temp_y, Y = 0 (the first channel index), and continue in sound_start_b's common part.
Music command $13: read the pulse sweep step ($D1A2), then the next command.
Music command $14: one pulse width sweep step ($D2B5), then the next command.

Start tune A (an entry of snd_table at $D764; 0-26 are defined) on set B (channels 3-5): keep Y, Y = 6 (2 x channel 3). Common part: SEI and bank the I/O area out; for each of the three voices of the tune's six-byte entry in the tune table at $D764 (a stream address per voice; 0 = unused, and that channel keeps whatever it was playing) mark the channel active, point its stream there ($75/$76 + 2 x channel), clear its counters and loops, take the instrument from the stream's first byte (snd_set_instrument), clear its tracking, load filter preset 0 into the set's filter record ($D362) and make it one-shot. Then restore X and Y, stir snd_random, bank the I/O area in and CLI.
Music command $15: a pulse sweep step ($D2B5), a pitch slide down ($D1CB), then a duration byte and key down ($D08F).
Music command $16: a pulse sweep step ($D2B5), a pitch slide up ($D1CF), then a duration ($D08F).
Music command $17: a pulse sweep step ($D2B5) and a filter sweep step ($D258), then the next command.

A = instrument (a byte offset into the instrument table at $D587, under the I/O area): move channel $6C's stream pointer on by one and copy the instrument's five bytes into the channel's pulse low/high, control, attack/decay and sustain/release shadows (snd_regs + 2..6). Called at a tune start, by music command $0C ($D4D2) and at the start of a called stream ($D0DD: commands 4, $0A, $20).
Music command $1B: a filter sweep step ($D258), a pulse sweep step ($D2B5), a pitch slide up ($D1CF), then a duration ($D08F).
Music command $1C: read the filter sweep step ($D15A) and the pulse sweep step ($D1A2), then the next command.
Music command $1E: read the pulse sweep step ($D1A2) and the pitch slide step (snd_read_slide), then the next command.

Second half of sound_frame: for SID voices 2, 1, 0 in turn, give the voice to the set-A channel if it is active, otherwise to the set-B channel (unless snd_filter_restore is set); write that set's filter record when pending; copy the channel's seven shadow registers to the voice ($D400 + 7v) and send a pending test bit once. Before that, for each set-B channel with tracking on, copy the key bit of channels 3 and 5 into snd_gate_ch3/ch5 and run the key-down tracker.

Reached from the command dispatch ($D35C) instead of snd_cmd_dispatch_jmp when snd_dispatch_count reaches 0: INC snd_rare_count and normally fall into snd_cmd_dispatch_jmp. When snd_rare_count wraps to 0 the command is skipped: if bit 5 of channel 0's frequency high byte is set, that byte becomes $3F and the RTS at $B3D7 leaves sound_frame early; otherwise the loop goes on with the next voice ($B541).

JMP to the current music command's handler. The dispatcher at $D33E writes the handler address from the table at $D700 into this instruction's operand (snd_cmd_dispatch_target) and jumps here ($D35F). $B3D7 (an RTS) in the unstarted image.
Operand of snd_cmd_dispatch_jmp, rewritten for every command: $D3C5 in play-02, $D4F3 in play-01, $D57C at the time prompt.
Operand of the JSR at $B3B9 (low byte), rewritten by snd_output with the key-down tracker's handler from snd_track_handlers.
Operand of the JSR at $B3B9 (high byte), see snd_track_call_lo.

Eight handler addresses for the key-down tracker, indexed by ((snd_track_state x 2) + key bit) AND 7: 0 nothing ($B3D7), 1 key down: set state bit 1 ($B3E1), 2 clear bit 0 ($B3CF), 3 nothing, 4 key up: set bit 0 ($B3D8), 5 and 6 nothing, 7 key down again: clear bit 1 and flip the toggle ($B3E6).
High byte of snd_track_handlers' first entry; the table is read as pairs at $B3AD/$B3B3.
Key-down tracker handler: clear bit 0 of snd_track_state for channel offset Y. Falls into the RTS at $B3D7.
Key-down tracker handler: set bit 0 of snd_track_state (Y = channel offset).
Key-down tracker handler: set bit 1 of snd_track_state (A = 2, then the OR at $B3DA).
Key-down tracker handler: clear bit 1 of snd_track_state and flip snd_toggle_ch3 (channel offset $15, channel 3) or snd_toggle_ch45 (channels 4 and 5) between $00 and $FF.
Music command $1F: read the filter sweep step, the pulse sweep step and the pitch slide step, then the next command.
Music command $1D: read the filter sweep step ($D15A) and the pitch slide step (snd_read_slide), then the next command.

Music command $26: STA snd_piece_ended with A as the dispatcher leaves it, the high byte of this handler's address ($B4), then the next command. It marks the end of a piece for the sound-request code (slot3_follow_flags at $365D).
Music command $18: a filter sweep step ($D258), a pitch slide down ($D1CB), then a duration ($D08F).
Music command $19: a filter sweep step, a pitch slide up ($D1CF), then a duration.
Music command $1A: a filter sweep step, a pulse sweep step, a pitch slide down, then a duration.

Music command $27: STA snd_track_enable + X (X = the channel's register offset) with A = $B4, the high byte of this handler's address left by the dispatcher, which turns the channel's key-down tracking on; then the next command.
Reached by JMP from music command 5 and from command 3 on a set-B channel ($D0C9-$D0CC): start the tune in A on set B, then run sound_frame again from the top.
Reached by JMP from music command 3 on a set-A channel ($D0C6): start the tune in A on set A, then fall into sound_frame.

The driver's frame update (via $B003 from the raster interrupt, and after snd_start_a_restart or snd_start_b_restart). First re-derives tune 12's second and third voice addresses from the first ($D7AC + 4, + 8); on the interrupt path the I/O area is banked in ($0723), so these three instructions address SID registers ($D40C, $D40E, $D410) instead of the tune table. Then advances snd_frame_mix, snd_dispatch_count, snd_frame_count and snd_random, and for voices 0-2 steps the set-A and set-B channels: count down the note, release the key, and at the end of a note read commands until one waits (snd_next_command). Ends in snd_output.

Read channel $6C's next stream byte with the I/O area banked out (streams may lie under it, $D800-$DDFF). Non-zero: JMP to the interpreter at $D000 ($B62D), which moves the pointer on, stores the byte in snd_last_cmd and dispatches it. Zero, the end of the stream: return to a caller saved by music command 4 (restoring its registers) or, with none, stop the channel and release its SID voice's key. The target of most command handlers and of commands $28-$2F.
Bank the I/O area back in (set bit 0 of $01), keeping A. Called before each channel step and at the end of a tune start.

Frequency words looked up with the note byte itself as the index, for notes below $90 ($D049-$D051): note byte $10 reads $B651/$B652 = 0, a rest. $B641-$B660 are all zero; bytes $50-$8F would index $B691-$B6D0, inside the tables that follow.
High bytes of snd_freq_direct (the table is read as pairs, low at $B641,Y and high at $B642,Y).

Top-octave frequency words for note bytes $90-$FF: index = (byte / 16) x 2, plus $20 when bit 3 is set ($D05B-$D06C); the value is halved 7 - (byte AND 7) times ($D071-$D07F), so the low three bits are the octave. Only fourteen slots are used, at $B673-$B680 and $B693-$B6A0; the others are zero or hold other data.
High bytes of snd_freq_octave (read as pairs at $B661,Y and $B662,Y).

Seven frequency words used by snd_freq_octave for note bytes $9x-$Fx without bit 3: $C8F3, $E18F, $FD2E, $861E, $968B, $A8FA, $B306. With snd_freq_notes_b they are the twelve semitones of an equal-tempered octave ($861E to $FD2E, each about 1.059 times the last).
A two-byte stream, $00 $00: instrument 0 and the end of the stream. Entry 2 of the shared stream-subroutine table (snd_subs_shared); tune 0 calls it.

Tune 0's stream (all three voices of tune 0 in the tune table at $D764 point here): instrument 0; $0F (no operation); $0D $04 (filter preset at offset 4: no filter, volume 15); $04 $82 (call shared subroutine 2, snd_stream_rest); $00 end. sound_init plays it on set A.
Seven frequency words used by snd_freq_octave for note bytes with bit 3 set: $D4E6, $EEF8, $861E, $8E18, $9F7E, $B306, $BDAC.

Filter presets, four bytes each, chosen by a byte offset (0 at every tune start, $D362; music command $0D's operand, $D4D8): cutoff low bits with bit 7 set (write pending), cutoff high byte ($D416), resonance and routing ($D417), mode and volume ($D418). Twenty presets to $B6F0; offsets 0 and 4 are 'no filter, volume 15'. Presets 11-14 (offsets $2C, $30, $34, $38) are a resonant band-pass (resonance 15 on voices 1 and 2, mode/volume $2F) at cutoff $40, $60, $80 and $A0: the vowel colours of the talking syllables.
snd_filter_presets + 1: cutoff high byte of each preset (read at $D372 with the preset offset in X).
snd_filter_presets + 2: resonance and routing of each preset ($D378).
snd_filter_presets + 3: mode and volume of each preset ($D37E).
Filter presets 16-19 of snd_filter_presets ($B6E1-$B6F0): 80 FF F1 3F, 80 6F F2 2F, 80 FF F2 2F, 80 90 F1 2F.

53 bytes with a repeating $44 $04 pattern, between the filter presets and the duration table. No reference found. Music command $0D forces the pending bit, so these could be further filter presets reached by larger offsets; not established.

Note durations, a pair per even duration byte: frames with the key down, then frames of release ($D09D-$D0AF put them in snd_note_on and snd_note_off). Pairs run to about $B7CF (duration bytes up to $A8); $B766-$B76B are also the start of snd_subs_shared.
snd_durations + 1: the release half of each pair (read at $D0AC).

Stream-subroutine table for operand bytes with bit 7 set on set-A channels (music commands 4, $0A, $20, $24 through $D527, which finds this table through the pointer at $D831): entry n at $B766 + 2n. Entry 1 is $B68B (tune 0's stream), entry 2 $B681 (snd_stream_rest); entries 3-55 overlap snd_durations; entries 56-75 are at snd_subs_shared_56.
$00 $FF three times, between the durations and the addresses at $B7D6. Nothing refers to them; they look like uninitialised RAM.

Entries 56-75 of snd_subs_shared: twenty stream addresses $DBA3, $DBA9, $DBAF, $DBB5, $DA98, $DA9D ... $DAEC (music data under the I/O area). Entries 56-59 are the talking syllables: each is instrument $69 (noise with the test bit), filter preset 11, 12, 13 or 14 (music command $0D), the top-octave note $B7 for 2 frames and 1 of release, and a return (command $21). Both voices of the talking tune $15 start with command $20 $B8 $03, which calls one of the four at random.

Stream-subroutine table of channel 1 for operand bytes with bit 7 clear (pointer at $D835): entry n at $B7FE + 2n. The only entries that are stream addresses are 100-111 at $B8C6-$B8DD; the rest of $B7FE-$B8C5 is zero, $FB00 (entry 0) or $FFxx values. The talking tune $15 calls entry 96-111 at random on channel 1 (command $20 $60 $0F), so entries 96-99 ($FF00, $FF40, $FF08, $FF00 at $B8BE-$B8C5, bytes that look like uninitialised RAM) send a quarter of those calls into memory at $FF00-$FF4F.

Entries 100-111 of snd_subs_ch1: stream addresses $DCEB, $DBCC, $DBEA, $DC08, $DC26, $DC44, $DC64, $DC8B, $DCBB, $DCBB, $DC8B, $DCEB: the talking phrases of channel 1 (notes with pitch glides: slide steps set by command 6, slides $18/$19 repeated by command 2). Channel 0 draws its phrases from entries 83-98 of its own table at $D8F5 (command $20 $53 $0F).

Stream-subroutine table of channel 2 (pointer at $D837): entries 0-3 at $B8DE-$B8E5 ($DBCC, $DC64, $DC44, $DC26) and 96-111 at snd_subs_ch2_96; the bytes between are zero apart from $00 $FF pairs. Its first entries are also entries 112-115 of snd_subs_ch1.
Entries 4-91 of snd_subs_ch2 ($B8E6-$B997): $FF00 in entry 4, zeros after it. No stream was found that calls them.
$00 $FF three times before snd_subs_ch2_96; unreferenced, like fill_B7D0.
Entries 96-111 of snd_subs_ch2: stream addresses $D891, $D895, $D899, $D895, $D899, $D899, $D895, $D899, $DAFC, $DB04, $DB14, $DB32, $DB54, $DB54, $DB80, $DAFC.

New clothes colours, activity 85 and the cold start ($04CE): a random number AND $1F picks pair 0-15 of colour_pairs, or the person's own pair $034B when it is 16 or more (so half the time); the pair's first colour goes to $1393 (the colour of his lower sprite) and its second to the sprite multicolour register $D025. Then person_head_colour, and next phase.

Head colour: while $0425 is non-zero (3 in the image) the head colour $042E is left alone; at 0 it would become, at random, $0B or $09 (head_colours) or the value in $D025. Then JMP $8F0B (next phase).
Two head colours for person_head_colour: $0B (dark grey) and $09 (brown).

New clothes colour, activity 103: a random number AND $0F picks colour 0-7 of colour_singles, or the person's own entry $034C when it is 8 or more; the colour goes to both $D025 and $1393. Then person_head_colour.
Second bytes of colour_pairs (read as LDA $BA0F,X): the value for $D025.
Eight single colours for person_colours_single: $0E, $03, $0D, $04, $04, $02, $03, $0D.
Pixel lines of the text band still to scroll for a RETURN: text_newline sets 7, text_scroll_step moves the band up one line per pass and decrements it. Also waited on by the letter code at $56E9.
Non-zero (7) while the cursor is being carried back to the left margin after a RETURN; text_return_step moves it 16 pixels a pass and clears this at the margin. Waited on at $56E6.

Non-zero makes the next glyph erase instead of print: glyph_fetch first moves the cursor back by that glyph's width + 1 (not past the margin), glyph_draw XORs it over the old one and does not advance. Set to 1 by the line editor's DEL ($3779, which then queues the character being deleted) and to 8 when print_queued takes a $08; cleared after the glyph (glyph_done).
Non-zero while print_queued must not take another character: set when one is taken, cleared by glyph_done, or at the end of a RETURN's carriage return and scroll ($BD6B).

Turn the top band into a blank text area: window $C1 = 0, no scroll or carriage return pending, text_band_timer $0710 = 3, cursor to the start of the line (text_home) and the band cleared to grey (text_band_blank). Called by print_queued before the first character after the band was closed, and from $04F8, $3755, $55B9.
Put the character in A into the 32-byte output ring $0202-$0221 at the index $0200 and advance it (mod 32). No check for a full ring. Callers: the line editor ($3786) and the letter typing ($5732).

Called once per main-loop pass ($0947, and at start-up $0530): prints at most one character. While text_busy is clear and the ring has one ($0201 differs from $0200): open the band if it is closed (text_band_open), restart text_band_timer at 3, take the character (index $0201 mod 32). While a letter is typed ($54DF) and the cursor is past X 255 ($8D non-zero), a space, or with $54DF negative a hyphen, becomes a RETURN (calling letter_wrap first when negative). A $08 sets text_erase_mode; anything else goes to print_char. When there is nothing to take: every 256 frames ($2B = 0) text_band_timer counts down and at 0 the band goes back to the sky and roof (text_band_restore); a RETURN in progress continues (text_return_step).

Put the picture back in the top band: bitmap $6000-$62BF filled with $55 (in multicolour every pixel pair takes the high nibble of the colour matrix, 6: the blue sky), roof_row_pattern copied into $62C0-$63BF (bitmap row 2, columns 8-39: the top of the roof), colour RAM $D800-$D87F = 0 and colour matrix $5C00-$5C7F = $62 (blue, red); $54DF and the key $30 cleared; then $57EB. Called by print_queued when text_band_timer runs out and at start-up ($0583).
JSR text_band_blank, then JMP $BB05, a jump to itself: code that would blank the text band and stop the main program. Nothing references it.

Print the character in A at the text cursor ($8C/$8D): glyph_fetch (glyph and width), glyph_screen_addr (bitmap pointers), clear bit 7 of $B8, glyph_draw. Character 0 draws nothing and $0D starts a RETURN (text_newline). Callers: print_queued and the start-up text loop at $050D. Other codes below $20 are not handled: glyph_fetch only sets the width to 0, so glyph_draw would XOR the previous glyph's rows again at the cursor and move it 1 pixel; nothing found queues such a code.
Adds $C0 + 1 to the pointer $B9/$BA. Nothing calls it.

Enter with the character in A (kept in $B8). Codes below $20: width 0, nothing else. Otherwise bit 7 picks the font ($B6: font_base_lo/font_base_hi, $5000 or $5800; the second font flips bit 5 of the glyph number) and the glyph's 8 bytes are copied to $92-$99 with $A2-$A9 cleared. First font: byte 0 is the metrics, low nibble the width ($90), high nibble added to the text row $8E to give the glyph's top row ($91). Second font: all 8 bytes are pixels; the glyph is shifted left to its first set column and its width measured, the top row is $8E. Then, in text_erase_mode, the cursor moves back by width + 1 (not past the margin $88/$89). Finally the rows are shifted right by the cursor's X AND 7, the overflow going to $A2-$A9. $5800 holds code, not a font, in this image.
Bitmap address for the glyph: $6000 + $140 x (top row / 8) + (top row AND 7) + (cursor X AND $F8, with $8D as the high byte) into $B2/$B3, and the same + 8 (the next cell) into $B4/$B5.

Draw the fetched glyph: character 0 does nothing; $0D goes to text_newline. Otherwise each row is XORed into the left cell ($B2) and its overflow into the right cell ($B4), moving to the cell row below after the eighth line of a cell; the first font starts at byte 1 (byte 0 is the metrics). Unless erasing, the cursor then moves right by width + 1. Ends in glyph_done.

For a character with bit 7 set this would move the cursor right by (character AND $7F) pixels without drawing. Unreachable: print_char clears bit 7 of $B8 before calling glyph_draw, and glyph_draw is called from nowhere else.
End of printing a character: text_erase_mode = A (0 here; 8 when print_queued jumps to $BCB7 for a $08) and text_busy = 0.
RETURN: text_scroll_left = 7 and text_return_left = 7, then the first text_return_step. text_busy stays set until both are done.
One pass of a RETURN: while text_return_left is set move the cursor 16 pixels left, and at or past the margin ($88/$89) put it on the margin and clear the flag; then text_scroll_step.

While text_scroll_left is non-zero, scroll the three cell rows of the text band up by one pixel line: in each of the 40 cells the rows move up one byte and the last row takes the top row of the cell below (the third cell row shifts rows 1-6 up, blanks row 6 and leaves its row 7, the band's last pixel line, alone); tables text_scroll_dst_lo to text_scroll_count. Then decrement text_scroll_left; when both counts are 0, text_busy is cleared.
Low bytes of the first cell of each text cell row for text_scroll_step: $00, $40, $80 (with text_scroll_dst_hi: $6000, $6140, $6280).
High bytes of the cell rows' addresses: $60, $61, $62.

Low bytes of the source pointer for each cell row: $39, $79, $00 (with text_scroll_src_hi: $6139, $6279, $0000); at index 7 it reads the top row of the cell below ($6140, $6280). The third entry is not used.
High bytes of the source pointers: $61, $62, $00.
Bytes of each cell handled by text_scroll_step, per cell row: 8, 8, 7 (the band's last pixel line is left alone).
Cursor to the start of text window $C1 (always 0): margin $88/$89 and cursor $8C/$8D = text_windows (3), right limit $8A/$8B = the window's right edge - 6 ($0139), text row $8E = $0E.

Blank the text band: colour matrix $5C00-$5C77 = $0C (hires: black set pixels on grey) and bitmap $6000-$63BE = 0. The loop (STA $62BF,X) stops one byte short, so $63BF, the last pixel line of cell (2, 39), keeps what was there.
Low bytes of the two font addresses for glyph_fetch, indexed by bit 7 of the character: $00, $00.
High bytes of the font addresses: $50 ($5000, the font) and $58 ($5800, which holds code in this image).

Text windows for text_home, four bytes each: left margin (word) and right edge (word). Window 0: $0003 and $013F. The bytes after it ($0140, then zeros) would be a window 1, but the window number $C1 is always 0.
text_windows + 1: high byte of the left margin (read at $BD87).
text_windows + 2: low byte of the right edge (read at $BD8E).
text_windows + 3: high byte of the right edge (read at $BD96); followed by the unused window 1 bytes $40 $01 $00 $00 and four zeros.

256 bytes of bitmap that text_band_restore copies to $62C0-$63BF: bitmap row 2, columns 8-39, the top of the roof under the text band (the sky pattern $55 at the ends, the roof slopes, then two rows of $AA along the ridge).
Columns 16-39 of roof_row_pattern ($BE10-$BECF): the ridge rows, then the far slope and sky ($55) at the right end.

Called first by activity_dispatch ($8DAB). When no request is running ($8D9D = 0), finds the first non-zero flag in request_flags ($BEF3-$BEFC) and stores its activity from request_activities in $8D9E, the pending request.

Activity for each request flag 0-9: $21 (33, dog food: CTRL D), $34 (52, the greeting reply), $19 (25, the telephone: CTRL C), $2C (44, food: CTRL F), $06 (6, the easy chair: CTRL P), $33 (51, a book: CTRL B), $32 (50, a record: CTRL R), $1D (29, a drink of water), $4A (74, a meal), $02 (2). Also read at $8F34, $8FA0, $9030 and $95E2.

Ten request flags, $BEF3-$BEFC (non-zero = requested), index = the entry in request_activities. Flag 0 is set by CTRL D ($2B86); $BEF4 (flag 1), $BEFA (7) and $BEFB (8): no store of a non-zero value was found in the image. A flag is cleared at $8F43 when its activity finishes a request.
Request flag 2 (activity 25, the telephone): set by CTRL C ($2C0B) and at $0B36.
Request flag 3 (activity 44, food delivered at the door): set by CTRL F ($2B6F).
Request flag 4 (activity 6, go and sit in the easy chair): set by CTRL P ($2C5C) when he is not sitting there.
Request flag 5 (activity 51, a book at the door): set by CTRL B ($2B9D).
Request flag 6 (activity 50, a record at the door): set by CTRL R ($2BBB) while $0711 is 0.
Request flag 9 (activity 2, which clears the pending request): set to 1 at $099A after the parser call, cleared at $9054 and $E161.
Wait count for act_paper_wait in activity 24, in units of 8 calls (8, 1, or 8-31).
Call counter of act_paper_wait: it acts only when the low three bits are 0.

Activity 24: JSR $3F11 switches on the phase $4C through 17 handler words. Walk to the easy chair (act_walk_chair_2b) and wait; sit (pose $23) with figure 2 set up in front of him (act_sit_paper), wait; pose $34 (act_paper_pose34), wait; then a loop of act_paper_frame1 (pose $35, figure 2 frame 1), wait, act_paper_turn (a random frame 1-3 with poses $35-$37), wait, act_paper_again (back to phase 6 unless a request is pending or 1 time in 8 at random); then pose $34, wait, pose $23, wait, act_paper_away; end. Figure 2 is white (colour 1) and changes frame while he sits: plausibly the newspaper in the easy chair that the manual mentions, not proven. One of the four choices of act116_choose.

Phase table of activity 24 ($18), read by the JSR $3F11 at $BEFF: one word per phase, the handler's address minus one. 0 act_walk_chair_2b ($BFC7); 1 wait_or_request ($8FA7); 2 act_sit_paper ($BFB7); 3 act_paper_wait ($BF99); 4 act_paper_pose34 ($BF45); 5 act_paper_wait ($BF99); 6 act_paper_frame1 ($BF52); 7 act_paper_wait ($BF99); 8 act_paper_turn ($BF24); 9 act_paper_wait ($BF99); 10 act_paper_again ($BF73); 11 act_paper_pose34 ($BF45); 12 act_paper_wait ($BF99); 13 act_sit_paper ($BFB7); 14 act_paper_wait ($BF99); 15 act_paper_away ($BF8B); 16 script_next ($8F0E).
Activity handler: a random 1-3 (0 counts as 1) into figure 2's frame $038D, $03C6 = $82, pose $34 + that ($35-$37) via set_pose ($9363), paper_wait = 1, next phase.
Shared tail: set_pose with A, paper_wait = 1, next phase.
Activity handler: gaze_mode = $A1, figure 2 back in front of him (paper_show), pose $34, paper_wait = 1, next phase.
Activity handler: gaze_mode = $42, figure 2 frame 1 ($038D = 1, $03C6 = $82), pose $35, paper_wait = ($0414 AND $1F) OR 8, next phase.
Activity handler: unless a request is pending or ($0414 AND 7) = 3, go back to phase 6 (act_paper_frame1), with paper_wait = $1E, which act_paper_frame1 then replaces; otherwise next phase.
Activity handler: gaze_mode = 2 and $03C6 = 2 (figure 2 put away), next phase. It starts with LDA #$00, which the LDA #$02 after it makes pointless.
Activity handler: counts paper_tick and acts on every eighth call: if a request is pending, or paper_wait is 0, next phase; otherwise decrement paper_wait.
Activity handler: paper_show, pose $23 (sitting), paper_wait = 8, next phase.
Activity handler: LDX #$2B, JMP $8EF9: walk to place $2B, the easy chair. First phase of activity 24.

Put figure 2 in front of the person: $0394 = $FF (multicolour), colour $1394 = 1 (white), $039C = 0, frame $038D = 0, x, floor and depth copied from the person ($03A7, $03AB, $03AF; depth $03B3 - 1), $03C6 = $83 (shown).
Three bytes $FF $00 $FB at the end of the range; nothing references them.

Parser read position: index (0-127) into the typed-line ring at $0224 of the next character the parser has not read yet. Only parse_advance ($C112) changes it (+1, modulo 128); it is never reset, it follows the line's write index $0222 (kept by the line editor at $3731) round the ring. The parser works whenever the two differ.

The character just before the line's write index ($0223+$0222), stored by parse_typed_line each time it runs. A letter means a word is still being typed and nothing is parsed yet; RETURN, '.', '!' or '?' ends the sentence.

The finished sentence: up to 8 action codes ended by a 0 ($C002-$C009). Written at the end of a sentence by parse_typed_line from parse_rule_actions ($C00B), or from $C00A (the constant $2E, then the first 7 actions) when the sentence score is 12 or more. An action code is an activity number: the main loop ($0986-$09B6) reads the list through parse_get_action, appends it to the 16-entry action queue at $E12A and zeroes $C002 (parse_clear_actions); activity 0 ($E13F) later stores each queued code in the activity number $8D9B (at $E393).

Constant $2E (activity 46), never written: the action put in front of a sentence's actions when its score ($C014) is 12 or more, because the copy at the end of a sentence then starts here instead of at $C00B.

Action codes of the rules matched so far in the current sentence, 0-terminated, 8 bytes ($C00B-$C012); parse_action_count ($C013) is the write index. Only parse_match_rules writes it and nothing clears it, so after a sentence in which no rule matched at all it still holds the previous sentence's list, which the end of the sentence copies again (a matched rule without actions, such as PLEASE, does empty it).

Number of action codes in parse_rule_actions ($C00B), where parse_match_rules stores the next one. parse_match_rules ANDs it with 7 after every rule check and the end of a sentence resets it to 0. Two matched rules with 8 codes between them write the ending 0 into $C013 itself (it becomes 0) and leave $C002-$C009 without a 0 (rules have at most 4 codes).

Score of the finished sentence: parse_mood_bonus[$035F AND 3] (3, 1 or 0) + parse_rule_score + a random 0-3 (bits 0-1 of $195E). 12 or more puts action $2E in front. parse_get_action returns it in Y; the main loop stores it in $092F and, at 8 or more, empties the action queue ($E129 = $E128) and sets $BEFC before queuing the new actions. Activity 0 serves the queue while $092F is 8 or more and counts $092F up from 4-7; below 4 queued actions wait.
Sum of the scores of the rules matched in the current sentence: each matched rule adds the low 7 bits of its end byte. Added into the sentence score and zeroed at the end of the sentence.

Concept bits of the list-1 words (vocab_verbs) read since the last rule matched: five bytes; parse_lookup_word ORs each word's five bit bytes in. parse_match_rules tests rule bytes 0-4 against them and clears both bit sets when a rule matches; the end of a sentence clears them too.
Concept bits of the list-2 words (vocab_nouns) read since the last rule matched: five bytes, ORed in by parse_lookup_word and tested against rule bytes 5-9. Cleared together with $C016.
The word being looked up ($C020-$C03F): upper-case letters ended by a 0, at most 31 letters (parse_extract_word drops the rest). An empty word (first byte 0) is not looked up.

The parser, called once per main-loop pass ($097F). Returns at once while parse_pos equals the line's write index $0222, or while the last character typed ($0223+$0222, kept in $C001) is a letter. Otherwise a word has just been ended: parse_extract_word copies it to $C020, parse_lookup_word ORs its concept bits into $C016 or $C01B, and parse_match_rules tests the rules. If the last character is RETURN, '.', '!' or '?' the sentence ends: the score $C014 = parse_mood_bonus[$035F AND 3] + parse_rule_score + random 0-3, parse_rule_score is zeroed, eight action bytes are copied to $C002-$C009 (from $C00B, or from $C00A so that $2E comes first when the score is 12 or more), and both concept-bit sets and parse_action_count are cleared. Nothing checks that a rule matched in this sentence.

Sentence-score bonus by the mood $035F (read through jt_get_mood at $0346), index mood AND 3: 3, 1, 0, 0, so the happiest mood, 0, adds 3. The mood is 0-2 and also picks the set of head graphics at $0E71.

Copies the next word of the typed line into parse_word ($C020): skips non-letters from parse_pos, stores letters converted to upper case (at most 31), ends the word with 0, then moves parse_pos on to the write index $0222, dropping whatever follows the word. Any non-letter ends a word, the apostrophe too: WHAT'S is read as WHAT and S, so the list-1 entry WHAT'S ($C5A1) can never match.
Carry set if A is a letter ($41-$5A or $61-$7A), with a lower-case letter converted to upper case in A; carry clear otherwise, A unchanged.
parse_pos ($C000) + 1, modulo 128 (the typed line is a 128-byte ring at $0224). Returns it in Y with A kept, Z set when it has reached the line's write index $0222.
Z set if A is one of the four characters in parse_end_chars ($C12F): RETURN, '.', '!', '?' (X = its index); Z clear otherwise (X = $FF).
The four characters that end a sentence: $0D (RETURN), '.', '!', '?'.
LDY $C001 / LDA $C020,X / RTS: an accessor for the word buffer, built like parse_get_action below it. No JSR or JMP to $C133 was found in the image; apparently unused.

Returns A = parse_sentence_actions+X ($C002+X), Z set when it is the 0 that ends the list, and Y = the sentence score ($C014). The main loop calls it with X = 0 at $0986 (is there a new sentence?) and at $099F for each action in turn.
Zeroes $C002, the first action of the finished sentence, once the main loop ($09B6) has queued the list, so each sentence is queued once.

Looks parse_word ($C020) up in word list 1 (vocab_verbs, $C234) and, only when it is not there, in list 2 (vocab_nouns, $C5E0); ORs the five bit bytes of the first matching record into $C016 (list 1) or $C01B (list 2) and returns carry set. Carry clear for an empty or unknown word. Because the search stops at the first match, the second list-1 records of START ($C396), LIKE ($C52F), APATHETIC ($C568) and IS ($C5D7) are never used.
Five-byte copy of the concept bits of the record parse_search_list is looking at; after a successful search, the bits of the word found.

Searches a word list for parse_word ($C020): A/X = list address (low/high), kept in $10/$11. For each record it copies the five bit bytes to parse_found_bits ($C182), stopping with carry clear at the first bit byte that is $FF (the end of the list), then compares the word letter by letter; carry set on an exact match of the whole word. List 2 therefore ends at the $FF at $C969.

Tests the rules (parse_rules, $C96A, 16-byte records) against the concept bits gathered so far: rule byte n (n = 0-9) against $C016+n. A rule matches when every bit set in its ten bytes is also set in the sentence; bits the rule does not name are ignored, and the first matching rule in table order wins. Its action codes (from offset 10 up to the first byte of $80 or more) are appended to parse_rule_actions ($C00B) at parse_action_count and followed by a 0, the low 7 bits of the end byte are added to parse_rule_score ($C015), and both concept-bit sets are cleared so that a new clause starts. A rule byte of $FF ends the table ($CB8A). Uses $10-$13 in zero page. Called after every word, so a rule fires as soon as the last word it needs has been typed.

Parser word list 1 (verbs, question words, feelings and manners), searched first: records of five bytes of concept bits, the word in upper-case ASCII, and $00; $FF at $C5DF ends it. Words with the same bits are synonyms (LIKE and ENJOY; LIGHT, START, MAKE, BURN and IGNITE). A word found here is not looked up in list 2, and only its first record counts (see parse_lookup_word). No rule uses the bits of DO, LIKE/ENJOY, WILL/WOULD, RELAX, ON, GET, IF or of LOGON, PROGRAM, UTILITIES, MATH, HOMEWORK, ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY, DIVIDE.
records.s: DO: 01 00 00 00 00; no rule uses its bits
LIKE: 04 00 00 00 00; no rule uses its bits
ENJOY: 04 00 00 00 00; no rule uses its bits
WILL: 10 00 00 00 00; no rule uses its bits
WOULD: 10 00 00 00 00; no rule uses its bits
RELAX: 80 00 00 00 00; no rule uses its bits
START: 00 08 00 00 00; never found: START at $C301 comes first
ON: 00 10 00 00 00; no rule uses its bits
LOGON: 00 00 02 00 00; no rule uses its bits
PROGRAM: 00 00 02 00 00; no rule uses its bits
UTILITIES: 00 00 02 00 00; no rule uses its bits
MATH: 00 00 02 00 00; no rule uses its bits
HOMEWORK: 00 00 02 00 00; no rule uses its bits
ADD: 00 00 02 00 00; no rule uses its bits
SUBTRACT: 00 00 02 00 00; no rule uses its bits
MULTIPLY: 00 00 02 00 00; no rule uses its bits
DIVIDE: 00 00 02 00 00; no rule uses its bits
GET: 00 00 40 00 00; no rule uses its bits
LIKE: 00 00 00 08 00; never found: LIKE at $C245 comes first
APATHETIC: 00 00 00 20 00; never found: APATHETIC at $C54F comes first
IF: 00 00 00 80 00; no rule uses its bits
WHAT'S: 00 00 00 00 02; never matches: the apostrophe ends a word
IS: 00 00 00 00 08; never found: IS at $C337 comes first

records.c: Parser word list 2 (things, rooms and games), in the same format as list 1 and searched only when list 1 has no match. No rule uses the bits of TV or CHAIR.

records.s: TV: 00 10 00 00 00; no rule uses its bits
CHAIR: 00 20 00 00 00; no rule uses its bits

records.c: The end of word list 2: a record with bits 00 00 00 00 01 and an empty word ($C95B), an all-zero record with an empty word ($C961), and the $FF at $C969 where parse_search_list stops. A typed word is never empty, so these records never match.

The parser's 34 rules, 16 bytes each: bytes 0-4 are list-1 concept bits, 5-9 list-2 concept bits, then action codes (activity numbers, below $80) ended by a byte of $80 or more whose low 7 bits are the rule's score. parse_match_rules takes the first rule all of whose bits are present; $FF at $CB8A ends the table. Rule 7 ($C9DA) needs the bit of the second IS record, which a lookup never returns, so it never fires. The side comments decode each rule: words -> activity numbers (hex), score.

records.s: rule 5: HEAR/LISTEN/PUT/START(2nd, never found)/SPIN + STEREO/TURNTABLE/MUSIC/RECORD/PLATTER -> $09; score 4
rule 7: SLOPPY/MESSY/UNTIDY + IS(2nd, never found) + HOUSE/HOME -> $13; score 2
rule 22: HATE/APATHETIC(2nd, never found)/AWFUL + STEREO/TURNTABLE/MUSIC/RECORD/PLATTER -> $27, $79; score 8
rule 26: WHAT + IN/INSIDE/STORED/KEEP + UPSTAIRS + CLOSET -> $0C, $23; score 6
rule 27: WHAT + IN/INSIDE/STORED/KEEP + BEDROOM + CLOSET -> $0D, $27; score 6
rule 28: WHAT + IN/INSIDE/STORED/KEEP + KITCHEN + CABINET -> $3C, $3E, $27, $3F; score 6
rule 29: WHAT + IN/INSIDE/STORED/KEEP + FILING + CABINET -> $17; score 6

records.c: Unused: 117 zero bytes, $CB8B-$CBFF, between the parser rules and the colour RAM image at $CC00. Loaded with the program and never changed; no instruction reads or writes them.

Zero byte in the unused stretch $CB8B-$CBFF. Its references ($910B, $8ECC, $ABBF) are bytes of switch tables in other ranges that decode as LDA $CB93,Y / INC / DEC $CB93,X; they are not real accesses.

The house picture's colour RAM image: 1000 nibbles, 25 rows of 40, for $D800-$DBE7 (the colour of the '11' bit pairs of the multicolour bitmap at $6000); $CFE8-$CFFF are zero. Loaded with the program. The crack's hand-over code (at $4855-$485B in crack-screen.vsf, before the game's first instruction) copies $CC00-$CFFF to $D800-$DBFF, as it copies $4C00-$4FFF to $0400-$07FF. No game code reads it (no absolute operand into $CB8B-$CFFF, no immediate high byte $CC-$CF in the image). The live colour RAM equals it in time-prompt.vsf and play-01.vsf; play-02.vsf differs only at $D8F5 and $D91D, the two cells written at $2D6B and $2D6E.

records.s: $CFE8-$CFFF: zero; copied to the unused colour RAM $DBE8-$DBFF

records.c: Sound driver (the one ticked from the raster IRQ through $B003), one event. RAM under the I/O area: entered by JMP $D000 from $B635 with $01 = $34. (Instructions elsewhere that name $D000-$D02E with I/O in, such as the sprite code at $048A and $076F, reach the VIC, not this code.) A = the event byte (never 0), X = channel*2 ($6C, 0-10), $75/$76+X = the channel's sequence pointer, advanced here past the byte, which is also kept in $B026+X. $10 and $50-$FF are notes (snd_note, via the JMP at $D043). $01-$4F are commands: the byte goes to $B150, $30-$3F and $40-$4F are folded to $30 and $31, and the handler address from snd_commands ($D700 + 2n) is stored in snd_cmd_handler ($D041); snd_dispatch then jumps to it with ($81) at the operand bytes, X = the voice's SID shadow offset ($70) and Y = 0.

records.s: handler address from snd_commands ($D026-$D031 is RAM, not the VIC)

records.c: Command handler address (low, high), written by snd_event from snd_commands and copied by snd_dispatch into the operand of the JMP at $B376. Zero in crack-screen.vsf; $D57C in time-prompt.vsf, $D4F3 in play-01.vsf and $D3C5 in play-02.vsf.
High byte of snd_cmd_handler ($D041): written at $D02F, copied to $B378 by snd_dispatch.
JMP $D046, a jump to the next instruction: where snd_event sends notes ($D00D, $D011) and commands $30-$3F send their slot's note ($D428).

Note event: A = the note byte, kept in $6E. For $10 and $50-$8F the frequency is the word at $B641+note (the note byte is a byte offset; $10 reads zero there, a rest). For $90-$FF, bits 7-3 pick a word from $B661 (index (note>>4)*2, +$20 when bit 3 is set) and the value is halved 7-(note AND 7) times, so bits 2-0 are the octave. The frequency goes to the voice's shadow $B031/$B032+X, then snd_duration reads the length.

Reads a note's length: the next sequence byte is an offset into the byte pairs at $B726: the first goes to $B019+channel*2, the ticks the note sounds with the gate on, the second to $B01A+channel*2, the ticks counted afterwards with the gate off ($B56A-$B590); then the next event is read. Sets the gate bit in the shadow control byte $B035+X and goes on to the next channel ($B554). Also the tail of the slide commands $08, $09 and $15-$1B.

Command $03 n: start sound n on the channel set of this channel: channels with shadow offset below $15 use $B255 (channels 0-2), the others fall into snd_cmd_sound_2. Jumps to $B4F8, which calls $B255 and then restarts the tick at $B4FB. The pointer is not advanced past n.
Command $05 n: start sound n on the second channel set (channels 3-5) through $B4F2, which calls $B268 and then restarts the tick at $B4FB. The pointer is not advanced past n.
Command $01 lo hi: jump: the channel's sequence pointer $75/$76+channel*2 is set to the inline address.

Start of a pattern or of a subsequence (after commands $04, $0A and $20): the first byte at the channel's new pointer is an instrument offset, applied by $B311 (five bytes from snd_instruments into the shadow $B033-$B037+X); then the channel is processed again ($B55D).

Command $02 count lo hi: loop. First time ($B069+channel*2 = 0): marks the loop active, stores the count in $B06A+channel*2 and jumps to the address. Later: while the count is not 0 it is decremented and the jump taken again; at 0 the loop is cleared and the three operand bytes skipped. So the section is played count+1 times.

Command $04 n: call pattern n. Saves the voice's seven shadow bytes $B031-$B037+X in $B08D+X and the return address (after n) in $B081/$B082+channel*2, looks the pattern up (snd_pattern_lookup) and starts it at snd_pattern_begin. The pattern ends with a 0 byte, where $B5CD restores the pointer and the seven shadow bytes.

Reads two operand bytes (low, high) as a filter-cutoff step for command $11 ($B249) and $1C, $1D, $1F: the low 11 bits, split like the SID cutoff registers: bits 0-2 to $B15C+channel*2 (with bits 3-7 set), bits 3-10 to $B15D+channel*2; the pointer moves on by 2. snd_filter_step adds the step.
Reads two operand bytes (low, high) into the channel's pulse-width step $B168/$B169+channel*2 for command $13 ($B25C) and $1C, $1E, $1F; the pointer moves on by 2. snd_pw_step adds the step.

Frequency slide down one step (snd_slide_up at $D1CF is the same with $85 = 1: up). The step is the channel's $B0C4/$B0C5+channel*2: $FFFF (set by command $07) means one eighth of the current frequency, computed and stored the first time; bit 7 of the high byte forces a downward step of the low 15 bits. Otherwise, one time in 16 (when $B0D0 AND $0F is 0) the step is halved and stored back, never below 1. The step is subtracted from or added to the shadow frequency $B031/$B032+X. Returns Y = 0.
Entry of snd_slide_down ($D1CB) that slides the frequency up: sets $85 = 1 and continues at $D1D1.

Filter sweep step (command $12 via $B24F, and commands $17-$1B): adds the channel's step $B15C/$B15D+channel*2 to the filter cutoff shadow of its layer ($B05B/$B05C for channels 0-2, $B062/$B063 for 3-5). If the result crosses the top or bottom of the range (sign test) the step is negated and nothing is stored; otherwise the new cutoff is stored with bit 7 of the low byte set, the flag that makes $B46A write the filter registers.

Pulse-width sweep step (command $14 via $B262, and $15-$17, $1A, $1B): adds the channel's step $B168/$B169+channel*2 to the pulse width shadow $B033/$B034+X (12 bits). While the width's high nibble is 6-9 the step is taken 1.5 times. If the sum leaves the 12-bit range the step is negated and nothing is stored.

Jumps to the command handler: copies snd_cmd_handler ($D041/$D042) into the operand of the JMP at $B376 and jumps there. (It first copies $B05C/$B05D over the same two bytes, which the next copy overwrites.) Every command event also decrements $B017; when that reaches 0 the jump goes through $B371, which increments $B0D1 and, when that wraps to 0, runs $B379 instead of the handler.

Loads a filter preset: X = offset into the four-byte records at $B6A1 (cutoff low, cutoff high, resonance and routing, mode and volume), copied to $B05B-$B05E (channels 0-2) or $B062-$B065 (channels 3-5, $6C of 6 or more); the next byte ($B05F or $B066) is zeroed. Called with X = 0 when a sound starts ($B2CE) and by command $0D.

Command $20 first mask: call a random pattern. Saves the voice's pulse width, control and envelope bytes ($B033-$B037+X) in $B10C+X, picks pattern number first + (mask AND $B0D3, the random byte the tick updates), keeps the return address (after the two operands) in $B134/$B135+channel*2 and starts the pattern at snd_pattern_begin. The pattern ends with command $21.
Command $21: return from a random pattern (command $20): restores the sequence pointer from $B134/$B135+channel*2 and the five saved shadow bytes from $B10C+X.

Command $23 notes... '#': copies up to 16 bytes, until a '#' ($23), into the channel's note slots at $B174 + 16*channel; command $40+n (snd_cmd_set_notes_n) enters at $D3E7 with at most n+1 bytes. The pointer moves past the bytes read, '#' included. At $D416 (no label: $D416 is also the SID filter register) commands $30-$3F play slot n of the channel: the note from $B174 + 16*channel + n goes to snd_note, and a length byte follows. (The SID register names and x-refs the listing shows on $D400-$D41C are the I/O chip's; this is RAM code.)

Commands $30-$3F (no label here: the SID filter register $D416 has the same address): play note slot n = command AND $0F of the channel, the byte at $B174 + 16*channel + n, through snd_note; a length byte follows.
Command $22 count lo hi: a second loop, like command $02 but with its own flag and counter $B075/$B076+channel*2, so two loops can be nested.
Command $08 length: slide the frequency down one step (snd_slide_down), then read a length.
Command $09 length: slide the frequency up one step (snd_slide_up), then read a length.
Command $07: sets the channel's slide step $B0C4/$B0C5+channel*2 to $FFFF, meaning one eighth of the frequency at the next slide.
Command $06 lo hi: reads the channel's slide step $B0C4/$B0C5+channel*2 from the two operand bytes ($B21C).

Command $0A n: call pattern n, second kind: saves the seven shadow bytes in $B0D4+X and the return address in $B0FE/$B0FF+channel*2; the pattern starts with an instrument byte and ends with command $0B.
Command $0B: return from a command $0A pattern: pointer from $B0FE/$B0FF+channel*2, seven shadow bytes from $B0D4+X.
Command $0C offset: sets the voice's instrument, five bytes from snd_instruments + offset ($B311).
Command $0D offset: loads filter preset $B6A1 + offset (snd_set_filter) and sets bit 7 of the layer's $B05B/$B062, the flag that has the tick write the filter registers.
Command $0E: skips its one operand byte; does nothing else.
Command $0F (and $10, $28-$2F through $B5B7): no operation, one byte.
Command $24 n: call pattern n, third kind: return address (after n) in $B140/$B141+channel*2; this pattern has no instrument byte and ends with command $25.
Command $25: return from a command $24 pattern to the address in $B140/$B141+channel*2.
Pattern lookup reading the pattern number from the sequence (($81),0); snd_pattern_lookup_a at $D529 takes it in A.

Pattern lookup: A = pattern number n. Bit 7 set picks the shared table, clear the channel's own; the entry is the word at table + (2n AND $FF). Channels 0-2 take the table addresses from snd_pattern_tables ($D831: shared, then channels 0, 1, 2); channels 3-5 from the words at ($D7AC/$D7AD)+12 (shared) and +14, +16, +18 (own), i.e. from the header of the sound-12 data (the piano piece chosen at $AB1A). The address is patched into the two LDA abs,Y at $D561 and $D567. Returns the pattern address in $73/$74, X = channel*2, Y = 0, A = the channel's pointer low byte.

records.s: operand ($D562/$D563) patched with the pattern-table list address

records.c: Operand low byte of the LDA $D831,Y at $D561, patched by snd_pattern_lookup_a: $31 for channels 0-2, ($D7AC)+6 for channels 3-5 (the carry is not added to the high byte).
Operand high byte of the LDA at $D561, patched by snd_pattern_lookup_a: $D8 for channels 0-2, ($D7AD) for channels 3-5.
Operand low byte of the LDA $D831,Y at $D567 (the pattern table's high byte), patched with the value written to $D562.
Operand high byte of the LDA at $D567, patched with the value written to $D563.
Command $40+n: like command $23, but copies at most n+1 note bytes (or up to '#') into the channel's note slots.

Instrument records of the sound driver, 5 bytes each at offsets $00-$CD (42 records, to $D658): pulse width low, pulse width high, control (waveform bits; bit 3, the test bit, resets the oscillator: the output loop at $B4C6 writes it and $B4D4 at once writes and keeps the byte without it), attack/decay, sustain/release. $B311 copies a record into a voice's shadow $B033-$B037 when a sequence or pattern starts (its first byte is the offset) and for command $0C. The sounds in $D800-$DDFF use offsets up to $B9.
Instrument records $3C-$CD, continuing snd_instruments ($D587).
After the instrument records: $00/$FF bytes to $D660, then zero up to $D6FF. No sound in $D800-$DDFF uses an instrument offset past $B9; nothing else reads here that was found.

Activity 53, the dance (the parser queues it after activity 9 for DANCE, MOON or SHOW). Counts its passes in act53_tick, then switches on the phase $4C through act53_phases: 0 walk out if a record is playing, 1 wait to arrive ($8FA7), 2 choose 3, 7, 11 or 15 moves, 3 choose the next move, 4-7 the moves (7 is activity 37's handler $22D5), 8 back to 3, 9 end ($8F0E).
Phase table of activity 53 for the switch at $E003 (index $4C), handler addresses minus one: $E01A, $8FA7, $E046, $E0AB, $E114, $E098, $E06F, $22D5, $E0A6, $8F0E.

Activity 53 phase 0: without a record playing ($801E, music_playing = 0) jumps to phase 9 and ends. Otherwise copies location 0 into the scratch location 54 ($16AE), moves it $14 half-pixels right ($1DA3), makes it the person's target ($03C0 = $36) and, unless he is already there ($1E11), sets his movement state $03BC to 2; next phase.
Activity 53 phase 2: act53_moves_left = (random AND $0F) OR 3, so 3, 7, 11 or 15 moves; next phase.

Activity 53's pass counter: incremented on every call ($E000), zeroed when a move is chosen ($E0AD). act53_step_gate acts on every fourth value and ends a move when it wraps to 0; the moves take their pose and facing from its bits.
Dance moves left (3, 7, 11 or 15 from act53_count_moves), counted down by act53_choose_move.

Gate at the start of each dance move handler: returns from the handler (PLA PLA RTS) unless act53_tick is a multiple of 4; goes back to phase 3 (act53_next_move) when act53_tick has wrapped to 0 or a request is waiting ($8F86); otherwise returns to the handler.
Activity 53 phase 6, a move: every fourth pass sets pose act53_tick/16 AND 7 with facing 8 or 0 by bit 2 of act53_tick.
Common tail of the dance moves: facing X to $039A, figure_set_pose ($1ADF) for the person with pose A, sets bit 1 (rebuild) of his flags $03C4 and clears $037C.
Activity 53 phase 5, a move: every fourth pass pose 4 with the facing $039A flipped (EOR 8).
Activity 53 phase 8: sets the phase back to 3 (act53_choose_move); also where act53_step_gate leaves a move.

Activity 53 phase 3: zeroes act53_tick and $68. Finishes (act53_finish) when a request is waiting ($8F86), the record has stopped ($801E = 0) or no moves are left; otherwise counts a move down and sets the phase to 4 + random 0-3, and the first time sets the head (figure 4) to pose $1E ($038F, $ACF1, $03F4 = 8, $03C8 = $82).

End of the dance: turns the person to pose $22 with his facing ($255B, one step per call) and, once turn_busy $2540 is clear, puts the head back (pose 8 in $038F and $03F4, $ACF1 = 0, $037C = 1, $03C8 = $82) and sets phase 9, the end.
Activity 53 phase 4, a move: every fourth pass sets pose ($38 - act53_tick)/16 AND 7, keeping the facing.

Activity 121 ($79, which the parser also queues after TIRED or HATE + MUSIC) waiting to be started by the chooser, or 0. Set at $E1B1 when $2B45 is non-zero, no record plays and bit 7 of $0369 is clear; cleared when started.
A request put off while the person is in bed ($0368 non-zero): chooser_start keeps it here and starts activity $1F (getting up) instead; the chooser starts it on its next call ($E152). 0 = none.

Write index (0-15) of action_queue, advanced by the main loop ($09A4-$09AE) for each action of a parsed sentence; the main loop also copies it to action_queue_out to empty the queue when a sentence scores 8 or more.
Read index (0-15) of action_queue: the chooser takes the entry here while request_score $092F is 8 or more ($E175-$E185). Equal to action_queue_in when the queue is empty.

The queue of actions from typed sentences: 16 activity numbers in a ring ($E12A-$E139), written by the main loop at action_queue_in and read by the chooser at action_queue_out. A sentence whose matched rules give 8 action codes leaves no 0 in $C002-$C009, so the main loop queues 17 entries and the ring overflows unnoticed.
Five zero bytes after the action queue ($E13A-$E13E); no instruction reads or writes them.

The activity chooser: activity 0 (also 77 and 123-127, and the target of activity 2's JMP at $9057). Zeroes the phases $4C and $68 and starts the first that applies: pending_activity $037B (a CTRL key) or chooser_deferred, each cleared when taken. It then clears request flag $BEFC, and request_activity $8D9E when that is 2. Next: the next typed action from action_queue while request_score $092F is 8 or more (an empty queue zeroes $092F; 4-7 is counted up by one); chooser_queued_121 unless it was the last choice; drinking ($1D) or eating ($4A) by the need levels $036E/$0371, the tank $2B51, the cupboard $30B4, the timers $0370/$0373 and chance; activity 4 while $0374 is set; getting up ($1F) if a request waits while he is in bed ($0368); at schedule step 0 or illness 3 or more, bed ($1E) or, already in bed, nothing except at step 0; at other steps, getting up if in bed; activity $4C at house hour $036C and 1 at hour $036D, once a day each; the morning or evening list asked for in $035C; otherwise chooser_by_step.

Once-a-day flag for activity $4C at house hour noon_act_hour ($036C): any other hour stores the hour here (non-zero, armed), the chooser starts $4C at that hour only when it is armed and then zeroes it. $0F in play.
Activity chooser, continued: re-arms chooser_noon_armed with the current hour, then starts activity 1 at house hour act_1_hour $036D if chooser_act1_armed is set (zeroing it).

Where the packed sprite graphics are: one word per graphic number 0-182, stored as the graphic's offset from $E453 plus $5000. unpack_figure_sprite ($0E41) reads the word at $E453 + 2n and adds $E453 - $5000 (high byte - $50, then + $E453). Graphics 0-182 follow at $E5C1-$FFB9 in order, without gaps; each unpacks to 63 bytes, one sprite image (checked for all 183). The $5000 bias suggests the data was once assembled to lie at $5000; unknown.
